a-plus.methods: Open-label randomised multicentre trial in Taiwan. Eligible patients were aged 20 to 75, had brain metastases from breast cancer not suitable for focal treatment, were whole-brain radiotherapy naive and had at least one measurable brain lesion. Patients were randomised 2:1 to three cycles of bevacizumab, etoposide and cisplatin followed by whole-brain radiotherapy, or to whole-brain radiotherapy alone. The primary endpoint was brain-specific progression-free survival assessed by local investigators using RECIST 1.1.
a-plus.results: 118 patients were randomised and 112 formed the intention-to-treat cohort. Median age was 56 years and 61 patients (54.5%) had HER2-positive disease. Median brain-specific progression-free survival was 8.1 versus 6.5 months (hazard ratio 0.71; 95% CI 0.44 to 1.13; P = .15). Brain-specific objective response at 2 months was 41.9% versus 52.6%. The 8-month brain-specific progression-free survival rate was 48.7% versus 26.3% (P = .03).

abc-study.methods: Single-arm phase II trial in patients with triple-negative breast cancer and active brain metastases. Patients received adebrelimab, bevacizumab and cisplatin or carboplatin until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity. The primary endpoint was CNS objective response rate by RANO-BM criteria. Secondary endpoints were CNS clinical benefit rate, progression-free survival, overall survival, first site of progression and safety.
abc-study.results: 35 patients were enrolled and treated, with a median of 2 prior lines of treatment. The confirmed CNS objective response rate was 77.1% (27 of 35) and the CNS clinical benefit rate was 80.0%. Median progression-free survival was 8.3 months, median CNS progression-free survival was 10.3 months and median overall survival was 21.1 months. Grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events occurred in 65.7% of patients.

abc-trials.methods: Three adjuvant randomised trials assigned women with high-risk HER2-negative early breast cancer to six cycles of docetaxel and cyclophosphamide or to a standard taxane plus anthracycline regimen. USOR 06-090 compared TC6 with TAC6. NSABP B-46-I/USOR 07132 compared TC6, TAC6 and TC6 plus bevacizumab. NSABP B-49 compared TC6 with several anthracycline and taxane regimens. A joint efficacy analysis with invasive disease-free survival as the primary endpoint was prespecified, with a hazard ratio above 1.18 defined as inferiority.
abc-trials.results: 2,125 patients were assigned to TC6 regimens and 2,117 to taxane plus anthracycline regimens. At a median follow-up of 3.3 years there were 334 invasive disease-free survival events and the hazard ratio for TC6 versus taxane plus anthracycline was 1.202 (95% CI 0.97 to 1.49), which triggered early reporting for futility. Four-year invasive disease-free survival was 88.2% versus 90.7% (P = .04). Interaction tests by protocol, hormone receptor status and nodal status were negative.

abcsg-8-arno-95.methods: Combined analysis of two prospective multicentre randomised open-label trials with nearly identical inclusion criteria. Postmenopausal women with hormone-sensitive early breast cancer who had completed 2 years of adjuvant tamoxifen were randomised to anastrozole 1 mg daily (n=1618) or to tamoxifen 20 or 30 mg daily (n=1606) for the remainder of adjuvant therapy. The primary endpoint was event-free survival, with events defined as local or distant metastasis or contralateral breast cancer. Analysis was by intention to treat.
abcsg-8-arno-95.results: 3,224 patients were included. At a median follow-up of 28 months there were 67 events with anastrozole and 110 with tamoxifen (hazard ratio 0.60; 95% CI 0.44 to 0.81; P = .0009). Both treatments were well tolerated. Fractures were significantly more frequent with anastrozole (P = .015) and thromboses significantly less frequent (P = .034).

abcsg12.methods: Randomised trial in premenopausal women with endocrine-responsive early breast cancer. 1803 patients were assigned to goserelin 3.6 mg subcutaneously every 28 days plus either tamoxifen 20 mg daily or anastrozole 1 mg daily, each with or without zoledronic acid 4 mg intravenously every 6 months, for 3 years. The primary end point was disease-free survival. Recurrence-free survival and overall survival were secondary end points.
abcsg12.results: After a median 47.8 months, 137 events occurred. Disease-free survival was 92.8% with tamoxifen, 92.0% with anastrozole, 90.8% without zoledronic acid and 94.0% with it. Anastrozole versus tamoxifen gave a hazard ratio of 1.10 (0.78 to 1.53, P=0.59). Zoledronic acid gave 0.64 (0.46 to 0.91, P=0.01) for disease progression and 0.60 (0.32 to 1.11, P=0.11) for death. The 94.4-month final analysis reported 0.77 (0.60 to 0.99, P=0.042) for progression.

abcsg16.methods: Prospective phase 3 trial. Postmenopausal women with hormone-receptor-positive breast cancer who had already received 5 years of adjuvant endocrine therapy were randomly assigned to anastrozole for an additional 2 years or an additional 5 years. The primary end point was disease-free survival, analysed in patients still in the trial and free of recurrence 2 years after randomisation. Secondary end points were overall survival, contralateral breast cancer, second primary cancer and clinical bone fracture.
abcsg16.results: Of 3484 women enrolled, 3208 remained without disease progression after the first 2 years of extended treatment following randomisation. In that primary-analysis set, disease progression or death occurred in 335 women in each group at 8 years, a hazard ratio of 0.99 (95% CI 0.85 to 1.15, P=0.90). Most secondary end points showed no between-group difference. Clinical bone fracture risk was higher in the 5-year group, hazard ratio 1.35 (1.00 to 1.84).

abcsg18.methods: Prospective, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 trial at 58 centres in Austria and Sweden. Postmenopausal patients with early hormone receptor-positive breast cancer receiving aromatase inhibitors were randomly assigned 1:1 to denosumab 60 mg or placebo subcutaneously every 6 months, stratified by DXA device type, previous aromatase inhibitor use and baseline bone mineral density. The primary endpoint was time to first clinical fracture by intention to treat. Treatment continued until 247 first clinical fractures had occurred.
abcsg18.results: Of 3425 eligible patients enrolled, 3420 were randomly assigned to denosumab (n=1711) or placebo (n=1709). Time to first clinical fracture was significantly delayed with denosumab, hazard ratio 0.50 (95% CI 0.39 to 0.65, p<0.0001). Fractures numbered 92 with denosumab and 176 with placebo. Adverse events occurred in 80% of the denosumab group and 79% of the placebo group, with serious events in 30% of each. No osteonecrosis of the jaw was reported. 93 patients died.

abrave.methods: Phase III trial. Patients with high-risk early triple-negative breast cancer were randomly assigned to 1 year of avelumab or to observation after completion of surgery and (neo)adjuvant chemotherapy. High risk meant at least pN2 with any pT, pN1/pT2 or pN0/pT3 after primary surgery (stratum A), or invasive residual disease after neoadjuvant chemotherapy (stratum B). Coprimary endpoints were disease-free survival in the intention-to-treat and stratum B populations. Secondary endpoints were overall survival and disease-free survival in PD-L1-positive patients.
abrave.results: 466 patients were randomly assigned, 383 to stratum B and 83 to stratum A. At a median follow-up of 52.1 months, the disease-free survival hazard ratio was 0.81 (95% CI 0.61 to 1.09, P=0.172) in the intention-to-treat population, with 3-year estimates of 68.3% versus 63.2%, and 0.80 (0.58 to 1.10, P=0.170) in stratum B, 66.9% versus 60.7%. The descriptive overall survival hazard ratio was 0.66 (0.45 to 0.97), 3-year rates 84.8% versus 76.3%.

acelera.methods: Randomised phase II study. Post-, pre- and perimenopausal women and men with measurable disease or evaluable bone lesions, whose estrogen receptor-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer had progressed after 1 to 2 lines of systemic therapy, were assigned 1:1 to giredestrant 30 mg orally once daily or to physician's choice of endocrine monotherapy until progression or unacceptable toxicity. Stratification was by visceral disease, prior CDK4/6 inhibitor and prior fulvestrant. The primary end point was investigator-assessed progression-free survival.
acelera.results: At the February 18, 2022 cutoff, with a median follow-up of 7.9 months and 303 patients, the investigator-assessed progression-free survival hazard ratio was 0.81 (95% CI 0.60 to 1.10, P=.1757). Among 232 patients evaluable for circulating tumour DNA, the hazard ratio was 0.60 (0.35 to 1.03) in the 90 with a detectable mutation and 0.88 (0.54 to 1.42) in the 142 without. Related grade 3-4 adverse events, serious adverse events and discontinuations were balanced.

adapt-her2-hr.methods: Prospective, neoadjuvant, phase II trial. 375 patients with early HER2-positive, hormone receptor-positive breast cancer, out of 463 screened, were randomly assigned to 12 weeks of trastuzumab emtansine with or without endocrine therapy, or to trastuzumab plus endocrine therapy. The primary end point was pathologic complete response (ypT0/is ypN0). Early response was assessed in core biopsies taken 3 weeks after starting therapy. Secondary end points included safety and the predictive impact of early response.
adapt-her2-hr.results: More than 90% of patients completed therapy per protocol. Pathologic complete response occurred in 41.0% with trastuzumab emtansine, 41.5% with trastuzumab emtansine plus endocrine therapy and 15.1% with trastuzumab plus endocrine therapy (P < .001). Early responders, 67% of those with assessable response, reached pathologic complete response in 35.7% compared with 19.8% of non-responders (odds ratio 2.2, 95% CI 1.24 to 4.19). Seventeen therapy-related severe adverse events were reported, 5.3% versus 3.1%.

adaptcycle.methods: Analysis within the WSG ADAPTcycle trial at 85 sites in Germany, in which 5292 patients were screened and 1684 randomised. Patients with intermediate-risk hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative early breast cancer defined by Oncotype DX and endocrine therapy response were randomised to (neo)adjuvant chemotherapy followed by endocrine therapy or to ribociclib plus an aromatase inhibitor, with a gonadotropin-releasing hormone agonist in premenopausal women. Local and central Ki67 at baseline and after endocrine therapy were compared.
adaptcycle.results: Median baseline Ki67 was 25% locally (n=4972) and centrally (n=4903). Overall agreement for Ki67 above versus at or below 10% was 86.9% (95% CI 85.9% to 87.9%). After short preoperative endocrine therapy, median Ki67 was 5% locally (n=2786) and 10% centrally (n=4429). Endocrine response, Ki67 at or below 10%, was seen in 1663 patients (64.2%) centrally and 1571 (60.7%) locally, overall agreement 80.5% (79% to 82.1%). Among local responders, 206 (13.1%) were central non-responders.

alienor.methods: Multicentre study. Patients whose tumour did not achieve a pathologically documented complete response after neoadjuvant chemotherapy entered a 5-year liquid biopsy surveillance programme. The primary objective was relapse-free interval in patients with or without circulating tumour DNA detection during adjuvant follow-up. Whole genome sequencing of primary tumour samples supported personalised multiplex digital PCR assays that tracked structural variants in plasma.
alienor.results: Eighty-three patients had a successful structural variant fingerprint designed, covering 473 plasma samples. Median follow-up from surgery was 60.6 months and 27 clinical recurrences (32.5%) occurred. Circulating tumour DNA was detected in 34 patients, 15 of them (44.1%) below 100 parts per million at the earliest positive sample. Detection predicted shorter relapse-free interval, hazard ratio 29.2 (95% CI 6.9 to 124.0, P<0.0001). Median lead time to relapse was 13.9 months. Sensitivity for relapse was 92.6%.

alternate.methods: Phase 3 randomised clinical trial. Postmenopausal women with clinical stage II to III, estrogen receptor-rich, ERBB2-negative breast cancer received anastrozole, fulvestrant or the combination for 6 months preoperatively. Tumour Ki67 was assessed at week 4 and optionally at week 12, and patients with Ki67 above 10% switched to neoadjuvant chemotherapy or immediate surgery. The primary outcome was the endocrine-sensitive disease rate. A secondary outcome was percentage change in Ki67 after 4 weeks.
alternate.results: Between February 2014 and November 2018, 1362 female patients were enrolled. Among 1298 evaluable patients, endocrine-sensitive disease rates were 18.7% with anastrozole, 22.8% with fulvestrant and 20.5% with the combination. Neither fulvestrant-containing regimen significantly improved that rate or week 4 Ki67 suppression. Ki67 above 10% at week 4 or 12 occurred in 25.1%, 24.2% and 15.7% respectively. PAM50 subtyping of 753 baseline biopsies identified 394 luminal A, 304 luminal B and 55 nonluminal tumours.

alternative.methods: Randomised phase III study in postmenopausal women with HER2-positive, hormone receptor-positive metastatic breast cancer who had received prior endocrine therapy and prior neoadjuvant, adjuvant or first-line trastuzumab with chemotherapy. Patients for whom chemotherapy was intended were excluded. Patients were randomised 1:1:1 to lapatinib plus trastuzumab plus an aromatase inhibitor, trastuzumab plus an aromatase inhibitor, or lapatinib plus an aromatase inhibitor. The primary endpoint was investigator-assessed progression-free survival for the triplet versus trastuzumab plus aromatase inhibitor.
alternative.results: 355 patients were analysed, with 120 on the triplet, 117 on trastuzumab plus aromatase inhibitor and 118 on lapatinib plus aromatase inhibitor. The triplet improved progression-free survival over trastuzumab plus aromatase inhibitor (hazard ratio 0.62; 95% CI 0.45 to 0.88; P = .0063), consistently across predefined subgroups. Median progression-free survival with lapatinib plus aromatase inhibitor was 8.3 versus 5.6 months (hazard ratio 0.85; 95% CI 0.62 to 1.17). Diarrhoea occurred in 69% on the triplet.

altto.methods: Randomised phase III trial. Patients with centrally confirmed HER2-positive early breast cancer were randomly assigned to 1 year of adjuvant trastuzumab, lapatinib, the sequence of trastuzumab then lapatinib, or the combination of lapatinib and trastuzumab. The primary end point was disease-free survival, with 850 events required for 80% power to detect a hazard ratio of 0.8 for the combination versus trastuzumab.
altto.results: Between June 2007 and July 2011, 8381 patients were enrolled. In 2011 the lapatinib arm was closed for futility, and a protocol modification required P of .025 or less for the two remaining comparisons. At a median follow-up of 4.5 years and 555 disease-free survival events, the combination gave a hazard ratio of 0.84 (97.5% CI 0.70 to 1.02, P=.048) and the sequence 0.96 (0.80 to 1.15, P=.61). Lapatinib caused more diarrhoea, rash and hepatic toxicity.

amaros.methods: Patients with T1-2 primary breast cancer and no palpable lymphadenopathy were enrolled at 34 centres in nine European countries. Those with a positive sentinel node were randomly assigned 1:1 to axillary lymph node dissection or axillary radiotherapy, stratified by institution. The primary endpoint was non-inferiority of 5-year axillary recurrence, with a margin of not more than 4% versus an expected 2%. Analyses were by intention to treat and per protocol.
amaros.results: Of 4806 eligible patients, 1425 had a positive sentinel node and were randomised. Axillary recurrence occurred in 4 of 744 after dissection and 7 of 681 after radiotherapy. Median follow-up was 6.1 years. 5-year axillary recurrence was 0.43% versus 1.19%. Lymphoedema was more frequent after dissection at 1, 3 and 5 years. The preplanned 10-year analysis reports cumulative axillary recurrence of 0.93% and 1.82%, with no difference in overall or disease-free survival.

ameera3.methods: Open-label, worldwide, randomised phase II trial. Patients with estrogen receptor-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer that had progressed in the (neo)adjuvant or advanced setting after no more than two previous lines of endocrine therapy were assigned 1:1 to amcenestrant or to single-agent endocrine treatment of physician's choice. Stratification was by visceral metastases, previous CDK4/6 inhibitor treatment and ECOG performance status. The primary end point was progression-free survival by independent central review.
ameera3.results: 290 patients were assigned to amcenestrant (n=143) or physician's choice (n=147). Median progression-free survival was 3.6 months versus 3.7 months, stratified hazard ratio 1.051 (95% CI 0.789 to 1.4, one-sided P=.643). Among the 120 of 280 patients with a baseline mutation, median progression-free survival was 3.7 versus 2.0 months, hazard ratio 0.9 (0.565 to 1.435). Overall survival data were immature, hazard ratio 0.913 (0.595 to 1.403). Grade 3 or higher adverse events occurred in 21.7% versus 15.6%.

aphinity.methods: Randomised trial. Patients with node-positive or high-risk node-negative HER2-positive operable breast cancer were randomly assigned to receive either pertuzumab or placebo added to standard adjuvant chemotherapy plus 1 year of trastuzumab. The assumed 3-year invasive-disease-free survival rates were 91.8% with pertuzumab and 89.2% with placebo.
aphinity.results: 2400 patients received pertuzumab and 2405 placebo. 63% had node-positive disease and 36% hormone-receptor-negative disease. Recurrence occurred in 171 patients (7.1%) with pertuzumab and 210 (8.7%) with placebo, hazard ratio 0.81 (95% CI 0.66 to 1.00, P=0.045). Three-year invasive-disease-free survival was 94.1% versus 93.2% overall, 92.0% versus 90.2% in node-positive and 97.5% versus 98.4% in node-negative patients. The 6-year follow-up report gave overall survival of 95% versus 94%, hazard ratio 0.85, P=.17.

apt.methods: Uncontrolled, single-group, multicenter, investigator-initiated study of adjuvant paclitaxel and trastuzumab in 406 patients with node-negative HER2-positive tumors measuring up to 3 cm. Patients received weekly paclitaxel and trastuzumab for 12 weeks, followed by 9 months of trastuzumab monotherapy. The primary end point was survival free from invasive disease.
apt.results: Median follow-up was 4.0 years. The 3-year rate of survival free from invasive disease was 98.7% (95% CI 97.6 to 99.8). Among 12 relapses, 2 were distant metastatic breast cancer. Seven disease-specific events were noted. Grade 3 neuropathy occurred in 13 patients (3.2%), symptomatic congestive heart failure in 2 (0.5%), and significant asymptomatic ejection fraction decline in 13 (3.2%). The final 10-year analysis reported 10-year invasive disease-free survival of 91.3% and overall survival of 94.3%.

ascent.methods: Randomized phase 3 trial of sacituzumab govitecan compared with single-agent chemotherapy of the physician's choice, either eribulin, vinorelbine, capecitabine, or gemcitabine, in patients with relapsed or refractory metastatic triple-negative breast cancer. The primary end point was progression-free survival determined by blinded independent central review among patients without brain metastases.
ascent.results: 468 patients without brain metastases were randomly assigned, 235 to sacituzumab govitecan and 233 to chemotherapy. Median age was 54 years. Median progression-free survival was 5.6 months versus 1.7 months (hazard ratio 0.41, 95% CI 0.32 to 0.52, P<0.001). Median overall survival was 12.1 months versus 6.7 months (hazard ratio 0.48, 95% CI 0.38 to 0.59, P<0.001). Objective response was 35% versus 5%. Grade 3 or higher neutropenia occurred in 51% versus 33%.

ascent03.methods: International, open-label, phase 3 randomized trial in patients with previously untreated, locally advanced unresectable or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer who were not candidates for PD-1 or PD-L1 inhibitors. Tumors were PD-L1-negative with a combined positive score below 10 or PD-L1-positive with a score of 10 or higher. Patients were assigned 1:1 to sacituzumab govitecan or chemotherapy, either paclitaxel, nab-paclitaxel, or gemcitabine plus carboplatin. The primary end point was progression-free survival by blinded independent central review.
ascent03.results: Among 558 patients, median progression-free survival was 9.7 months (95% CI 8.1 to 11.1) with sacituzumab govitecan and 6.9 months (95% CI 5.6 to 8.2) with chemotherapy (stratified hazard ratio 0.62, 95% CI 0.50 to 0.77, P<0.001). A confirmed objective response occurred in 48% versus 46% of patients. Median duration of response was 12.2 months versus 7.2 months. Adverse events of grade 3 or higher occurred in 66% versus 62%.

ascent04.methods: Phase 3, open-label, international trial in patients with previously untreated, PD-L1-positive, locally advanced unresectable or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer. Patients were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to sacituzumab govitecan plus pembrolizumab or chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab. The primary end point was progression-free survival assessed by blinded independent central review. Secondary end points included overall survival, objective response, duration of response, and safety.
ascent04.results: 443 patients were randomly assigned, 221 to sacituzumab govitecan plus pembrolizumab and 222 to chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab. Median progression-free survival was 11.2 months versus 7.8 months (hazard ratio 0.65, 95% CI 0.51 to 0.84, P<0.001). Overall survival data were immature. Objective response was 60% versus 53%. Median duration of response was 16.5 months versus 9.2 months. Grade 3 or higher adverse events occurred in 71% versus 70%. Discontinuation for adverse events was 12% versus 31%.

ascent05.methods: Design report of the international randomized phase 3 AFT-65/ASCENT-05/OptimICE-RD trial. It enrolls patients with early-stage triple-negative breast cancer who have residual invasive disease after neoadjuvant therapy. Sacituzumab govitecan plus pembrolizumab is compared with treatment of physician's choice, which is pembrolizumab with or without capecitabine. The trial was recruiting at the time of this report.

astefania.methods: Randomised trial in patients with high-risk HER2-positive early breast cancer and residual disease after HER2-based neoadjuvant therapy. Patients are randomised within 12 weeks of primary surgery to ado-trastuzumab emtansine combined with either atezolizumab or placebo for 14 cycles. The primary outcome is invasive disease-free survival. Secondary outcomes include additional efficacy endpoints, safety and pharmacokinetics. Planned enrolment is 1,700 patients across 32 countries.

astrra.methods: Randomized phase 3 trial enrolling 1,483 premenopausal women aged 45 years or younger with estrogen receptor-positive breast cancer treated with definitive surgery after adjuvant or neoadjuvant chemotherapy. Ovarian function was assessed every 6 months for 2 years using follicle-stimulating hormone levels and vaginal bleeding history. Patients confirmed premenopausal at each visit were randomly assigned to 5 years of tamoxifen alone or 5 years of tamoxifen with 2 years of monthly goserelin.
astrra.results: 1,293 patients were randomly assigned and 1,282 were eligible for analysis. The estimated 5-year disease-free survival rate was 91.1% with tamoxifen plus ovarian function suppression and 87.5% with tamoxifen alone (hazard ratio 0.69, 95% CI 0.48 to 0.97, p=0.033). The estimated 5-year overall survival rate was 99.4% versus 97.8% (hazard ratio 0.31, 95% CI 0.10 to 0.94, p=0.029). The 8-year follow-up reported 8-year disease-free survival of 85.4% versus 80.2% (hazard ratio 0.67).

atac.methods: Comparison of anastrozole 1 mg with tamoxifen 20 mg, each given orally every day for 5 years as adjuvant treatment for postmenopausal women with early-stage breast cancer, analysed after a median follow-up of 120 months. A proportional hazards model assessed disease-free survival and secondary endpoints in all randomised patients (anastrozole 3125, tamoxifen 3116) and in hormone-receptor-positive patients (anastrozole 2618, tamoxifen 2598). Fractures and serious adverse events continued to be collected in masked fashion.
atac.results: Median follow-up was 120 months. In hormone-receptor-positive patients, anastrozole improved disease-free survival (hazard ratio 0.86, 95% CI 0.78 to 0.95, p=0.003), time to recurrence (0.79, 0.70 to 0.89, p=0.0002) and time to distant recurrence (0.85, 0.73 to 0.98, p=0.02). Absolute differences in time to recurrence were 2.7% at 5 years and 4.3% at 10 years. Overall mortality differed little (0.95, 0.84 to 1.06, p=0.4). Fractures during active treatment numbered 451 versus 351.

atempt.methods: Patients with stage I centrally confirmed HER2-positive breast cancer were randomly assigned 3:1 to trastuzumab emtansine 3.6 mg/kg intravenously every 3 weeks for 17 cycles or to paclitaxel 80 mg/m2 with weekly trastuzumab for 12 weeks followed by trastuzumab for 39 weeks. The co-primary objectives were to compare the incidence of clinically relevant toxicities between the arms and to evaluate invasive disease-free survival with trastuzumab emtansine.
atempt.results: The analysis population was 497 patients who initiated protocol therapy, 383 on trastuzumab emtansine and 114 on paclitaxel plus trastuzumab. Clinically relevant toxicities were experienced by 46% on trastuzumab emtansine and 47% on paclitaxel plus trastuzumab (p=0.83). The 3-year invasive disease-free survival with trastuzumab emtansine was 97.8% (95% CI 96.3 to 99.3). The 5-year report gave 5-year invasive disease-free survival of 97.0% and overall survival of 97.8%.

atezolizumab-plus-pertuzumab-and-high-do.methods: Single-arm multicentre phase II trial in patients with HER2-positive breast cancer and brain metastases. Participants received atezolizumab 1,200 mg intravenously every 3 weeks, pertuzumab at a loading dose of 840 mg followed by 420 mg every 3 weeks, and high-dose trastuzumab 6 mg/kg weekly for 24 weeks and then every 3 weeks. The primary endpoint was CNS overall response rate by RANO-BM criteria. Secondary endpoints included clinical benefit rate, overall survival and safety.
atezolizumab-plus-pertuzumab-and-high-do.results: 19 participants were enrolled. Two had a confirmed intracranial partial response, giving a CNS overall response rate of 10.5% (90% CI 1.9 to 29.6). The prespecified efficacy threshold was not met and the study was terminated early. The clinical benefit rate was 42.1% at 18 weeks and 31.6% at 24 weeks. Seven patients (36.8%) required a dose delay or hold. The most frequent any-grade adverse events were diarrhoea and fatigue, each 26.3%.

atlas.methods: In the worldwide ATLAS trial, 12,894 women with early breast cancer who had completed 5 years of tamoxifen were randomly allocated 1:1 by central computer minimisation to continue tamoxifen to 10 years or to stop at 5 years with open control. Women entered between 1996 and 2005. Yearly follow-up forms recorded any recurrence, second cancer, hospital admission, or death. Breast cancer outcomes are reported for the 6846 women with ER-positive disease.
atlas.results: Among women with ER-positive disease, continuing tamoxifen reduced recurrence (617 recurrences in 3428 women versus 711 in 3418 controls, p=0.002), breast cancer mortality (331 versus 397 deaths, p=0.01) and overall mortality (639 versus 722 deaths, p=0.01). Cumulative recurrence risk during years 5 to 14 was 21.4% versus 25.1%, and breast cancer mortality 12.2% versus 15.0%. The rate ratio was 1.87 for pulmonary embolus and 1.74 for endometrial cancer.

attom.methods: Translational analysis within the aTTom trial of 10 versus 5 years of adjuvant tamoxifen. Breast Cancer Index HOXB13/IL17BR results were available for 2,445 aTTom patients. The primary endpoint was recurrence-free interval and the secondary endpoints were disease-free interval and disease-free survival, examined using Cox proportional hazards regression and the log-rank test.
attom.results: In the overall population of 2,445 patients, extended tamoxifen did not significantly improve recurrence-free interval (hazard ratio 0.90; 95% CI 0.69 to 1.16; P = .401). In the preplanned node-positive subset of 789 patients, Breast Cancer Index (H/I)-High patients benefited from extended tamoxifen (9.7% absolute benefit; hazard ratio 0.33; 95% CI 0.14 to 0.75; P = .016) while (H/I)-Low patients did not (hazard ratio 1.11; P = .581). The treatment-by-biomarker interaction was significant (P = .037).

b35.methods: Double-blind, randomised, phase 3 NSABP trial done at 333 centres in the USA and Canada. Postmenopausal women with hormone-positive ductal carcinoma in situ treated by lumpectomy with clear resection margins and whole-breast irradiation were randomly assigned 1:1 to oral tamoxifen 20 mg per day or oral anastrozole 1 mg per day for 5 years, each with a matching placebo. Randomisation was stratified by age. The primary outcome was breast cancer-free interval, analysed by intention to treat.
b35.results: Between January 2003 and June 2006, 3104 eligible patients were enrolled, 1552 to each group. Median follow-up was 9.0 years. There were 212 breast cancer-free interval events, 122 in the tamoxifen group and 90 in the anastrozole group (hazard ratio 0.73, 95% CI 0.56 to 0.96, p=0.0234). Interactions with time (p=0.0410) and with age group (p=0.0379) were significant. Grade 4 or worse thrombosis or embolism occurred 17 times versus four.

b59.methods: Multicenter, multinational, double-blinded randomized phase 3 trial in stage II to III triple-negative breast cancer. Patients were randomized to atezolizumab (773 patients) or placebo (777 patients) added to sequential taxane, carboplatin and anthracycline-based neoadjuvant chemotherapy. The primary endpoint was event-free survival.
b59.results: Atezolizumab did not significantly improve event-free survival (hazard ratio 0.80, 95% CI 0.062 to 1.03, stratified log-rank P=0.083), with a 4-year event-free survival difference of 3.3 points. The hazard ratio for overall survival was 0.86 (95% CI 0.62 to 1.19), with a 4-year benefit of 0.7 points. Subgroup analyses suggested benefit in patients with clinical lymph node involvement (P=0.039). Grade 3 or higher treatment-emergent adverse events occurred in 75.3% versus 73.4%.

bcirg006.methods: 3222 women with HER2-positive early-stage breast cancer were randomly assigned to doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide followed by docetaxel every 3 weeks (AC-T), to the same regimen plus 52 weeks of trastuzumab, or to docetaxel and carboplatin plus 52 weeks of trastuzumab (TCH). The primary end point was disease-free survival. Secondary end points were overall survival and safety.
bcirg006.results: At a median follow-up of 65 months, 656 events triggered the protocol-specified analysis. Estimated 5-year disease-free survival was 75% with AC-T, 84% with AC-T plus trastuzumab, and 81% with TCH. Estimated 5-year overall survival was 87%, 92%, and 91%. No significant differences in disease-free or overall survival were found between the two trastuzumab regimens. Both were superior to AC-T. Congestive heart failure and cardiac dysfunction were significantly more frequent with AC-T plus trastuzumab than with TCH (P<0.001).

big1-98.methods: BIG 1-98 is a randomised, double-blind, phase 3 trial in postmenopausal women with hormone receptor-positive early breast cancer. It compares 5 years of tamoxifen or letrozole monotherapy against sequential treatment with 2 years of one drug followed by 3 years of the other. Randomisation was stratified by randomisation option, participating institution and chemotherapy use. The primary endpoint was disease-free survival. Secondary endpoints were overall survival, distant recurrence-free interval and breast cancer-free interval.
big1-98.results: 8010 patients were enrolled, with a median follow-up of 8.1 years. At 8.7 years median follow-up letrozole monotherapy was better than tamoxifen by intention to treat. Disease-free survival HR was 0.86 (0.78-0.96), overall survival HR 0.87 (0.77-0.999), distant recurrence-free interval HR 0.86, breast cancer-free interval HR 0.86. Neither sequence differed from letrozole monotherapy on any endpoint. The 12.6-year long-term follow-up reported a disease-free survival HR of 0.91 (0.81-1.01).

bolero2.methods: This was a phase 3 randomised trial in 724 patients with hormone receptor-positive advanced breast cancer who had recurrence or progression on a nonsteroidal aromatase inhibitor given in the adjuvant setting or for advanced disease. Patients were assigned 2:1 to everolimus plus exemestane or placebo plus exemestane. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival. Secondary endpoints included survival, response rate and safety. A preplanned interim analysis was done after 359 progression-free survival events.
bolero2.results: Median age was 62 years, 56% had visceral involvement and 84% had hormone-sensitive disease. At the interim analysis median progression-free survival by local investigator assessment was 6.9 months with everolimus plus exemestane and 2.8 months with placebo plus exemestane (hazard ratio 0.43, 95% CI 0.35-0.54). By central assessment the medians were 10.6 and 4.1 months (hazard ratio 0.36, 0.27-0.47). The 2014 overall survival report gave median overall survival of 31.0 versus 26.6 months (hazard ratio 0.89).

brightness.methods: This was a phase 3, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial at 145 sites in 15 countries. Patients aged 18 years and older with untreated clinical stage II-III triple-negative breast cancer and ECOG performance status 0 or 1 were randomly assigned 2:1:1 to weekly paclitaxel plus carboplatin plus veliparib, paclitaxel plus carboplatin plus veliparib placebo, or paclitaxel with both placebos. All then received four cycles of doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide. The primary endpoint was pathological complete response in breast and lymph nodes.
brightness.results: 634 patients were randomised, 316 to paclitaxel plus carboplatin plus veliparib, 160 to paclitaxel plus carboplatin, and 158 to paclitaxel alone. Pathological complete response was reached in 168 of 316 (53%) with veliparib and carboplatin, 92 of 160 (58%) with carboplatin, and 49 of 158 (31%) with paclitaxel alone (p<0.0001 versus paclitaxel alone, p=0.36 versus carboplatin). The 4.5-year follow-up reported event-free survival HR 0.57 (0.36-0.91) for carboplatin with paclitaxel versus paclitaxel, with no overall survival difference.

brocade3.methods: Randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 trial in 36 countries. Adults with germline BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutations, advanced HER2-negative breast cancer, ECOG 0 to 2, and up to two prior chemotherapy lines for metastatic disease were assigned 2:1 to carboplatin AUC 6 plus weekly paclitaxel with veliparib 120 mg twice daily or placebo. Veliparib or placebo continued at a higher dose if chemotherapy stopped. Primary endpoint was investigator-assessed progression-free survival.
brocade3.results: 509 patients were analysed, 337 assigned veliparib and 172 placebo. Median follow-up was about 35.7 months. Median progression-free survival was 14.5 months versus 12.6 months, hazard ratio 0.71 (95% CI 0.57 to 0.88), p=0.0016. Grade 3 or worse neutropenia occurred in 81% versus 84%, anaemia in 42% versus 40%, thrombocytopenia in 40% versus 28%. Serious adverse events occurred in 34% versus 29%. There were no study drug-related deaths.

bylieve.methods: Ongoing phase 2, multicentre, open-label, non-comparative study at 114 sites in 18 countries. Cohort A enrolled adults with hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer and a tumour PIK3CA mutation who had progressed on a CDK4/6 inhibitor plus an aromatase inhibitor as immediate previous treatment, with ECOG 2 or less and no more than two prior anticancer treatments. Patients received alpelisib 300 mg daily plus fulvestrant 500 mg. Primary endpoint was the proportion alive without progression at 6 months.
bylieve.results: 127 patients with at least 6 months of follow-up were enrolled in cohort A and 121 had a centrally confirmed PIK3CA mutation. Median follow-up was 11.7 months. 61 of 121 patients, 50.4% (95% CI 41.2 to 59.6), were alive without disease progression at 6 months. Grade 3 or worse hyperglycaemia occurred in 28%, rash in 9% and maculopapular rash in 9%. Serious adverse events occurred in 26%. No treatment-related deaths were reported.

calgb-40502-ncctg-n063h.methods: Randomised phase 3 trial. Patients aged 18 years or older with chemotherapy-naive advanced breast cancer were assigned to bevacizumab plus one of three weekly regimens given 3 weeks of every 4: paclitaxel 90 mg/m2, nab-paclitaxel 150 mg/m2, or ixabepilone 16 mg/m2. Planned enrolment was 900 patients, giving 88% power to detect a hazard ratio of 0.73. The comparison was progression-free survival for each experimental arm against paclitaxel.
calgb-40502-ncctg-n063h.results: 799 patients were enrolled and 783 received treatment, with 97% receiving bevacizumab. The ixabepilone arm closed for futility at the first interim analysis and the other two arms closed at the second. Median progression-free survival was 11 months with paclitaxel, 7.4 months with ixabepilone (hazard ratio 1.59, 95% CI 1.31 to 1.93, p<0.001) and 9.3 months with nab-paclitaxel (hazard ratio 1.20, 95% CI 1.00 to 1.45, p=0.054). Toxicity including peripheral neuropathy was greater with nab-paclitaxel.

calgb-40601.methods: Randomised phase 3 neoadjuvant trial. 305 women with untreated stage II and III HER2-positive breast cancer were assigned to weekly paclitaxel combined with trastuzumab plus lapatinib, with trastuzumab alone, or with lapatinib alone. The primary endpoint was pathological complete response. Secondary endpoints included relapse-free survival, overall survival and gene expression analyses. mRNA sequencing was performed on 264 pretreatment samples.
calgb-40601.results: 118 patients were assigned paclitaxel with trastuzumab and lapatinib, 120 paclitaxel with trastuzumab and 67 paclitaxel with lapatinib. At more than 7 years, dual blockade improved relapse-free survival (hazard ratio 0.32, 95% CI 0.14 to 0.71, p=0.005) and overall survival (hazard ratio 0.34, 95% CI 0.12 to 0.94, p=0.037) versus trastuzumab alone, with no difference between trastuzumab and lapatinib. Of 688 signatures, 215 were associated with pathological complete response and 45 with relapse-free survival.

calgb-9344.methods: Randomised adjuvant trial. 3121 women with operable breast cancer and involved lymph nodes were assigned after surgery to cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m2 with doxorubicin at 60, 75 or 90 mg/m2 for four cycles, followed by either no further therapy or four cycles of paclitaxel 175 mg/m2. Tamoxifen was given to 94% of patients with hormone receptor-positive tumours. Endpoints were time to recurrence and survival.
calgb-9344.results: There was no doxorubicin dose effect, with 5-year disease-free survival of 69%, 66% and 67% at 60, 75 and 90 mg/m2. Adding paclitaxel reduced the hazard of recurrence by 17% (p=0.0023) and of death by 18% (p=0.0064). Five-year disease-free survival was 70% with paclitaxel versus 65% without, and overall survival 80% versus 77%. In an unplanned analysis the recurrence hazard ratio was 0.72 in oestrogen receptor-negative and 0.91 in receptor-positive tumours.

calgb40603.methods: CALGB 40603 was a 2 x 2 factorial, open-label, randomised phase 2 trial. 443 patients with stage II to III triple-negative breast cancer received weekly paclitaxel 80 mg/m2 for 12 weeks followed by four cycles of doxorubicin plus cyclophosphamide every 2 weeks. They were randomly assigned to carboplatin AUC 6 every 3 weeks for four cycles and/or bevacizumab 10 mg/kg every 2 weeks for nine cycles. Endpoints were pathological complete response in breast and in breast and axilla.
calgb40603.results: Using one-sided P values, carboplatin raised pathological complete response in the breast from 44% to 60% (P = .0018) and bevacizumab from 48% to 59% (P = .0089). Only carboplatin raised pathological complete response in breast and axilla, 54% versus 41% (P = .0029). More-than-additive interaction between the agents was not demonstrated. Patients given either agent less often completed treatment without dose changes. The long-term report at median 7.9 years found no outcome gain from either agent.

calgb49907.methods: Patients aged 65 years or older with early breast cancer were randomly assigned to standard adjuvant chemotherapy or capecitabine. Standard chemotherapy was the physician's choice of cyclophosphamide, methotrexate and fluorouracil, or cyclophosphamide and doxorubicin. An adaptive Bayesian design determined the sample size and tested noninferiority of capecitabine. The primary endpoint was recurrence-free survival. This report updates the trial at a median follow-up of 11.4 years.
calgb49907.results: The design stopped accrual with 633 patients. At 10 years, recurrence-free survival was 56% with standard chemotherapy and 50% with capecitabine (HR 0.80, P = .03). Breast cancer-specific survival was 88% and 82% (HR 0.62, P = .03). Overall survival was 62% and 56% (HR 0.84, P = .16). Standard chemotherapy remained superior in hormone receptor-negative patients (HR 0.66, P = .02) but not in receptor-positive patients (HR 0.89, P = .43). 43.9% of patients had died.

calgb9343.methods: Between July 1994 and February 1999, 636 women aged 70 years or older with clinical stage I (T1N0M0) estrogen receptor-positive breast carcinoma treated by lumpectomy were randomly assigned to tamoxifen plus radiation therapy (317 women) or tamoxifen alone (319 women). Primary endpoints were time to local or regional recurrence, frequency of mastectomy, breast cancer-specific survival, time to distant metastasis and overall survival.
calgb9343.results: Median follow-up for treated patients was 12.6 years. At 10 years, 98% of women given tamoxifen plus radiation (95% CI 96% to 99%) were free from local and regional recurrence, compared with 90% of those given tamoxifen alone (95% CI 85% to 93%). Time to mastectomy, time to distant metastasis, breast cancer-specific survival and overall survival did not differ significantly. Ten-year overall survival was 67% (62% to 72%) with radiation and 66% (61% to 71%) without.

calgb9741.methods: This adjuvant trial used a 2 x 2 factorial design in women with axillary node-positive breast cancer. 2005 patients were randomly assigned to one of four regimens. These were sequential doxorubicin, then paclitaxel, then cyclophosphamide, four doses each, given every 3 weeks or every 2 weeks with filgrastim, or concurrent doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide for four cycles followed by four cycles of paclitaxel, given every 3 weeks or every 2 weeks with filgrastim. The primary endpoint was disease-free survival.
calgb9741.results: At a protocol-specified analysis at median follow-up of 36 months, 315 patients had relapsed or died against 515 expected treatment failures. Dose-dense treatment improved disease-free survival (risk ratio 0.74, P = .010) and overall survival (risk ratio 0.69, P = .013). Four-year disease-free survival was 82% for the dose-dense regimens and 75% for the others. Concurrent and sequential schedules did not differ. There was no interaction between density and sequence. Severe neutropenia was less frequent with dose-dense treatment.

calor.methods: CALOR was a pragmatic, open-label, randomised trial. It accrued patients with histologically proven, completely excised isolated locoregional recurrence after unilateral breast cancer treated by mastectomy or lumpectomy with clear surgical margins. Patients were centrally randomised 1:1 to chemotherapy, type selected by the investigator, or to no chemotherapy, stratified by previous chemotherapy, hormone receptor status and location of the recurrence. Endocrine therapy, radiotherapy for involved margins and anti-HER2 therapy were specified separately. The primary endpoint was disease-free survival.
calor.results: From August 2003 to January 2010, 85 patients were assigned chemotherapy and 77 no chemotherapy. At a median follow-up of 4.9 years, 24 of 85 (28%) in the chemotherapy group had a disease-free survival event, compared with 34 of 77 (44%). Five-year disease-free survival was 69% with chemotherapy and 57% without (hazard ratio 0.59, 95% CI 0.35-0.99, p=0.046). Benefit was greater for oestrogen receptor-negative recurrence (p interaction 0.046). Serious adverse events occurred in 12 of 81 treated patients.

cambria1.methods: CAMBRIA-1 is a phase 3, randomised, open-label trial in patients with ER-positive, HER2-negative early breast cancer at intermediate or high risk of recurrence. It compares 5 years of the next-generation oral selective estrogen receptor degrader camizestrant with standard endocrine therapy, either an aromatase inhibitor or tamoxifen. Patients enter after 2 to 5 years of standard endocrine therapy, with or without a CDK4/6 inhibitor, and without recurrence. The primary endpoint is invasive breast cancer-free survival.

cambria2.methods: CAMBRIA-2 is a phase 3, randomised, open-label trial in patients with ER-positive, HER2-negative early breast cancer at intermediate or high risk of recurrence. It compares 7 years of upfront adjuvant camizestrant, a next-generation oral selective estrogen receptor degrader, with standard endocrine therapy, either an aromatase inhibitor or tamoxifen. Abemaciclib is permitted in both arms for the first 2 years. The primary endpoint is invasive breast cancer-free survival. Secondary endpoints include invasive disease-free survival, distant recurrence-free survival and overall survival.

capitello-290.methods: Randomised global phase 3 trial. Patients with previously untreated metastatic triple-negative breast cancer were randomised 1:1 to paclitaxel 80 mg/m2 on day 1 of weeks 1 to 3 of each 4-week cycle plus either capivasertib 400 mg or placebo twice daily on days 2 to 5 of those weeks. PIK3CA, AKT1 and PTEN alterations were analysed by retrospective central molecular testing. Dual primary endpoints were overall survival overall and in altered tumours, with investigator-assessed progression-free survival a key secondary endpoint.
capitello-290.results: 812 patients were randomised from July 2019 to February 2022 and 30.7% had PIK3CA, AKT1 or PTEN alterations. Median overall survival was 17.7 versus 18.0 months (hazard ratio 0.92, 95% CI 0.78 to 1.08, p=0.3239), and 20.4 months in both arms among altered tumours (hazard ratio 1.05, p=0.7602). Median progression-free survival was 5.6 versus 5.1 months (hazard ratio 0.72), and 7.5 versus 5.6 months in altered tumours (hazard ratio 0.70). Grade 3 or worse diarrhoea occurred in 12.7% versus 0.7%.

capitello291.methods: This was a phase 3, randomised, double-blind trial. It enrolled pre-, peri- and postmenopausal women and men with hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer who had relapsed or progressed during or after an aromatase inhibitor, with or without previous CDK4/6 inhibitor therapy. Patients were randomly assigned 1:1 to capivasertib plus fulvestrant or placebo plus fulvestrant. The dual primary endpoint was investigator-assessed progression-free survival in the overall population and in patients with AKT pathway-altered tumours. Safety was assessed.
capitello291.results: 708 patients underwent randomisation. 289 (40.8%) had AKT pathway alterations and 489 (69.1%) had previously received a CDK4/6 inhibitor for advanced disease. In the overall population median progression-free survival was 7.2 months with capivasertib-fulvestrant and 3.6 months with placebo-fulvestrant (hazard ratio 0.60, 95% CI 0.51-0.71, P<0.001). In the AKT pathway-altered population it was 7.3 versus 3.1 months (hazard ratio 0.50, 0.38-0.65, P<0.001). Grade 3 or higher rash occurred in 12.1% versus 0.3%, diarrhoea in 9.3% versus 0.3%.

cbcsg006.methods: Open-label, randomised, phase 3 trial at 12 Chinese centres. Patients aged 18 to 70 years with previously untreated metastatic triple-negative breast cancer and ECOG 0 or 1 were assigned 1:1 to cisplatin 75 mg/m2 on day 1 with gemcitabine 1250 mg/m2 on days 1 and 8, or paclitaxel 175 mg/m2 on day 1 with the same gemcitabine, every 3 weeks for up to eight cycles. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival, with a non-inferiority margin of 1.2.
cbcsg006.results: 236 of 240 randomised patients received at least one dose and were analysed, 118 per group. After median follow-up of about 16 months the hazard ratio for progression-free survival was 0.692 (95% CI 0.523 to 0.915), non-inferiority p<0.0001 and superiority p=0.009. Median progression-free survival was 7.73 months with cisplatin and gemcitabine versus 6.47 months with paclitaxel and gemcitabine. Grade 3 or 4 anaemia (33% versus 5%) and thrombocytopenia (32% versus 3%) were more common with cisplatin.

checkmate7fl.methods: This was a randomised, multicentre, double-blind phase 3 trial. 510 patients with newly diagnosed, high-risk, grade 3 or grade 2 (ER 1 to 10% or less) ER-positive, HER2-negative primary breast cancer were randomised to anthracycline and taxane-based neoadjuvant chemotherapy with either intravenous nivolumab or placebo. The primary endpoint was pathological complete response.
checkmate7fl.results: Pathological complete response was 24.5% with nivolumab and 13.8% with placebo (P = 0.0021). In patients with PD-L1-positive tumours (VENTANA SP142 1% or above) the rates were 44.3% and 20.2%. No new safety signals were identified. Five deaths occurred in the nivolumab arm, two of them related to study drug toxicity. No deaths occurred in the placebo arm.

ciboma.methods: Phase 3 trial in patients with operable triple-negative breast cancer, either node-positive or node-negative with a tumour of 1 cm or more, who had received prior anthracycline and/or taxane chemotherapy. Triple-negative status was confirmed centrally by immunohistochemistry. Patients were randomly assigned to capecitabine or observation. Stratification was by institution, prior taxane-based therapy, involved axillary nodes, and centrally determined basal or non-basal phenotype. The primary objective was to compare disease-free survival between the arms.
ciboma.results: 876 patients were assigned to capecitabine (448) or observation (428). Median age was 49 years, 55.9% were node-negative, 73.9% had a basal phenotype, and 67.5% had received anthracyclines plus taxanes. Median follow-up was 7.3 years. The disease-free survival hazard ratio was 0.82 (95% CI 0.63 to 1.06, P=.136). In non-basal patients the disease-free survival hazard ratio was 0.53 versus 0.94 in basal disease (interaction P=.0694), and overall survival 0.42 versus 1.23 (interaction P=.0052).

citrine.methods: Randomised, open label, phase 3 trial at one centre in China between March 2020 and March 2022. Female patients with operable high risk triple negative breast cancer, node positive or node negative with Ki-67 of 50% or more, were randomised 1:1 after surgery. The carboplatin arm received four cycles of two weekly epirubicin and cyclophosphamide then four cycles of weekly paclitaxel with carboplatin. The control arm received the same regimen without carboplatin. The primary endpoint was disease-free survival.
citrine.results: 808 patients were enrolled and 807 received treatment. At a median follow-up of 44.7 months, three year disease-free survival was 92.3% with carboplatin and 85.8% in the control arm (hazard ratio 0.64, 95% CI 0.43 to 0.95, P=0.03), but the proportional hazards assumption was violated (P=0.02). Three year overall survival was 98.0% versus 94.0% (hazard ratio 0.41, 0.20 to 0.83, P=0.01). Grade 3-4 treatment related adverse events occurred in 66.7% versus 55.0%.

cleopatra.methods: Double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled phase 3 trial at 204 centres in 25 countries. Eligible patients were 18 years or older with HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer, no previous chemotherapy or biological treatment for metastatic disease, and ECOG performance status 0 or 1. Patients were randomly assigned 1:1 to pertuzumab or placebo, each with trastuzumab and docetaxel given intravenously every 3 weeks, stratified by geographical region and previous treatment. This prespecified end-of-study analysis was descriptive.
cleopatra.results: 808 patients were randomly assigned, 402 to pertuzumab and 406 to placebo. 50 patients crossed over from placebo to pertuzumab. Median follow-up was 99.9 months in the pertuzumab group and 98.7 months in the placebo group. Median overall survival was 57.1 months versus 40.8 months (hazard ratio 0.69, 95% CI 0.58 to 0.82). The 8-year landmark overall survival rate was 37% versus 23%. The most common grade 3-4 adverse event was neutropenia, in 49% versus 46%.

clever.methods: Randomised phase 2 trial in breast cancer survivors within 5 years of diagnosis who had detectable disseminated tumour cells on bone marrow aspirate. Patients received hydroxychloroquine, everolimus, or the combination. Primary endpoints were feasibility and safety. Secondary endpoints included disseminated tumour cell reduction or clearance and recurrence-free survival.
clever.results: 51 patients with detectable disseminated tumour cells started hydroxychloroquine (15), everolimus (15), or both (21). Treatment was feasible and tolerable, and one patient stopped early for grade 3 toxicity. At 42 months median follow-up, landmark 3-year recurrence-free survival was 91.7% for hydroxychloroquine, 92.9% for everolimus, and 100% for the combination, and was greater in patients who cleared disseminated tumour cells (hazard ratio 0.21, 95% CI 0.01 to 3.4). Estimated disseminated tumour cell reductions were 80%, 78%, and 87%.

comet.methods: Prospective randomised noninferiority trial at 100 US Alliance clinical trial sites from 2017 to 2023. It enrolled 995 women aged 40 years or older with newly diagnosed hormone receptor-positive grade 1 or 2 ductal carcinoma in situ without invasive cancer. Randomisation was to active monitoring with imaging and physical examination every 6 months (n=484) or guideline-concordant care, surgery with or without radiation (n=473). The primary outcome was 2-year cumulative ipsilateral invasive cancer, with a noninferiority bound of 5%.
comet.results: 957 participants were analysed. Median follow-up was 36.9 months. 346 patients had surgery for ductal carcinoma in situ, 264 in the guideline-concordant care group and 82 in the active monitoring group. 46 women were diagnosed with invasive cancer, 19 with active monitoring and 27 with guideline-concordant care. The 2-year cumulative rate of ipsilateral invasive cancer was 4.2% with active monitoring and 5.9% with guideline-concordant care, a difference of -1.7% with an upper 95% CI limit of 0.95%.

compassher2-rd.methods: Ongoing prospective, multicentre, phase 3 randomised trial in the United States and Canada. Eligible patients have high-risk HER2-positive residual disease after a predefined course of neoadjuvant chemotherapy and HER2-directed treatment, high risk being oestrogen receptor-negative and/or node-positive. Patients are randomised 1:1 to adjuvant T-DM1 plus placebo or T-DM1 plus tucatinib, alongside adjuvant radiotherapy and endocrine therapy where indicated. The primary objective is invasive disease-free survival.

compassher2pcr.methods: Single-arm trial in patients with clinical stage II or IIIa HER2-positive breast cancer. Patients received four cycles of trastuzumab and pertuzumab with either weekly paclitaxel for 12 weeks or docetaxel every 3 weeks for four cycles, followed by surgery. This report covers the secondary endpoints of pathologic complete response and associated factors. The HER2DX pCR score was measured on diagnostic biopsies in a subset. Logistic regression identified factors associated with response.
compassher2pcr.results: 2,175 patients were enrolled, 781 oestrogen receptor-negative and 1,394 oestrogen receptor-positive. Among the 2,141 who started treatment the pathologic complete response rate was 43.8%, 63.7% in oestrogen receptor-negative and 32.4% in oestrogen receptor-positive tumours. Higher rates occurred with negative or low oestrogen and progesterone receptor expression, HER2 immunohistochemistry 3+, and weekly paclitaxel. T3 disease had a lower rate in oestrogen receptor-negative tumours. Among 569 patients tested, a high HER2DX score independently predicted response.

confirm.methods: Double-blind, parallel-group, multicentre phase 3 study in postmenopausal women with oestrogen receptor-positive advanced breast cancer who had progressed after prior endocrine therapy. Patients were randomly assigned to fulvestrant 500 mg, given intramuscularly on days 0, 14 and 28 and every 28 days thereafter, or fulvestrant 250 mg every 28 days. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival. Secondary endpoints included objective response rate, clinical benefit rate, duration of clinical benefit, overall survival and quality of life.
confirm.results: Progression-free survival was longer with fulvestrant 500 mg (n=362) than 250 mg (n=374), hazard ratio 0.80, 95% CI 0.68 to 0.94, P=.006. Objective response rate was 9.1% versus 10.2% and clinical benefit rate 45.6% versus 39.6%. Duration of clinical benefit was 16.6 versus 13.9 months and overall survival 25.1 versus 22.8 months. The final overall survival report gave median survival of 26.4 versus 22.3 months, hazard ratio 0.81, 95% CI 0.69 to 0.96.

coralleen.methods: Multicentre, randomised, open-label phase 2 trial at 21 hospitals in Spain. Postmenopausal women with stage I-IIIA hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative, PAM50 luminal B breast cancer and an operable tumour of at least 2 cm were randomly assigned 1:1 to six cycles of ribociclib plus letrozole or to four cycles of doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide followed by 12 weeks of paclitaxel. Neoadjuvant treatment lasted 24 weeks. The primary endpoint was the proportion with PAM50 low risk-of-relapse disease at surgery.
coralleen.results: 106 patients were enrolled. At baseline 92 (87%) had high risk-of-relapse disease and 14 (13%) intermediate. Median follow-up was 200 days. At surgery 23 of 49 patients (46.9%, 95% CI 32.5 to 61.7) in the ribociclib plus letrozole group and 24 of 52 (46.1%, 32.9 to 61.5) in the chemotherapy group were low risk-of-relapse. The most common grade 3-4 adverse event was neutropenia, in 43% and 60%. No deaths occurred.

create-x.methods: 910 patients with HER2-negative residual invasive breast cancer after neoadjuvant chemotherapy containing anthracycline, taxane, or both were randomly assigned to standard postsurgical treatment either with capecitabine or without it. The primary endpoint was disease-free survival. Secondary endpoints included overall survival.
create-x.results: The trial stopped early because the prespecified interim analysis met the primary endpoint. At 5 years, disease-free survival was 74.1% with capecitabine versus 67.6% in controls (hazard ratio 0.70, 95% CI 0.53 to 0.92, P=0.01) and overall survival was 89.2% versus 83.6% (hazard ratio 0.59, 95% CI 0.39 to 0.90, P=0.01). In triple-negative disease, disease-free survival was 69.8% versus 56.1% (hazard ratio 0.58) and overall survival 78.8% versus 70.3% (hazard ratio 0.52). Hand-foot syndrome affected 73.4%.

ctrak-tn.methods: Multicentre phase 2 trial with integrated prospective circulating tumour DNA surveillance by digital PCR. Patients had early-stage triple-negative breast cancer with residual disease after neoadjuvant chemotherapy, or stage II or III disease treated with adjuvant chemotherapy. Blood was sampled every three months to 12 months. Patients with detected circulating tumour DNA were randomised 2:1 to pembrolizumab or observation, and the observation group was closed by amendment. Co-primary endpoints were detection rate and sustained clearance on pembrolizumab.
ctrak-tn.results: 208 patients registered, 185 had tumour sequenced, 171 (92.4%) had trackable mutations and 161 entered surveillance. Circulating tumour DNA was detected by 12 months in 27.3% (44 of 161). Seven patients relapsed without prior detection. Forty-five patients entered the therapeutic component, 31 to intervention and 14 to observation. Of those allocated to intervention, 72% (23 of 32) had metastases on staging, and four declined pembrolizumab. None of the five who started pembrolizumab achieved sustained clearance.

daisy.methods: Phase 2 trial of trastuzumab deruxtecan in metastatic breast cancer, enrolling three cohorts by HER2 status: HER2-overexpressing (n=72), HER2-low (n=74) and HER2 non-expressing (n=40). The primary endpoint was confirmed objective response rate. Secondary endpoints included safety. Tumour samples were examined for T-DXd staining and ERBB2 expression.
daisy.results: In the full analysis set of 177 patients, the confirmed objective response rate was 70.6% (95% CI 58.3 to 81) in the HER2-overexpressing cohort, 37.5% (26.4 to 49.7) in HER2-low and 29.7% (15.9 to 47) in non-expressing disease. The primary endpoint was met in the first two cohorts. No new safety signals were observed. Among HER2 immunohistochemistry 0 patients, 5 of 14 (35.7%) with below-median ERBB2 expression responded versus 3 of 10 (30%) above the median.

daphne.methods: Single-arm prospective phase 2 trial. Patients with treatment-naive stage II to III HER2-positive breast cancer received neoadjuvant weekly paclitaxel for 12 doses with trastuzumab and pertuzumab every 3 weeks for 4 doses, then surgery. Adjuvant therapy was guided by pathologic response, with antibody doublet alone for patients with pathologic complete response. The primary endpoint was receipt of adjuvant non-HER2-directed cytotoxic chemotherapy.
daphne.results: Ninety-eight patients received at least one dose. Median age was 50 years, 86 percent had stage II tumours and 34 percent were hormone receptor negative. Five patients with incomplete clinical response received doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide before surgery and were classified as non-pCR. The overall pCR rate was 56.7 percent. Adherence to antibody-only adjuvant therapy was 98.2 percent. At median follow-up of 19.1 months there were no recurrences.

data.methods: Prospective, randomised, open-label, multicentre phase 3 study in 79 hospitals in the Netherlands. Postmenopausal women with hormone receptor-positive early breast cancer and no sign of recurrence after 2 to 3 years of adjuvant tamoxifen were randomly assigned 1:1 to 3 or 6 years of anastrozole 1 mg once daily. Stratification was by nodal status, hormone receptor status, HER2 status and duration of tamoxifen. The primary endpoint was disease-free survival starting beyond 3 years after randomisation.
data.results: 1912 patients were screened, 955 assigned to 3 years and 957 to 6 years of anastrozole. 1860 were eligible and 1660 were disease free 3 years after randomisation. Five-year adapted disease-free survival was 83.1% (95% CI 80.0 to 86.3) in the 6-year group and 79.4% in the 3-year group (hazard ratio 0.79, 95% CI 0.62 to 1.02, p=0.066). The 6-year group had more arthralgia or myalgia, 58% versus 53%, and more osteopenia or osteoporosis, 21% versus 16%.

dawna-1.methods: Double-blind randomised phase 3 trial. Patients with hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer whose disease had progressed after endocrine therapy were randomised 2 to 1 to dalpiciclib plus fulvestrant or placebo plus fulvestrant. The primary endpoint was investigator-assessed progression-free survival. The report is an interim analysis.
dawna-1.results: A total of 361 patients were randomised. Median progression-free survival was 15.7 months (95% CI 11.1 to not reached) with dalpiciclib plus fulvestrant versus 7.2 months (95% CI 5.6 to 9.2) with placebo plus fulvestrant, hazard ratio 0.42 (95% CI 0.31 to 0.58), one-sided p less than 0.0001. Grade 3 or 4 neutropenia occurred in 84.2 percent and leukopenia in 62.1 percent. Serious adverse events occurred in 5.8 percent versus 6.7 percent.

dawna-2.methods: Randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 trial at 42 hospitals in China. Patients with untreated hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer were randomly assigned 2 to 1 to oral dalpiciclib 150 mg daily for 3 weeks of every 4, or matching placebo. Both groups received letrozole 2.5 mg or anastrozole 1 mg daily. Randomisation was stratified by visceral metastasis, previous endocrine therapy and endocrine partner. The primary endpoint was investigator-assessed progression-free survival.
dawna-2.results: 456 patients were randomised, 303 to dalpiciclib and 153 to placebo. At median follow-up of 21.6 months, median progression-free survival was 30.6 months (95% CI 30.6 to not reached) versus 18.2 months (95% CI 16.5 to 22.5), stratified hazard ratio 0.51 (95% CI 0.38 to 0.69), one-sided p less than 0.0001. Grade 3 or 4 adverse events occurred in 90 percent versus 12 percent, most often neutropenia and leukopenia. Two treatment-related deaths occurred with dalpiciclib.

debbrah.methods: Ongoing single-arm, five-cohort phase 2 study in pretreated HER2-positive or HER2-low advanced breast cancer with stable, untreated or progressing brain metastases, or leptomeningeal carcinomatosis. This report covers HER2-positive patients with non-progressing brain metastases after local therapy (cohort 1, 8 patients), asymptomatic untreated brain metastases (cohort 2, 4 patients) and brain metastases progressing after local therapy (cohort 3, 9 patients). Patients received trastuzumab deruxtecan 5.4 mg/kg intravenously every 21 days.
debbrah.results: Twenty-one patients received trastuzumab deruxtecan. The 16-week progression-free survival rate was 87.5 percent (95% CI 47.3 to 99.7) in cohort 1. Intracranial objective response rate was 50.0 percent in cohort 2 and 44.4 percent in cohort 3, and 46.2 percent overall in patients with active brain metastases. Objective response among patients with measurable lesions was 66.7 percent, all partial. Two patients (9.5 percent) had grade 1 interstitial lung disease.

debbrah-cohort-5.methods: Single-arm, open-label, five-cohort phase 2 trial. Cohort 5 enrolled seven patients with HER2-positive or HER2-low advanced breast cancer and pathologically confirmed leptomeningeal disease. They received trastuzumab deruxtecan 5.4 mg/kg intravenously every 21 days until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity. The primary endpoint was overall survival, with progression-free survival and safety as key secondary endpoints.
debbrah-cohort-5.results: At a median follow-up of 12.0 months, median overall survival was 13.3 months (95% CI 5.7 to not available, p less than 0.001) and median progression-free survival was 8.9 months (95% CI 2.1 to not available). Two of seven patients remained on treatment at 18.6 and 11.9 months. None of the five patients who progressed and died had intracranial progression. Prolonged stabilisation for at least 24 weeks occurred in 71.4 percent.

deposein.methods: Randomised open-label phase 3 study. Patients with newly diagnosed leptomeningeal metastasis from breast cancer, defined by tumour cells in the cerebrospinal fluid or by combined clinical and neuroimaging signs, were randomised to systemic therapy alone or systemic therapy plus intrathecal liposomal cytarabine. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival related to leptomeningeal metastasis.
deposein.results: Thirty-seven patients were assigned to control and 36 to the experimental group. The median number of liposomal cytarabine injections was 5. Median leptomeningeal progression-free survival was 2.2 months (95% CI 1.3 to 3.1) versus 3.8 months (95% CI 2.3 to 6.8), hazard ratio 0.61 (95% CI 0.38 to 0.98), p equal to 0.04. Median overall survival was 4.0 versus 7.3 months, hazard ratio 0.85, p equal to 0.51. Serious adverse events occurred in 22 and 30 patients.

destiny-b03.methods: A phase 3, multicenter, open-label, randomized trial compared trastuzumab deruxtecan, a HER2 antibody-drug conjugate, with trastuzumab emtansine. Patients had HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer previously treated with trastuzumab and a taxane. The primary end point was progression-free survival as determined by blinded independent central review. Secondary end points included overall survival, objective response, and safety.
destiny-b03.results: Among 524 randomly assigned patients, 75.8% were alive without disease progression at 12 months with trastuzumab deruxtecan versus 34.1% with trastuzumab emtansine, hazard ratio 0.28. Alive at 12 months were 94.1% versus 85.9%, hazard ratio 0.55. Overall response occurred in 79.7% versus 34.2%. Adjudicated drug-related interstitial lung disease or pneumonitis occurred in 10.5% versus 1.9%. The long-term survival analysis reported median overall survival of 52.6 versus 42.7 months, hazard ratio 0.73.

destiny-b04.methods: A phase 3 trial enrolled patients with HER2-low metastatic breast cancer who had received one or two previous lines of chemotherapy. HER2-low was defined as immunohistochemistry 1+, or 2+ with negative in situ hybridization. Patients were randomly assigned in a 2:1 ratio to trastuzumab deruxtecan or the physician's choice of chemotherapy. The primary end point was progression-free survival in the hormone receptor-positive cohort. Key secondary end points were progression-free survival in all patients and overall survival.
destiny-b04.results: Of 557 patients randomized, 494 (88.7%) had hormone receptor-positive disease. In that cohort median progression-free survival was 10.1 months with trastuzumab deruxtecan and 5.4 months with physician's choice, hazard ratio 0.51. Median overall survival in that cohort was 23.9 versus 17.5 months, hazard ratio 0.64. Among all patients progression-free survival was 9.9 versus 5.1 months, hazard ratio 0.50. Overall survival was 23.4 versus 16.8 months, hazard ratio 0.64.

destiny-b05.methods: A phase 3, open-label, international, randomized trial compared postneoadjuvant trastuzumab deruxtecan at 5.4 mg per kilogram with trastuzumab emtansine at 3.6 mg per kilogram. Patients had HER2-positive breast cancer with residual invasive disease and node-positive disease at surgery, or inoperable disease at diagnosis. The primary end point was invasive disease-free survival. The key secondary end point was disease-free survival. Other end points included overall survival, distant recurrence-free interval, brain metastasis-free interval, and safety.
destiny-b05.results: A total of 1635 patients were randomly assigned, 818 to trastuzumab deruxtecan and 817 to trastuzumab emtansine. Median follow-up was about 30 months. Invasive-disease events or deaths occurred in 51 patients (6.2%) versus 102 patients (12.5%), hazard ratio 0.47. Three-year invasive disease-free survival was 92.4% versus 83.7%. Three-year disease-free survival was 92.3% versus 83.5%. Adjudicated drug-related interstitial lung disease occurred in 9.6% versus 1.6%. Two patients with interstitial lung disease in the trastuzumab deruxtecan group died.

destiny-b06.methods: A phase 3, multicenter, open-label trial enrolled patients with hormone receptor-positive metastatic breast cancer with HER2-low expression (immunohistochemistry 1+ or 2+ with negative in situ hybridization) or HER2-ultralow expression (immunohistochemistry 0 with membrane staining). All had received one or more lines of endocrine-based therapy and no chemotherapy for metastatic disease. Patients were randomly assigned 1:1 to trastuzumab deruxtecan or physician's choice of chemotherapy. The primary end point was progression-free survival in HER2-low disease.
destiny-b06.results: Of 866 patients randomized, 713 had HER2-low disease and 153 had HER2-ultralow disease. Among those with HER2-low disease, median progression-free survival was 13.2 months with trastuzumab deruxtecan and 8.1 months with chemotherapy, hazard ratio 0.62. Results were consistent in the exploratory HER2-ultralow population. Overall survival data were immature. Grade 3 or higher adverse events occurred in 52.8% versus 44.4%. Adjudicated interstitial lung disease or pneumonitis occurred in 49 patients (11.3%) versus 1 patient (0.2%).

destiny-b09.methods: A phase 3 trial enrolled patients with HER2-positive advanced or metastatic breast cancer and no previous chemotherapy or HER2-directed therapy for metastatic disease. Patients were randomly assigned in a 1:1:1 ratio to trastuzumab deruxtecan plus pertuzumab, trastuzumab deruxtecan plus placebo, or a taxane with trastuzumab and pertuzumab. The primary end point was progression-free survival assessed by blinded independent central review. Secondary end points included objective response, duration of response, and safety.
destiny-b09.results: At the February 26, 2025 data cutoff, median progression-free survival was 40.7 months with trastuzumab deruxtecan plus pertuzumab (383 patients) and 26.9 months with taxane, trastuzumab, and pertuzumab (387 patients), hazard ratio 0.56. Confirmed response occurred in 85.1% versus 78.6%, with complete responses in 15.1% and 8.5%. Median duration of response was 39.2 versus 26.4 months. Adjudicated drug-related interstitial lung disease or pneumonitis occurred in 12.1% versus 1.0%.

destiny-b11.methods: This open-label phase III trial ran at 147 sites in 18 countries. Adults with high-risk (at least cT3cN0 or cT0-4cN1-3) HER2-positive early breast cancer were randomised 1:1:1 to trastuzumab deruxtecan for eight cycles, trastuzumab deruxtecan for four cycles followed by paclitaxel, trastuzumab, and pertuzumab for four, or dose-dense doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide followed by the same four cycles. Enrolment in the trastuzumab deruxtecan alone arm closed early. The primary endpoint was pathological complete response.
destiny-b11.results: 286 patients were randomised to trastuzumab deruxtecan, 321 to trastuzumab deruxtecan followed by paclitaxel, trastuzumab, and pertuzumab, and 320 to dose-dense doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide followed by the same. Pathological complete response rates were 43.0%, 67.3%, and 56.3%. The difference between the two combination sequences was 11.2 percentage points (95% CI 4.0 to 18.3, P = 0.003). The event-free survival hazard ratio was 0.56 (95% CI 0.26 to 1.17) at 4.5% maturity.

destiny-b12.methods: The phase 3b/4 study was single-arm and open-label in patients with HER2-positive advanced or metastatic breast cancer, 263 with stable or active brain metastases and 241 without. All had received one or more prior anti-HER2-based regimens and received trastuzumab deruxtecan 5.4 mg per kg. Primary endpoints were progression-free survival in the brain metastases cohort and objective response rate by RECIST version 1.1 in the cohort without. No formal hypothesis testing was conducted.
destiny-b12.results: In the brain metastases cohort, 12-month progression-free survival was 61.6% and 12-month central nervous system progression-free survival was 58.9%. In the cohort without brain metastases, objective response rate was 62.7%. Grade 3 or higher adverse events occurred in 51% of the brain metastases cohort and 49% of the cohort without. Investigator-reported interstitial lung disease or pneumonitis occurred in 16% of patients with brain metastases and 13% of those without.

destiny-breast01.methods: Two-part, open-label, single-group, multicentre phase 2 study in adults with pathologically documented HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer previously treated with trastuzumab emtansine. Part one evaluated three doses to establish a recommended dose, and part two evaluated efficacy and safety at that dose. The primary endpoint was objective response by independent central review.
destiny-breast01.results: 184 patients with a median of six previous treatments received trastuzumab deruxtecan 5.4 mg/kg. Response occurred in 112 patients, 60.9 percent (95% CI 53.4 to 68.0). Median response duration was 14.8 months and median progression-free survival was 16.4 months at 11.1 months of follow-up. Grade 3 or higher events included decreased neutrophil count in 20.7 percent. Adjudicated interstitial lung disease occurred in 13.6 percent, including grade 5 in 2.2 percent.

destiny-breast02.methods: Randomised, open-label, multicentre phase 3 trial at 227 sites. Eligible patients had unresectable or metastatic HER2-positive breast cancer that had progressed after trastuzumab emtansine, with ECOG performance status 0 or 1. Patients were randomly assigned 2 to 1 to trastuzumab deruxtecan 5.4 mg/kg every 3 weeks or treatment of physician's choice, either capecitabine plus trastuzumab or capecitabine plus lapatinib. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival by blinded independent central review.
destiny-breast02.results: 608 patients were randomised, 406 to trastuzumab deruxtecan and 202 to physician's choice. Median progression-free survival was 17.8 months (95% CI 14.3 to 20.8) versus 6.9 months (95% CI 5.5 to 8.4), hazard ratio 0.36 (95% CI 0.28 to 0.45), p less than 0.0001. Grade 3 or higher treatment-emergent adverse events occurred in 53 percent versus 44 percent. Drug-related interstitial lung disease occurred in 10 percent versus less than 1 percent.

e2112.methods: E2112 was a multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase III study. It enrolled men and women with advanced hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer whose disease progressed after a nonsteroidal aromatase inhibitor. Participants were randomly assigned to exemestane 25 mg daily with either entinostat 5 mg weekly or placebo. Primary end points were progression-free survival by central review and overall survival. Secondary end points included safety, objective response rate, and lysine acetylation change in peripheral blood mononuclear cells.
e2112.results: 608 patients were randomly assigned between March 2014 and October 2018. Median progression-free survival was 3.3 months with entinostat versus 3.1 months with placebo, hazard ratio 0.87, P = .30. Median overall survival was 23.4 versus 21.7 months, hazard ratio 0.99, P = .94. Objective response rate was 5.8% versus 5.6%. The most common grade 3 or 4 event with entinostat was neutropenia at 20%.

e5194.methods: The Oncotype DX DCIS Score was measured in patients with ductal carcinoma in situ treated with surgical excision without radiation in the ECOG E5194 study. The score was calculated from seven cancer-related genes and five reference genes. Its association with the risk of an ipsilateral breast event, defined as local recurrence of ductal carcinoma in situ or invasive carcinoma, was analyzed by Cox regression. The prespecified primary analysis adjusted for tamoxifen use.
e5194.results: 327 patients had adequate tissue for analysis. The continuous DCIS Score was significantly associated with the risk of an ipsilateral breast event, hazard ratio 2.31 (95% CI 1.15 to 4.49, P=.02), and with invasive ipsilateral breast event, unadjusted hazard ratio 3.68 (95% CI 1.34 to 9.62, P=.01). For the low, intermediate, and high risk groups, 10-year risks of an ipsilateral breast event were 10.6%, 26.7%, and 25.9%, and of an invasive event 3.7%, 12.3%, and 19.2%.
