ea1131.methods: Patients with clinical stage II or III triple-negative breast cancer and at least 1 cm of residual invasive disease after neoadjuvant chemotherapy were randomly assigned to platinum, carboplatin or cisplatin, once every 3 weeks for four cycles, or capecitabine on 14 of every 21 days for six cycles. Triple-negative subtype, basal or nonbasal, was assigned by PAM50 on the residual disease. The design tested noninferiority with a superiority alternative, assuming 4-year invasive disease-free survival of 67% with capecitabine.
ea1131.results: 410 of a planned 775 participants were randomly assigned between 2015 and 2021. After median follow-up of 20 months and 120 invasive disease-free survival events, representing 61% of full information, in the 308 patients (78%) with basal subtype disease, 3-year invasive disease-free survival was 42% (95% CI 30 to 53) with platinum and 49% (95% CI 39 to 59) with capecitabine. Grade 3 and 4 toxicities were more common with platinum.

ecog-e1199.methods: 4,950 women with axillary lymph node-positive or high-risk lymph node-negative breast cancer were enrolled. All first received four cycles of intravenous doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide at 3-week intervals. They were then assigned to intravenous paclitaxel or docetaxel, given at 3-week intervals for four cycles or at 1-week intervals for 12 cycles. The primary end point was disease-free survival.
ecog-e1199.results: Against standard paclitaxel every 3 weeks, the odds ratio for disease-free survival was 1.27 with weekly paclitaxel (P=0.006), 1.23 with docetaxel every 3 weeks (P=0.02) and 1.09 with weekly docetaxel (P=0.29). Weekly paclitaxel also improved survival, odds ratio 1.32, P=0.01. An exploratory subgroup whose tumours expressed no HER2 protein showed similar gains regardless of hormone receptor expression. Grade 2 to 4 neuropathy was more frequent with weekly paclitaxel, 27% versus 20%.

efect.methods: This was a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter phase III trial in postmenopausal women with hormone receptor-positive advanced breast cancer progressing or recurring after a nonsteroidal aromatase inhibitor. Fulvestrant used a loading-dose regimen of 500 mg intramuscularly on day 0, 250 mg on days 14 and 28, then 250 mg every 28 days. Exemestane was 25 mg orally once daily. The primary end point was time to progression.
efect.results: 693 women were randomly assigned, 351 to fulvestrant and 342 to exemestane. About 60% had received at least two prior endocrine therapies. Median time to progression was 3.7 months in both groups, hazard ratio 0.963 (95% CI 0.819 to 1.133, P=.6531). Overall response rate was 7.4% versus 6.7% (P=.736) and clinical benefit rate 32.2% versus 31.5% (P=.853). Median duration of clinical benefit was 9.3 and 8.3 months.

egf100151.methods: Women with HER2-positive locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer that had progressed after regimens including an anthracycline, a taxane and trastuzumab were randomly assigned to lapatinib 1,250 mg per day continuously plus capecitabine 2,000 mg per square metre on days 1 through 14 of a 21-day cycle, or to capecitabine alone 2,500 mg per square metre on days 1 through 14 of a 21-day cycle. The primary end point was time to progression by blinded independent review.
egf100151.results: The interim analysis of time to progression met the criteria for early reporting on grounds of superiority in the combination arm. The hazard ratio for independently assessed time to progression was 0.49 (95% CI 0.34 to 0.71, P<0.001), with 49 events in the combination arm and 72 in the monotherapy arm. Median time to progression was 8.4 months with the combination and 4.4 months with monotherapy, without more serious toxic effects or symptomatic cardiac events.

egf104900.methods: Patients with HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer whose disease progressed during prior trastuzumab-based therapies were randomly assigned to lapatinib monotherapy or lapatinib in combination with trastuzumab. Overall survival and updated progression-free survival were presented with Kaplan-Meier curves and log-rank tests stratified for hormone receptor status and visceral disease status. Subgroup analyses sought characteristics of patients deriving the greatest clinical benefit.
egf104900.results: Among the 291 patients randomly assigned with strata, lapatinib plus trastuzumab remained superior to lapatinib alone for progression-free survival, hazard ratio 0.74 (95% CI 0.58 to 0.94, P=.011), and gave an overall survival benefit, hazard ratio 0.74 (95% CI 0.57 to 0.97, P=.026). Absolute overall survival rates were 10% higher at 6 months and 15% higher at 12 months with the combination. Performance status 0, nonvisceral disease and fewer than three metastatic sites were associated with better survival.

egf30008.methods: Postmenopausal women with hormone receptor-positive metastatic breast cancer were randomly assigned to daily letrozole 2.5 mg orally plus lapatinib 1,500 mg orally, or letrozole plus placebo, as first-line treatment. The primary end point was progression-free survival in the HER2-positive population. A preplanned Cox regression analysis examined factors in the HER2-negative population.
egf30008.results: In 219 hormone receptor-positive, HER2-positive patients, adding lapatinib reduced the risk of progression, hazard ratio 0.71 (95% CI 0.53 to 0.96, P=.019), with median progression-free survival of 8.2 versus 3.0 months. Clinical benefit was 48% versus 29% (P=.003). The 952 centrally confirmed HER2-negative patients had no progression-free survival improvement. Grade 3 or 4 diarrhea occurred in 10% versus 1% and rash in 1% versus 0%.

ember3.methods: In a phase 3, open-label trial, patients with ER-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer that recurred or progressed during or after aromatase inhibitor therapy, given alone or with a CDK4/6 inhibitor, were assigned in a 1:1:1 ratio to imlunestrant, standard endocrine monotherapy, or imlunestrant with abemaciclib. Primary end points were investigator-assessed progression-free survival for imlunestrant versus standard therapy in patients with ESR1 mutations and in all patients, and for imlunestrant-abemaciclib versus imlunestrant among concurrently randomized patients.
ember3.results: 874 patients underwent randomization, with 331 assigned to imlunestrant, 330 to standard therapy, and 213 to imlunestrant-abemaciclib. Among 256 patients with ESR1 mutations, median progression-free survival was 5.5 months with imlunestrant and 3.8 months with standard therapy, P<0.001. In the overall population median progression-free survival was 5.6 versus 5.5 months, hazard ratio 0.87. Among 426 patients compared concurrently, it was 9.4 months with imlunestrant-abemaciclib versus 5.5 months with imlunestrant, hazard ratio 0.57.

embraca.methods: A randomized, open-label, phase 3 trial assigned patients with advanced breast cancer and a germline BRCA1/2 mutation in a 2:1 ratio to talazoparib 1 mg once daily or standard single-agent therapy of the physician's choice, which was capecitabine, eribulin, gemcitabine, or vinorelbine in continuous 21-day cycles. The primary end point was progression-free survival assessed by blinded independent central review.
embraca.results: Of 431 patients randomized, 287 received talazoparib and 144 standard therapy. Median progression-free survival was 8.6 months with talazoparib versus 5.6 months with standard therapy, hazard ratio 0.54, P<0.001. The interim median hazard ratio for death was 0.76. Objective response rate was 62.6% versus 27.2%. Grade 3-4 hematologic adverse events occurred in 55% versus 38%. The final overall survival analysis reported median overall survival of 19.3 versus 19.5 months, hazard ratio 0.848.

embrace.methods: In this phase 3 open-label study, women with locally recurrent or metastatic breast cancer were randomly allocated 2:1 to eribulin mesilate 1.4 mg/m2 given intravenously on days 1 and 8 of a 21-day cycle or to treatment of physician's choice. Patients had received two to five previous chemotherapy regimens, including an anthracycline and a taxane. Randomisation was stratified by geographical region, previous capecitabine treatment, and HER2 status. The primary endpoint was overall survival in the intention-to-treat population.
embrace.results: 762 women were allocated to treatment, 508 to eribulin and 254 to treatment of physician's choice. Median overall survival was 13.1 months with eribulin versus 10.6 months with physician's choice, hazard ratio 0.81, p=0.041. The most common adverse events in both groups were asthenia or fatigue, in 54% on eribulin and 40% on physician's choice, and neutropenia, in 52% and 30%. Peripheral neuropathy led to discontinuation of eribulin in 24 patients (5%).

emerald.methods: Randomised open-label phase 3 trial. Eligible patients had ER-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer with one or two prior lines of endocrine therapy. Prior treatment with a CDK4/6 inhibitor was required. No more than one line of chemotherapy was allowed. Patients were assigned to elacestrant 400 mg orally once daily or to standard-of-care endocrine monotherapy. Primary endpoints were progression-free survival by blinded independent central review in all patients and in patients with a detectable ESR1 mutation.
emerald.results: 239 patients were assigned to elacestrant and 238 to standard of care. A mutation was detected in 47.8% of patients. 43.4% had received two prior endocrine therapies. The progression-free survival hazard ratio was 0.70 (95% CI 0.55 to 0.88) in all patients and 0.55 (0.39 to 0.77) in mutation-positive patients. Treatment-related grade 3 or 4 adverse events occurred in 7.2% on elacestrant and 3.1% on standard of care. Any-grade nausea occurred in 35.0% versus 18.8%.

emilia.methods: Patients with HER2-positive advanced breast cancer previously treated with trastuzumab and a taxane were randomly assigned to trastuzumab emtansine (T-DM1) or to lapatinib plus capecitabine. Primary endpoints were progression-free survival by independent review, overall survival and safety. Secondary endpoints included investigator-assessed progression-free survival, objective response rate and time to symptom progression. Two interim analyses of overall survival were conducted.
emilia.results: Among 991 randomly assigned patients, median progression-free survival by independent review was 9.6 months with T-DM1 versus 6.4 months with control (hazard ratio 0.65, 95% CI 0.55 to 0.77). Median overall survival at the second interim analysis was 30.9 versus 25.1 months (hazard ratio 0.68, 0.55 to 0.85). The objective response rate was 43.6% versus 30.8%. The 2017 final overall survival analysis reported medians of 29.9 versus 25.9 months (hazard ratio 0.75, 0.64 to 0.88).

eortc-22952-26001.methods: Phase 3 randomised trial. Patients with one to three brain metastases of solid tumours, excluding small-cell lung cancer, with stable systemic disease or asymptomatic primary tumours and WHO performance status 0 to 2 were treated with complete surgery or radiosurgery. They were then randomly assigned to adjuvant whole-brain radiotherapy of 30 Gy in 10 fractions or to observation. The primary endpoint was time to WHO performance status deterioration beyond 2.
eortc-22952-26001.results: Of 359 patients, 199 had radiosurgery and 160 had surgery. Median time to performance status worse than 2 was 10.0 months with observation and 9.5 months with radiotherapy (P = .71). Median overall survival was 10.7 versus 10.9 months (P = .89). Radiotherapy lowered 2-year relapse at initial sites (surgery 59% to 27%; radiosurgery 31% to 19%) and at new sites (42% to 23%; 48% to 33%). Intracranial progression caused death in 44% versus 28%.

eortc22922.methods: Women with a centrally or medially located primary tumour, irrespective of axillary involvement, or an externally located tumour with axillary involvement were randomly assigned to two groups. One group received whole-breast or thoracic-wall irradiation plus internal mammary and medial supraclavicular nodal irradiation. The control group received whole-breast or thoracic-wall irradiation alone. The primary endpoint was overall survival. Secondary endpoints were disease-free survival, survival free from distant disease, and death from breast cancer.
eortc22922.results: Between 1996 and 2004, 4004 patients underwent randomisation. 76.1% had breast-conserving surgery. At a median follow-up of 10.9 years, 811 patients had died. Ten-year overall survival was 82.3% with nodal irradiation versus 80.7% (hazard ratio 0.87, 95% CI 0.76 to 1.00). Disease-free survival was 72.1% versus 69.1% (hazard ratio 0.89). Distant disease-free survival was 78.0% versus 75.0% (hazard ratio 0.86). Breast-cancer mortality was 12.5% versus 14.4% (hazard ratio 0.82).

etna.methods: Multicentre open-label phase 3 trial. Patients with newly diagnosed, centrally confirmed HER2-negative breast cancer were randomly assigned to paclitaxel 90 mg/m2 (349 patients) or nab-paclitaxel 125 mg/m2 (346 patients). Each drug was given on weeks 1, 2 and 3 followed by one week of rest for 4 cycles, before 4 cycles of an anthracycline regimen chosen by the investigator. The primary endpoint was pathological complete response, ypT0/is ypN0.
etna.results: 814 patients were registered and 695 were randomly assigned. Pathological complete response was 22.5% with nab-paclitaxel versus 18.6% with paclitaxel (odds ratio 0.77, 95% CI 0.52 to 1.13, P = .19). Serious adverse events occurred in 54 of 337 patients (16.0%) on nab-paclitaxel and 38 of 335 (11.3%) on paclitaxel. Grade 3 or higher peripheral neuropathy occurred in 4.5% versus 1.8%. Tumour subtype was the strongest factor influencing outcome (odds ratio 4.85).

extenet.methods: Multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 trial at 495 centres. Eligible women had stage 1-3 HER2-positive breast cancer and had completed neoadjuvant and adjuvant trastuzumab up to 2 years before randomisation. Criteria were later amended to stage 2-3 disease completed within 1 year. Patients were randomly assigned 1:1 to oral neratinib 240 mg per day or matching placebo, stratified by hormone receptor status, nodal status and trastuzumab regimen. The primary outcome was invasive disease-free survival at 2 years.
extenet.results: 2840 women were assigned to neratinib (n=1420) or placebo (n=1420). Median follow-up was 24 months. At 2 years there were 70 invasive disease-free survival events with neratinib versus 109 with placebo (stratified hazard ratio 0.67, 95% CI 0.50 to 0.91, p=0.0091). Two-year invasive disease-free survival was 93.9% versus 91.6%. Grade 3 diarrhoea occurred in 40% versus 2%. The 2023 final analysis reported 8-year overall survival of 90.1% versus 90.2% (stratified hazard ratio 0.95, 0.75 to 1.21).

face.methods: Randomised phase 3 trial. Postmenopausal women with hormone receptor-positive, node-positive early breast cancer were assigned to adjuvant letrozole 2.5 mg or anastrozole 1 mg once daily for 5 years or until recurrence of disease. Patients were stratified by number of involved lymph nodes and by HER2 status. The primary endpoint was 5-year disease-free survival, with overall survival and safety as key secondary endpoints.
face.results: 4136 patients were assigned to letrozole (2061) or anastrozole (2075). The final analysis was done at 709 disease-free survival events, 341 (16.5%) with letrozole and 368 (17.7%) with anastrozole. 5-year disease-free survival was 84.9% versus 82.9% (hazard ratio 0.93, 95% CI 0.80 to 1.07, P = .3150), with similar results across subgroups. 5-year overall survival was 89.9% versus 89.2% (hazard ratio 0.98, P = .7916). Grade 3 to 4 arthralgia occurred in 3.9% versus 3.3%.

fact.methods: Open-label randomised phase 3 trial. Postmenopausal women, or premenopausal women receiving a gonadotropin-releasing hormone agonist, with oestrogen receptor or progesterone receptor positive disease at first relapse after primary treatment of localised disease were randomly assigned to a fulvestrant loading dose regimen followed by monthly injection plus anastrozole 1 mg daily, or to anastrozole 1 mg daily alone. The primary endpoint was time to progression.
fact.results: 514 women were assigned to fulvestrant plus anastrozole (258) or anastrozole alone (256). About two thirds had received adjuvant antiestrogens and only eight had received an aromatase inhibitor. Median time to progression was 10.8 versus 10.2 months (hazard ratio 0.99, 95% CI 0.81 to 1.20, P = .91). Median overall survival was 37.8 versus 38.2 months (hazard ratio 1.0, P = 1.00). Hot flashes occurred in 24.6% versus 13.8% (P = .0023).

faktion.methods: Randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 2 trial at 19 UK hospitals. Postmenopausal women aged at least 18 years with ECOG performance status 0 to 2 and oestrogen receptor-positive, HER2-negative metastatic or locally advanced inoperable breast cancer who had relapsed or progressed on an aromatase inhibitor were randomly assigned 1:1 to fulvestrant 500 mg every 28 days plus either capivasertib 400 mg or placebo twice daily on a 4 days on, 3 days off schedule.
faktion.results: 183 patients were screened and 140 were randomly assigned, 69 to capivasertib and 71 to placebo. At the primary analysis 112 progression-free survival events had occurred, 49 (71%) with capivasertib and 63 (89%) with placebo. Median progression-free survival was 10.3 months versus 4.8 months (hazard ratio 0.58, 95% CI 0.39 to 0.84, p = 0.0044). Common grade 3 to 4 events were hypertension (32% versus 24%), diarrhoea (14% versus 4%) and rash (20% versus 0).

falcon.methods: Phase 3 randomised double-blind trial at 113 hospitals and community centres in 20 countries. Eligible patients were postmenopausal, endocrine therapy-naive, with oestrogen receptor-positive or progesterone receptor-positive locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer, WHO performance status 0-2 and at least one measurable or non-measurable lesion. Patients were randomly assigned 1:1 to fulvestrant 500 mg intramuscularly on days 0, 14 and 28 then every 28 days, or anastrozole 1 mg orally daily. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival.
falcon.results: 524 patients were enrolled and 462 were randomised, 230 to fulvestrant and 232 to anastrozole. Progression-free survival favoured fulvestrant (hazard ratio 0.797, 95% CI 0.637 to 0.999, p=0.0486). Median progression-free survival was 16.6 versus 13.8 months. The most common adverse events were arthralgia (17% versus 10%) and hot flushes (11% versus 10%). The 2025 final overall survival analysis reported medians of 44.8 versus 42.7 months (hazard ratio 0.97, 0.77 to 1.21) after 314 deaths.

fast-forward.methods: Multicentre phase 3 randomised non-inferiority trial at 97 UK centres. Patients aged at least 18 years with invasive breast carcinoma (pT1-3, pN0-1, M0) after breast conservation surgery or mastectomy were eligible. Allocation was to 40 Gy in 15 fractions over 3 weeks, 27 Gy in five fractions over 1 week, or 26 Gy in five fractions over 1 week, to the whole breast or chest wall. The primary endpoint was ipsilateral breast tumour relapse.
fast-forward.results: 4096 patients were recruited, 1361 to 40 Gy, 1367 to 27 Gy and 1368 to 26 Gy. At a median follow-up of 71.5 months, 79 primary endpoint events occurred (31, 27 and 21). Hazard ratios versus 40 Gy were 0.86 (95% CI 0.51 to 1.44) for 27 Gy and 0.67 (0.38 to 1.16) for 26 Gy. Five-year relapse incidence after 40 Gy was 2.1%. Moderate or marked clinician-assessed normal tissue effects at 5 years were 9.9%, 15.4% and 11.9%.

fata-gim3.methods: Multicentre, open-label, randomised phase 3 trial of six treatments. Postmenopausal women with completely resected hormone receptor-positive invasive breast cancer, any tumour size and nodal status, and no previous tamoxifen, were assigned in equal ratio to oral anastrozole 1 mg, exemestane 25 mg or letrozole 2.5 mg daily upfront for 5 years, or to tamoxifen 20 mg daily for 2 years followed by one of those aromatase inhibitors for 3 years. The primary endpoint was disease-free survival.
fata-gim3.results: 3697 patients were enrolled. After a median follow-up of 60 months, 401 disease-free survival events occurred, 211 of 1850 on the switch strategy and 190 of 1847 on upfront treatment. 5-year disease-free survival was 88.5% versus 89.8% (hazard ratio 0.89, 95% CI 0.73 to 1.08, p = 0.23). By drug it was 90.0% with anastrozole, 88.0% with exemestane and 89.4% with letrozole (p = 0.24). Grade 3 to 4 musculoskeletal events occurred in 7% of each strategy.

finher.methods: Randomised trial. 1010 women with axillary node-positive or high-risk node-negative breast cancer were assigned to three cycles of docetaxel or vinorelbine, each followed by three cycles of fluorouracil, epirubicin and cyclophosphamide. The 232 women whose tumours had an amplified HER2/neu gene were further assigned to receive or not to receive nine weekly trastuzumab infusions. The primary endpoint was recurrence-free survival.
finher.results: 3-year recurrence-free survival was 91% with docetaxel and 86% with vinorelbine (hazard ratio 0.58, 95% CI 0.40 to 0.85, P = 0.005), with no difference in overall survival (P = 0.15). Among HER2-positive patients, 3-year recurrence-free survival was 89% with trastuzumab and 78% without (hazard ratio 0.42, 95% CI 0.21 to 0.83, P = 0.01). Docetaxel caused more adverse effects. Trastuzumab was not associated with decreased left ventricular ejection fraction or cardiac failure.

first.methods: Phase 2 randomised open-label multicentre study in postmenopausal women with hormone receptor-positive advanced breast cancer receiving first-line endocrine therapy. Patients received fulvestrant 500 mg per month plus 500 mg on day 14 of month 1, or anastrozole 1 mg daily. The primary endpoint was clinical benefit rate, defined as objective response or stable disease for at least 24 weeks. The primary analysis was done 6 months after the last patient was randomly assigned.
first.results: Clinical benefit rate was 72.5% for fulvestrant 500 mg (n=102) and 67.0% for anastrozole (n=103), odds ratio 1.30, 95% CI 0.72 to 2.38, P=.386. Objective response rate was 36.0% versus 35.5%. Median time to progression was not reached with fulvestrant versus 12.5 months with anastrozole, hazard ratio 0.63, 95% CI 0.39 to 1.00, P=.0496. Both treatments were well tolerated with no significant difference in prespecified adverse events.

gap70.methods: Cluster-randomised trial in 40 community oncology practice clusters across the USA. Eligible patients were aged 70 years and older with incurable solid tumours or lymphoma, had at least one impaired geriatric assessment domain, and were starting a new regimen. Clusters were randomly assigned 1:1 to the intervention, in which oncologists received a tailored geriatric assessment summary and management recommendations, or usual care. The primary outcome was the proportion of patients with any grade 3-5 toxic effect over 3 months.
gap70.results: 718 patients were enrolled. Mean age was 77.2 years and 311 of 718 participants (43%) were female. The mean number of impaired geriatric assessment domains was 4.5. Grade 3-5 toxic effects occurred in 177 of 349 patients (51%) in the intervention group versus 263 of 369 (71%) with usual care (relative risk 0.74, 95% CI 0.64 to 0.86, p=0.0001). Falls over 3 months were 12% versus 21% (adjusted relative risk 0.58).

gbg-26-big-03-05.methods: Randomised trial in patients with HER2-positive breast cancer progressing during trastuzumab. Patients were assigned to capecitabine 2,500 mg/m2 on days 1 through 14, given as 1,250 mg/m2 twice daily, alone or with continuation of trastuzumab 6 mg/kg, in 3-week cycles. The primary endpoint was time to progression.
gbg-26-big-03-05.results: 78 patients were assigned to capecitabine and 78 to capecitabine plus trastuzumab. During 15.6 months of follow-up there were 65 events and 38 deaths with capecitabine and 62 events and 33 deaths with capecitabine plus trastuzumab. Median time to progression was 5.6 versus 8.2 months, hazard ratio 0.69, 95% CI 0.48 to 0.97, P=.0338. Overall response rate was 27.0% versus 48.1%, odds ratio 2.50, P=.0115. Toxicity was not increased.

geparnuevo.methods: Randomised phase 2 double-blind placebo-controlled study. Patients with primary cT1b-cT4a-d centrally confirmed triple-negative breast cancer were randomised to durvalumab or placebo every 4 weeks in addition to nab-paclitaxel followed by standard epirubicin and cyclophosphamide. In a window phase, durvalumab or placebo alone was given 2 weeks before the start of nab-paclitaxel. Randomisation was stratified by stromal tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes. The primary objective was pathological complete response (ypT0 ypN0).
geparnuevo.results: 174 patients were randomised and 117 took part in the window phase. Median age was 49.5 years. Pathological complete response was 53.4% with durvalumab versus 44.2% with placebo (P=0.287, odds ratio 1.45). In the window cohort it was 61.0% versus 41.4% (odds ratio 2.22, P=0.035, interaction P=0.048). Thyroid dysfunction of any grade occurred in 47%. The 2022 survival report gave 3-year overall survival of 95.2% versus 83.5% (hazard ratio 0.24, 95% CI 0.08 to 0.72).

geparsepto-gbg-69.methods: Phase 3 randomised trial in patients with previously untreated primary invasive breast cancer, assigned 1:1 with minimisation by subtype, Ki67 and SPARC expression. Patients received nab-paclitaxel 150 mg/m2, later amended to 125 mg/m2, or solvent-based paclitaxel 80 mg/m2 on days 1, 8 and 15 for four 3-week cycles, followed by epirubicin plus cyclophosphamide for four cycles. Patients with HER2-positive tumours also received trastuzumab and pertuzumab. The primary endpoint was pathological complete response.
geparsepto-gbg-69.results: 1229 women were randomly assigned and 1206 started treatment. The nab-paclitaxel dose was reduced to 125 mg/m2 after 464 participants because of discontinuation and neuropathy. Pathological complete response occurred in 233 patients (38%) given nab-paclitaxel versus 174 (29%) given solvent-based paclitaxel, odds ratio 1.53, 95% CI 1.20 to 1.95, p=0.00065. Grade 3-4 sensory neuropathy occurred in 10% versus 3% and grade 3-4 anaemia in 2% versus 1%. Four deaths occurred on treatment.

geparsixto.methods: Randomised phase 2 trial. Patients with previously untreated, non-metastatic, stage II-III triple-negative or HER2-positive breast cancer received 18 weeks of weekly paclitaxel plus non-pegylated liposomal doxorubicin. Triple-negative patients also received bevacizumab. HER2-positive patients also received trastuzumab and lapatinib. Patients were randomly assigned 1:1, stratified by subtype and Ki-67, to weekly carboplatin AUC 1.5 (AUC 2.0 for the first 329 patients) or no carboplatin. The primary endpoint was pathological complete response (ypT0 ypN0).
geparsixto.results: 296 patients were assigned carboplatin and 299 no carboplatin. Pathological complete response was 43.7% (129 patients) versus 36.9% (108 patients), odds ratio 1.33, p=0.107. In triple-negative disease it was 53.2% (84 of 158) versus 36.9% (58 of 157), p=0.005. In HER2-positive disease it was 32.8% (45 of 137) versus 36.8% (50 of 136), p=0.581, interaction p=0.015. Grade 3 or 4 neutropenia occurred in 65% versus 27%.

gim2.methods: Open-label 2x2 factorial phase 3 trial at 81 Italian centres. Patients aged 18-70 years with operable, node-positive, early-stage breast cancer were randomly allocated 1:1:1:1. Allocation was to dose-dense chemotherapy every 2 weeks with pegfilgrastim support or standard-interval chemotherapy every 3 weeks, and to fluorouracil plus epirubicin, cyclophosphamide and paclitaxel (FEC-P) or to EC-P alone. The primary endpoint was disease-free survival in the intention-to-treat population.
gim2.results: 2091 patients were recruited and median follow-up was 7.0 years. For the dose-density comparison, 5-year disease-free survival was 81% with every-2-week treatment versus 76% with every-3-week treatment (hazard ratio 0.77, 95% CI 0.65 to 0.92, p=0.004). Five-year overall survival was 94% versus 89% (hazard ratio 0.65, 0.51 to 0.84, p=0.001). For the chemotherapy-type comparison, 5-year disease-free survival was 78% with FEC-P versus 79% with EC-P (hazard ratio 1.06, p=0.561).

gim4.methods: Multicentre open-label randomised phase 3 trial at 69 Italian hospitals. Eligible women were postmenopausal with stage I to III operable hormone receptor-positive breast cancer, had taken adjuvant tamoxifen for 2 to 3 years with no sign of recurrence, and had ECOG performance status 2 or lower. Patients were assigned 1:1 to letrozole 2.5 mg once daily for 2 to 3 years or for 5 years. The primary endpoint was invasive disease-free survival.
gim4.results: 2056 patients were assigned to letrozole for 2 to 3 years (n=1030) or 5 years (n=1026). After a median follow-up of 11.7 years, disease-free survival events occurred in 262 control patients (25.4%) and 212 extended patients (20.7%). 12-year disease-free survival was 62% versus 67%, hazard ratio 0.78, 95% CI 0.65 to 0.93, p=0.0064. Grade 3 or 4 arthralgia occurred in 2.2% versus 3.0%. No deaths were related to toxic effects.

h0648g.methods: Randomised trial of trastuzumab added to chemotherapy in women with metastatic breast cancer overexpressing HER2. 234 patients were assigned to standard chemotherapy alone and 235 to standard chemotherapy plus trastuzumab. Patients with no prior adjuvant anthracycline received doxorubicin, or epirubicin in 36 women, plus cyclophosphamide, alone in 138 women or with trastuzumab in 143. Patients with prior adjuvant anthracycline received paclitaxel alone in 96 women or paclitaxel with trastuzumab in 92.
h0648g.results: Adding trastuzumab lengthened time to progression (median 7.4 versus 4.6 months, P<0.001), raised objective response (50 versus 32 percent, P<0.001), lengthened response duration (median 9.1 versus 6.1 months, P<0.001), lowered death at 1 year (22 versus 33 percent, P=0.008) and lengthened median survival (25.1 versus 20.3 months, P=0.01). Class III or IV cardiac dysfunction occurred in 27 percent given anthracycline, cyclophosphamide and trastuzumab, 8 percent without trastuzumab, 13 percent given paclitaxel with trastuzumab and 1 percent without.

helen-006.methods: Multicentre randomised phase 3 trial at six hospitals in China. Patients aged 18 to 70 with untreated stage II to III HER2-positive breast cancer were assigned 1:1, stratified by tumour stage, nodal status and hormone receptor status. One group received nab-paclitaxel 125 mg/m2 on days 1, 8 and 15 for six 3-week cycles, the other docetaxel 75 mg/m2 plus carboplatin AUC 6 for six 3-week cycles. Both received concurrent trastuzumab and pertuzumab. The primary endpoint was pathological complete response.
helen-006.results: 689 of 789 screened patients were randomly assigned and 669 started treatment. All were Asian women with a median age of 50 years, and median follow-up was 26 months. Pathological complete response occurred in 220 patients (66.3%, 95% CI 61.2 to 71.4) given nab-paclitaxel versus 194 (57.6%, 52.3 to 62.9) given docetaxel plus carboplatin, odds ratio 1.54, 95% CI 1.10 to 2.14, p=0.011. Grade 3-4 adverse events occurred in 30% versus 38%.

her2climb.methods: Randomised double-blind placebo-controlled trial. Patients with HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer previously treated with trastuzumab, pertuzumab and trastuzumab emtansine, with or without brain metastases, were assigned to tucatinib or placebo in combination with trastuzumab and capecitabine. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival among the first 480 patients randomised. Secondary endpoints in the total population of 612 patients included overall survival, progression-free survival in patients with brain metastases, confirmed objective response rate and safety.
her2climb.results: One-year progression-free survival was 33.1% with tucatinib versus 12.3% with placebo (hazard ratio 0.54, 95% CI 0.42 to 0.71), with medians of 7.8 and 5.6 months. Two-year overall survival was 44.9% versus 26.6% (hazard ratio 0.66, 0.50 to 0.88), with medians of 21.9 and 17.4 months. Among patients with brain metastases, 1-year progression-free survival was 24.9% versus 0% (hazard ratio 0.48, 0.34 to 0.69), with medians of 7.6 and 5.4 months.

her2climb-02.methods: Phase III randomised trial in patients with HER2-positive locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer previously treated with trastuzumab and a taxane in any setting, including patients with brain metastases. Patients were assigned 1:1 to trastuzumab emtansine 3.6 mg/kg intravenously every 21 days with either tucatinib 300 mg orally twice daily or placebo twice daily.
her2climb-02.results: 463 patients were randomly assigned. After a median follow-up of 24.4 months, median progression-free survival was 9.5 months with tucatinib versus 7.4 months with placebo, hazard ratio 0.76, 95% CI 0.61 to 0.95, P=0.0163, with benefit across all prespecified subgroups including patients with brain metastases. Discontinuation for treatment-emergent adverse events was 22.1% versus 11.6% and grade 3 or higher events 68.8% versus 41.2%, most often raised alanine and aspartate aminotransferase.

her2climb-05.methods: Phase III randomised trial in patients with centrally confirmed HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer who had no progression after induction therapy and had no or asymptomatic brain metastases. Patients were assigned 1:1 to tucatinib 300 mg or placebo twice a day combined with trastuzumab and pertuzumab. The primary endpoint was investigator-assessed progression-free survival. Secondary endpoints included overall survival, progression-free survival by blinded independent central review, CNS progression-free survival and safety.
her2climb-05.results: 654 patients were assigned to tucatinib (n=326) or placebo (n=328) between March 2022 and July 2024. Median age was 54 years, 69.3% had de novo metastatic disease, 52.6% were hormone receptor-positive and 12.4% had baseline brain metastases. Median progression-free survival was 24.9 versus 16.3 months, hazard ratio 0.641, 95% CI 0.514 to 0.799, P<.0001, with benefit regardless of brain metastases or hormone receptor status. Diarrhoea affected 72.7% of tucatinib patients.

hera.methods: International multicentre open-label phase 3 randomised trial of 5102 women with HER2-positive early breast cancer, enrolled in 39 countries between December 2001 and June 2005. After completion of all primary therapy, including surgery, chemotherapy and radiotherapy as indicated, patients were randomly assigned 1:1:1 to trastuzumab for 1 year, trastuzumab for 2 years, or observation. The primary endpoint was disease-free survival in the intention-to-treat population. The 2-year versus 1-year comparison used 366-day landmark analyses.
hera.results: 5099 patients were analysed, 1697 in observation, 1702 in the 1-year group and 1700 in the 2-year group. After a median follow-up of 11 years, 1 year of trastuzumab reduced disease-free survival events (hazard ratio 0.76, 95% CI 0.68 to 0.86) and death (0.74, 0.64 to 0.86) versus observation. Two years did not improve disease-free survival over 1 year (hazard ratio 1.02, 0.89 to 1.17). Ten-year disease-free survival was 63%, 69% and 69%. 884 observation patients (52%) crossed over.

ibis2-dcis.methods: Double-blind, multicentre, randomised placebo-controlled trial. Postmenopausal women with locally excised, hormone-receptor-positive DCIS were randomly assigned 1:1 by central computer allocation to 1 mg oral anastrozole or 20 mg oral tamoxifen daily for 5 years. Randomisation was stratified by major centre or hub and done in blocks. Trial personnel, participants and clinicians were masked. The primary endpoint was all recurrence, including recurrent DCIS and new contralateral tumours. Analysis was modified intention to treat.
ibis2-dcis.results: Between March 2003 and February 2012, 2980 postmenopausal women from 236 centres in 14 countries were enrolled, with 1449 analysed on anastrozole and 1489 on tamoxifen. Median follow-up was 7.2 years and 144 breast cancer recurrences were recorded. Overall recurrence was 67 with anastrozole versus 77 with tamoxifen, HR 0.89 (95% CI 0.64-1.23). Deaths numbered 33 versus 36, HR 0.93 (0.58-1.50), p=0.78. Any adverse event was reported by 1323 women (91%) versus 1379 (93%).

ideal.methods: Randomised phase III trial. Postmenopausal patients with hormone receptor-positive breast cancer were randomly allocated to either 2.5 or five years of letrozole after an initial five years of any endocrine therapy. The primary end point was disease-free survival. Secondary end points were overall survival, distant metastasis-free interval, new primary breast cancer, and safety. Hazard ratios were determined by Cox regression analysis. All analyses followed the intention-to-treat principle.
ideal.results: 1824 patients were assigned to 2.5 years (n=909) or five years (n=915) of letrozole, with median follow-up of 6.6 years. A disease-free survival event occurred in 152 patients in the five-year group and 163 in the 2.5-year group, HR 0.92 (95% CI 0.74 to 1.16). Overall survival HR was 1.04 (0.78 to 1.38). Distant metastasis-free interval HR was 1.06 (0.78 to 1.45). Second primary breast cancer was reduced with five years, HR 0.39 (0.19 to 0.81).

ies.methods: 4724 postmenopausal patients with unilateral invasive, oestrogen-receptor-positive or oestrogen-receptor-unknown breast cancer who were disease-free on 2-3 years of tamoxifen were randomly assigned to switch to exemestane (n=2352) or to continue tamoxifen (n=2372) for the remainder of a 5-year endocrine treatment period. The primary endpoint was disease-free survival. Overall survival was a secondary endpoint. Efficacy analyses were intention to treat.
ies.results: After a median follow-up of 55.7 months, 809 disease-free survival events were reported, 354 with exemestane and 455 with tamoxifen. The unadjusted hazard ratio was 0.76 (95% CI 0.66-0.88, p=0.0001) in favour of exemestane, an absolute benefit of 3.3% (1.6-4.9) by the end of treatment. There were 222 deaths with exemestane and 261 with tamoxifen, hazard ratio 0.85 (0.71-1.02, p=0.08), and 0.83 (0.69-1.00, p=0.05) after excluding 122 patients with oestrogen-receptor-negative disease.

impact.methods: Postmenopausal women with ER-positive, invasive, nonmetastatic, operable or locally advanced potentially operable breast cancer were randomly assigned to neoadjuvant tamoxifen 20 mg daily, anastrozole 1 mg daily, or the combination for 3 months. Tumour objective response was assessed by caliper and by ultrasound. Further comparisons covered clinical versus ultrasound response, actual and feasible surgery against feasible surgery at baseline, response in HER2-positive cancers, and tolerability.
impact.results: Objective response did not differ significantly between the three arms in the intention-to-treat population. Among 124 patients judged at baseline to require mastectomy, 44% had breast-conserving surgery after anastrozole versus 31% after tamoxifen (P = .23). Among those their surgeon deemed feasible for breast-conserving surgery the difference reached significance, 46% versus 22% (P = .03). Objective response in 34 HER2-positive cancers was 58% with anastrozole versus 22% with tamoxifen (P = .18). All treatments were well tolerated.

impassion030.methods: Open-label international randomised phase 3 trial in more than 330 centres in 31 countries. Patients undergoing surgery as initial treatment for stage II or III triple-negative breast cancer were enrolled between August 2018 and November 2022. They were randomised 1:1 to standard chemotherapy for 20 weeks with atezolizumab for up to 1 year (n=1101) or without it (n=1098). The primary end point was invasive disease-free survival. The last follow-up was August 2023.
impassion030.results: The independent data monitoring committee halted enrolment at 2199 of 2300 planned patients. All patients stopped atezolizumab after a planned early interim and futility analysis. At the premature final analysis, invasive disease-free survival events had occurred in 141 patients (12.8%) on atezolizumab plus chemotherapy and 125 (11.4%) on chemotherapy alone, with median follow-up 32 months. The stratified hazard ratio was 1.11 (95% CI 0.87-1.42, P=.38). Treatment-related grade 3 or 4 adverse events were 54% versus 44%.

impassion031.methods: Double-blind, randomised, phase 3 study at 75 academic and community sites in 13 countries. Patients with previously untreated stage II-III triple-negative breast cancer were randomly assigned 1:1 to chemotherapy plus intravenous atezolizumab 840 mg or placebo every 2 weeks. Chemotherapy was weekly nab-paclitaxel for 12 weeks followed by doxorubicin plus cyclophosphamide every 2 weeks for 8 weeks, then surgery. Co-primary endpoints were pathological complete response in the all-randomised and PD-L1-positive populations.
impassion031.results: Of 333 eligible patients, 165 were randomly assigned to atezolizumab plus chemotherapy and 168 to placebo plus chemotherapy. Pathological complete response was documented in 95 patients (58%, 95% CI 50-65) versus 69 (41%, 34-49), a rate difference of 17% (6-27). In the PD-L1-positive population it was documented in 53 of 77 (69%) versus 37 of 75 (49%), a difference of 20% (4-35). The final analysis at 3 years reported overall survival hazard ratio 0.56 (0.30-1.04).

impassion050.methods: Patients with a primary tumour larger than 2 cm and histologically confirmed positive nodes (T2-4, N1-3, M0) were randomly assigned 1:1 to atezolizumab or placebo with dose-dense doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide, then paclitaxel, plus pertuzumab and trastuzumab. After surgery patients continued atezolizumab or placebo with pertuzumab and trastuzumab to complete 1 year of HER2-targeted therapy, and those with residual disease could switch to ado-trastuzumab emtansine. Coprimary endpoints were pathologic complete response rates in the intention-to-treat and PD-L1-positive populations.
impassion050.results: At the February 5, 2021 cutoff, pathologic complete response was 62.7% (143 of 228) with placebo and 62.4% (141 of 226) with atezolizumab, a difference of -0.33% (95% CI -9.2 to 8.6, P = .9551). In PD-L1-positive tumours the rates were 72.5% and 64.2%, a difference of -8.26% (95% CI -20.6 to 4.0, P = .1846). Grade 3-4 and serious adverse events were more frequent with atezolizumab, and five grade 5 events occurred, all with atezolizumab.

impassion130.methods: Phase 3 trial. Patients with untreated metastatic triple-negative breast cancer were randomly assigned 1:1 to atezolizumab plus nab-paclitaxel or placebo plus nab-paclitaxel, continued until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity. Stratification was by receipt of neoadjuvant or adjuvant taxane, presence of liver metastases at baseline, and PD-L1 expression at baseline. The two primary end points were progression-free survival in the intention-to-treat population and the PD-L1-positive subgroup, and overall survival tested first in the intention-to-treat population.
impassion130.results: Each group included 451 patients, with median follow-up 12.9 months. In the intention-to-treat analysis median progression-free survival was 7.2 months with atezolizumab plus nab-paclitaxel versus 5.5 months with placebo, hazard ratio 0.80 (95% CI 0.69-0.92, P=0.002). In PD-L1-positive tumours it was 7.5 versus 5.0 months, hazard ratio 0.62 (0.49-0.78). Median overall survival was 21.3 versus 17.6 months, hazard ratio 0.84 (0.69-1.02, P=0.08). The final overall survival analysis reported 21.0 versus 18.7 months, hazard ratio 0.87 (0.75-1.02).

impassion131.methods: Eligible patients had advanced triple-negative breast cancer with no prior systemic therapy for advanced disease or at least 12 months since neoadjuvant or adjuvant chemotherapy. They were randomised 2:1 to atezolizumab 840 mg or placebo on days 1 and 15, both with paclitaxel 90 mg/m2 on days 1, 8 and 15, every 28 days until progression or unacceptable toxicity. Stratification used PD-L1 status, prior taxane, liver metastases and region. The primary endpoint was investigator-assessed progression-free survival.
impassion131.results: Of 651 randomised patients, 45% had PD-L1-positive disease. Adding atezolizumab did not improve investigator-assessed progression-free survival in the PD-L1-positive population, hazard ratio 0.82 (95% CI 0.60 to 1.12, P = 0.20), median 6.0 versus 5.7 months. Unconfirmed best overall response was 63% versus 55% and median duration of response 7.2 versus 5.5 months. Final overall survival showed no difference, hazard ratio 1.11 (95% CI 0.76 to 1.64), median 22.1 versus 28.3 months. Intention-to-treat results were consistent.

import-low.methods: Multicentre, randomised, phase 3, non-inferiority trial at 30 UK radiotherapy centres. Women aged 50 years or older who had breast-conserving surgery for unifocal invasive ductal adenocarcinoma up to 3 cm, with none to three positive axillary nodes and microscopic margins of 2 mm or more, were randomly assigned 1:1:1 to 40 Gy whole-breast radiotherapy, 36 Gy whole breast plus 40 Gy partial breast, or 40 Gy partial breast alone, in 15 fractions. The primary endpoint was ipsilateral local relapse.
import-low.results: Between May 2007 and October 2010, 2018 women were recruited and two withdrew consent. 674 patients were analysed in the whole-breast control group, 673 in the reduced-dose group, and 669 in the partial-breast group. Median follow-up was 72.2 months. Five-year cumulative incidence of local relapse was 1.1% (95% CI 0.5-2.3) in the control group, 0.2% (0.02-1.2) in the reduced-dose group, and 0.5% (0.2-1.4) in the partial-breast group. Non-inferiority was shown for both experimental groups.

inavo120.methods: Phase 3, double-blind, randomised trial. Patients with hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer carrying a mutation in the gene encoding the p110 alpha catalytic subunit of PI3K, who had relapsed during or within 12 months after completing adjuvant endocrine therapy, received first-line inavolisib 9 mg orally once daily plus palbociclib and fulvestrant or placebo plus palbociclib and fulvestrant. The primary end point was investigator-assessed progression-free survival.
inavo120.results: 161 patients were assigned to the inavolisib group and 164 to the placebo group, with median follow-up 21.3 and 21.5 months. Median progression-free survival was 15.0 months (95% CI 11.3 to 20.5) with inavolisib and 7.3 months (5.6 to 9.3) with placebo, hazard ratio 0.43 (0.32 to 0.59, P<0.001). Objective response occurred in 58.4% versus 25.0%. The final overall survival analysis reported median 34.0 versus 27.0 months, hazard ratio 0.67 (0.48 to 0.94, P=0.02).

intrathecal-trastuzumab-bonneau-phase-i.methods: This multicentre phase I dose-escalation study gave intrathecal trastuzumab once weekly for at least 4 weeks at dose levels of 30, 60, 100 and 150 mg to patients with meningeal carcinomatosis from HER2-positive breast cancer. The maximum tolerated dose was defined by achieving an intra-cerebrospinal fluid trastuzumab concentration close to a conventional therapeutic plasma concentration of 30 mg/L and by dose-limiting toxicity. Cerebrospinal fluid was sampled before each injection for pharmacokinetics. Sixteen patients were treated.
intrathecal-trastuzumab-bonneau-phase-i.results: No dose-limiting toxicity was observed. Eleven patients had no toxicity attributed to intrathecal trastuzumab. At 60 mg and above, minor attributed toxicities were headache in 2 patients, nausea in 2, vomiting in 1, cervical pain in 1 and peripheral neuropathy in 1. Two patients had immediate headache or vomiting. Mean residual cerebrospinal fluid trastuzumab concentration at the 150 mg level was 27.9 mg/L. Three patients had a clinical response, seven had stable disease and four had progressive disease.

intrathecal-trastuzumab-kumthekar-phase-.methods: This multicentre combined phase I/II study enrolled 34 patients with HER2-positive leptomeningeal disease to determine the maximum tolerated dose of intrathecal trastuzumab and its efficacy. Any HER2-positive histology was allowed in phase I, while phase II was limited to HER2-positive breast cancer. Cerebrospinal fluid pharmacokinetics were sampled during treatment.
intrathecal-trastuzumab-kumthekar-phase-.results: Intrathecal trastuzumab was well tolerated, with one dose-limiting toxicity of grade 4 arachnoiditis at 80 mg twice weekly, the dose taken forward as the recommended phase II dose. Among 26 patients evaluated at 80 mg, 5 (19.2%) had a partial response, 13 (50.0%) stable disease and 8 (30.8%) progressive disease. Median overall survival was 8.3 months at the phase II dose and 10.5 months in phase II breast cancer patients. Cerebrospinal fluid concentrations stayed stable with repeated dosing.

intrathecal-trastuzumab-oberkampf-phase-.methods: This phase II study gave weekly intrathecal trastuzumab 150 mg, the recommended dose from a preceding phase I dose-escalation study, to patients with HER2-positive breast cancer and leptomeningeal metastasis. The primary endpoint was clinical neurologic progression-free survival related to leptomeningeal disease after 8 weeks. Overall survival, toxicity and quality of life were secondary endpoints. Nineteen patients were enrolled.
intrathecal-trastuzumab-oberkampf-phase-.results: Of the 19 patients enrolled, 16 (84%) had concomitant brain metastases and 15 of these had received prior brain radiotherapy. All had received at least one line of systemic anti-HER2 therapy. At 8 weeks, 14 patients (74%) were free of neurological progression. Median leptomeningeal-related progression-free survival was 5.9 months and median overall survival was 7.9 months. Global health-related quality of life on the QLQ-C30 and BN20 scales appeared preserved, and no toxicity above grade 3 was observed.

ipatunity130-cohort-a.methods: In cohort A of this randomised double-blind placebo-controlled phase III trial, taxane-eligible patients with PIK3CA, AKT1 or PTEN-altered measurable advanced triple-negative breast cancer and no prior chemotherapy for advanced disease were randomised 2:1 to ipatasertib 400 mg on days 1 to 21 or placebo, both with paclitaxel 80 mg/m2 on days 1, 8 and 15, every 28 days until progression or unacceptable toxicity. The primary endpoint was investigator-assessed progression-free survival.
ipatunity130-cohort-a.results: Between February 2018 and April 2020, 255 patients were randomised, 168 to ipatasertib and 87 to placebo. Progression-free survival did not differ, hazard ratio 1.02 (95% CI 0.71 to 1.45), median 7.4 versus 6.1 months. Overall survival did not differ, hazard ratio 1.08 (95% CI 0.73 to 1.58), median 24.4 versus 24.9 months. Ipatasertib caused more grade 3 or higher diarrhoea (9% versus 2%) and more dose reductions (39% versus 14%).

ispy2.methods: Multicenter platform trial of women with operable clinical stage 2 or 3 breast cancer, no prior surgery or systemic therapy, and primary tumours 2.5 cm or larger. Participants were adaptively randomised within molecular subtypes to one of several investigational regimens or control therapy from March 2010 through 2016. Treatment was taxane with or without an investigational agent or combination, followed by doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide. Measures were pathologic complete response and 3-year event-free and distant recurrence-free survival.
ispy2.results: Of 950 participants with median age 49 years, 330 (34.7%) achieved pathologic complete response. Three-year event-free survival and distant recurrence-free survival for those patients were both 95%. Hazard ratios for pathologic complete response versus no pathologic complete response were 0.19 for event-free survival (95% CI 0.12-0.31) and 0.21 for distant recurrence-free survival (0.13-0.34). These were similar across molecular subtypes, ranging from 0.14 to 0.18 for event-free survival and 0.10 to 0.20 for distant recurrence-free survival.

ispy2-pembro.methods: I-SPY2 is an ongoing open-label, multicenter, adaptively randomised phase 2 platform trial in high-risk stage II or III breast cancer, with standard neoadjuvant chemotherapy as the common control arm. Patients with ERBB2-negative breast cancer were eligible for randomisation to pembrolizumab between November 2015 and November 2016. They received taxane- and anthracycline-based neoadjuvant chemotherapy with or without four cycles of pembrolizumab, followed by definitive surgery. The primary end point was pathologic complete response.
ispy2-pembro.results: Of 250 women in the final analysis, 181 were randomised to standard control chemotherapy and 69 to pembrolizumab with weekly paclitaxel followed by doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide, 40 hormone receptor-positive and 29 triple-negative. Pembrolizumab graduated in all three biomarker signatures. Final estimated pathologic complete response rates were 44% versus 17% in ERBB2-negative disease, 30% versus 13% in hormone receptor-positive ERBB2-negative disease, and 60% versus 22% in triple-negative disease. Thyroid abnormalities occurred in 13.0% and adrenal insufficiency in 8.7%.

jlgk0901.methods: This prospective observational study at 23 Japanese facilities enrolled patients with one to ten newly diagnosed brain metastases, largest tumour under 10 mL and 3 cm and total volume at most 15 mL, with Karnofsky performance status 70 or higher. Stereotactic radiosurgery was given without whole-brain radiotherapy, 22 Gy at the periphery for tumours under 4 mL and 20 Gy for those of 4 to 10 mL. The primary endpoint was overall survival, with a non-inferiority margin of 1.30.
jlgk0901.results: Between March 2009 and February 2012, 1194 eligible patients were enrolled. Median overall survival was 13.9 months in 455 patients with one tumour, 10.8 months in 531 with two to four tumours and 10.8 months in 208 with five to ten tumours. Survival did not differ between the two multiple-tumour groups, hazard ratio 0.97 (95% CI 0.81 to 1.18, p = 0.78). Radiosurgery-induced adverse events occurred in 101 patients (8%), and four patients died.

jpbo-abemaciclib-cns-study.methods: Nonrandomised phase II study in four subtype specific cohorts. Cohort A was hormone receptor positive HER2 negative brain metastases, cohort B hormone receptor positive HER2 positive brain metastases, cohort C leptomeningeal metastases, cohort D brain metastases undergoing surgical resection. Abemaciclib 200 mg twice daily was given as monotherapy or with endocrine therapy, or 150 mg twice daily with trastuzumab. Cohorts A and B used a Simon two stage design.
jpbo-abemaciclib-cns-study.results: Cohort A (58 patients) had 3 confirmed responders, an intracranial objective response rate of 5.2 percent and a clinical benefit rate of 24 percent, with median overall survival 12.5 months. Cohort B (27 patients) had no confirmed intracranial responses and a clinical benefit rate of 11 percent, with median overall survival 10.1 months. Cohort C (10 patients) had one complete parenchymal response. In cohort D, unbound brain drug concentrations exceeded the CDK4 and CDK6 targets 96 fold and 19 fold.

kaitlin.methods: Phase III study in adults with excised HER2-positive early breast cancer that was node-positive, or node-negative, hormone receptor-negative with tumour greater than 2.0 cm. After surgery patients were randomly assigned 1:1 to anthracycline-based chemotherapy for three or four cycles followed by 18 cycles of trastuzumab emtansine plus pertuzumab, or by taxane for three or four cycles plus trastuzumab plus pertuzumab. Coprimary end points were invasive disease-free survival in the node-positive and overall intention-to-treat populations.
kaitlin.results: Median follow-up was 57.1 months for taxane plus trastuzumab plus pertuzumab (n=918) and 57.0 months for trastuzumab emtansine plus pertuzumab (n=928). Invasive disease-free survival did not differ in the node-positive population (n=1658, stratified hazard ratio 0.97, 95% CI 0.71 to 1.32) or the overall population (n=1846, stratified hazard ratio 0.98, 0.72 to 1.32). Three-year invasive disease-free survival was 94.2% with the taxane arm and 93.1% with the conjugate arm. Treatment completion was 88.4% versus 65.0%.

kamilla.methods: Ongoing single arm phase IIIb study of trastuzumab emtansine in HER2 positive locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer previously treated with HER2 targeted therapy and chemotherapy. Patients received trastuzumab emtansine 3.6 mg/kg intravenously every 3 weeks until unacceptable toxicity, withdrawal of consent, or progression. This post hoc exploratory analysis assessed tumour response and outcomes in patients with baseline brain metastases, using best overall response rate, clinical benefit rate, progression free survival, overall survival and safety.
kamilla.results: Of 2002 treated patients, 398 had baseline brain metastases. In 126 with measurable brain metastases the best overall response rate was 21.4 percent and the clinical benefit rate 42.9 percent. Lesion diameter sums fell by at least 30 percent in 42.9 percent, and in 49.3 percent of 67 patients without prior brain radiotherapy. Across the 398 patients, median progression free survival was 5.5 months and median overall survival 18.9 months. Nervous system adverse events were commoner with brain metastases.

katherine.methods: Phase 3, open-label trial in patients with HER2-positive early breast cancer who were found to have residual invasive disease in the breast or axilla at surgery after neoadjuvant therapy containing a taxane, with or without anthracycline, and trastuzumab. Patients were randomly assigned to adjuvant trastuzumab emtansine or trastuzumab for 14 cycles. The primary end point was invasive disease-free survival.
katherine.results: At the interim analysis of 1486 randomly assigned patients, 743 per group, invasive disease or death had occurred in 91 patients (12.2%) on trastuzumab emtansine and 165 (22.2%) on trastuzumab. Freedom from invasive disease at 3 years was 88.3% versus 77.0%, hazard ratio 0.50 (95% CI 0.39 to 0.64, P<0.001). The survival update at 8.4 years median follow-up reported 7-year overall survival of 89.1% versus 84.4%, hazard ratio 0.66 (0.51 to 0.87, P=0.003).

keynote119.methods: Randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial at 150 centres in 31 countries. Patients aged 18 years or older with centrally confirmed metastatic triple-negative breast cancer, ECOG status 0 or 1, one or two previous systemic treatments for metastatic disease, and prior anthracycline or taxane were assigned 1:1 to pembrolizumab 200 mg every 3 weeks for 35 cycles or investigator's choice of capecitabine, eribulin, gemcitabine, or vinorelbine. Primary endpoints were overall survival by PD-L1 combined positive score and in all participants.
keynote119.results: 622 of 1098 assessed patients were randomly assigned, 312 to pembrolizumab and 310 to chemotherapy. Median follow-up was about 31.4 months. Median overall survival with CPS 10 or more was 12.7 versus 11.6 months (HR 0.78, 95% CI 0.57 to 1.06; p=0.057). With CPS 1 or more it was 10.7 versus 10.2 months (HR 0.86, 0.69 to 1.06; p=0.073). Overall it was 9.9 versus 10.8 months (HR 0.97, 0.82 to 1.15).

keynote355.methods: Patients with previously untreated locally recurrent inoperable or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer were randomly assigned 2:1 to pembrolizumab 200 mg every 3 weeks plus investigator's choice of chemotherapy (nab-paclitaxel, paclitaxel, or gemcitabine-carboplatin) or to placebo plus chemotherapy. The primary endpoints were progression-free survival, reported previously, and overall survival among patients with a PD-L1 combined positive score of 10 or more, those with a score of 1 or more, and the intention-to-treat population. Safety was also assessed.
keynote355.results: 847 patients were randomised, 566 to pembrolizumab-chemotherapy and 281 to placebo-chemotherapy. Median follow-up was 44.1 months. In the CPS-10 subgroup median overall survival was 23.0 versus 16.1 months (HR 0.73, 95% CI 0.55 to 0.95; P=0.0185). In the CPS-1 subgroup it was 17.6 versus 16.0 months (HR 0.86, 0.72 to 1.04; P=0.1125). In the intention-to-treat population it was 17.2 versus 15.5 months (HR 0.89, 0.76 to 1.05).

keynote522.methods: Phase 3 trial. Patients with previously untreated stage II or III triple-negative breast cancer were randomly assigned 2:1 to four cycles of pembrolizumab 200 mg every 3 weeks plus paclitaxel and carboplatin (784 patients) or placebo plus the same chemotherapy (390 patients), then four further cycles with doxorubicin-cyclophosphamide or epirubicin-cyclophosphamide. After definitive surgery patients received adjuvant pembrolizumab or placebo for up to nine cycles. Primary endpoints were pathological complete response and event-free survival.
keynote522.results: Among the first 602 randomised patients, pathological complete response was 64.8% with pembrolizumab-chemotherapy and 51.2% with placebo-chemotherapy, a difference of 13.6 percentage points (95% CI 5.4 to 21.8; P<0.001). After median follow-up of 15.5 months, 58 of 784 patients (7.4%) versus 46 of 390 (11.8%) had progression precluding surgery, recurrence, second primary, or death (HR 0.63, 0.43 to 0.93). The 2024 overall survival report gave 60-month overall survival of 86.6% versus 81.7% (P=0.002).

keynote756.methods: In this double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 study, patients with untreated ER-positive, HER2-negative grade 3 high-risk invasive breast cancer (T1c-2 at least 2 cm cN1-2, or T3-4 cN0-2) were assigned 1:1 to neoadjuvant pembrolizumab 200 mg or placebo every 3 weeks with weekly paclitaxel for 12 weeks, then four cycles of doxorubicin or epirubicin with cyclophosphamide. After surgery they received adjuvant pembrolizumab or placebo for nine cycles with endocrine therapy. Dual primary endpoints were pathological complete response and event-free survival.
keynote756.results: 635 patients were assigned to pembrolizumab-chemotherapy and 643 to placebo-chemotherapy. At the prespecified first interim analysis the pathological complete response rate was 24.3% (95% CI 21.0 to 27.8) versus 15.6% (95% CI 12.8 to 18.6), a treatment difference of 8.5 percentage points (95% CI 4.2 to 12.8; P=0.00005). Event-free survival was not mature. During the neoadjuvant phase, grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events occurred in 52.5% and 46.4% of patients.

kristine.methods: Randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial at 68 centres in Asia, Europe, the USA, and Canada. Patients aged 18 years or older with centrally confirmed HER2-positive stage II-III operable breast cancer larger than 2 cm, ECOG status 0-1, and left ventricular ejection fraction of at least 55% were assigned 1:1 to six neoadjuvant 3-weekly cycles of trastuzumab emtansine plus pertuzumab or of docetaxel, carboplatin, and trastuzumab plus pertuzumab. The primary endpoint was pathological complete response (ypT0/is ypN0).
kristine.results: 444 patients were randomly assigned, 223 to trastuzumab emtansine plus pertuzumab and 221 to docetaxel, carboplatin, and trastuzumab plus pertuzumab. Pathological complete response occurred in 99 patients (44.4%) versus 123 (55.7%), a difference of -11.3 percentage points (95% CI -20.5 to -2.0; p=0.016). Grade 3-4 adverse events occurred in 29 of 223 (13%) versus 141 of 219 (64%). The 3-year report found a higher event-free survival event risk with trastuzumab emtansine plus pertuzumab (HR 2.61, 1.36 to 4.98).

landscape.methods: Single arm, open label, multicentre phase 2 study. Eligible patients had HER2 positive metastatic breast cancer with brain metastases not previously treated with whole brain radiotherapy, capecitabine or lapatinib. Treatment was given in 21 day cycles of lapatinib 1250 mg orally daily and capecitabine 2000 mg/m2 orally on days 1 to 14. The primary endpoint was the proportion of patients with a confirmed objective central nervous system response. Efficacy analyses included all patients who received study drugs and were assessable.
landscape.results: 45 patients were enrolled between April 2009 and August 2010, and 44 were assessable, with median follow up 21.2 months. 29 patients had an objective central nervous system response, 65.9 percent (95% CI 50.1 to 79.5), all partial. Grade 3 or 4 treatment related adverse events occurred in 22 of 45 patients, most often diarrhoea and hand foot syndrome, each in 9. 14 patients had a severe adverse event and 4 stopped for toxicity. No toxic deaths occurred.

lord.methods: Randomised international multicentre open-label phase III non-inferiority trial led by the Dutch Breast Cancer Research Group and the EORTC. It compares standard treatment with active surveillance in 1240 women aged 45 years or older with asymptomatic, screen-detected, pure low-grade ductal carcinoma in situ diagnosed on vacuum-assisted biopsy of microcalcifications. Both arms are monitored with annual digital mammography for 10 years. The primary endpoint is the 10-year ipsilateral invasive breast cancer free percentage.

loris.methods: Phase III trial of surgery versus active monitoring in women with screen-detected or asymptomatic low grade ductal carcinoma in situ, or intermediate grade disease with low grade features. It is designed to determine whether such women can be managed by active monitoring rather than by surgical treatment.

lotus.methods: Randomised, placebo controlled, double blind phase 2 trial at 44 hospitals in eight countries. Women aged 18 or older with measurable inoperable locally advanced or metastatic triple negative breast cancer untreated with systemic therapy were assigned 1:1 to intravenous paclitaxel 80 mg/m2 on days 1, 8 and 15 with either ipatasertib 400 mg or placebo daily on days 1 to 21 every 28 days, until progression or unacceptable toxicity. Stratification used prior therapy, chemotherapy free interval and PTEN status.
lotus.results: 124 patients were enrolled between September 2014 and February 2016, 62 to ipatasertib and 62 to placebo. Median follow up was 10.4 and 10.2 months. Median progression free survival was 6.2 versus 4.9 months, stratified hazard ratio 0.60 (p=0.037), and in 48 PTEN low patients 6.2 versus 3.7 months, hazard ratio 0.59 (p=0.18). Grade 3 or worse diarrhoea occurred in 14 of 61 ipatasertib patients and none on placebo. Serious adverse events occurred in 17 versus 9 patients.

lumina.methods: Prospective single-group cohort study. Women at least 55 years of age who had undergone breast-conserving surgery for T1N0, grade 1 or 2, luminal A breast cancer (estrogen receptor at least 1%, progesterone receptor above 20%, HER2-negative, Ki67 index 13.25% or less) and who received adjuvant endocrine therapy were enrolled after central Ki67 testing and did not receive radiotherapy. The primary outcome was local recurrence in the ipsilateral breast, with an acceptable 5-year cumulative incidence below 5%.
lumina.results: Of 740 registered patients, 500 eligible patients were enrolled. At 5 years after enrollment, local recurrence was reported in 2.3% of patients (90% CI 1.3 to 3.8; 95% CI 1.2 to 4.1), which met the prespecified boundary. Breast cancer occurred in the contralateral breast in 1.9% of patients (90% CI 1.1 to 3.2). Recurrence of any type was observed in 2.7% (90% CI 1.6 to 4.1).

m77001.methods: Randomised multicentre trial comparing first line trastuzumab plus docetaxel with docetaxel alone in patients with HER2 positive metastatic breast cancer. Patients were randomly assigned to six cycles of docetaxel 100 mg/m2 every 3 weeks, with or without trastuzumab given as a 4 mg/kg loading dose followed by 2 mg/kg weekly until disease progression.
m77001.results: 186 patients received at least one dose. Trastuzumab plus docetaxel was superior for overall response rate, 61 percent versus 34 percent (p=0.0002), median overall survival, 31.2 versus 22.7 months (p=0.0325), median time to progression, 11.7 versus 6.1 months (p=0.0001), median time to treatment failure, 9.8 versus 5.3 months (p=0.0001), and median duration of response, 11.7 versus 5.7 months (p=0.009). Grade 3 to 4 neutropenia occurred in 32 percent versus 22 percent and febrile neutropenia in 23 percent versus 17 percent.

ma-27.methods: Open label randomised phase III trial of 5 years of exemestane versus 5 years of anastrozole in postmenopausal women with hormone dependent early breast cancer. The two sided superiority design was powered to detect a 2.4 percent improvement with exemestane in 5 year event free survival. Secondary objectives were overall survival, distant disease free survival, incidence of contralateral new primary breast cancer, and safety.
ma-27.results: 7576 women with a median age of 64.1 years were enrolled. At median follow up 4.1 years, 4 year event free survival was 91 percent with exemestane and 91.2 percent with anastrozole, stratified hazard ratio 1.02 (95% CI 0.87 to 1.18, p=0.85). Distant disease free survival and disease specific survival were also similar. 31.6 percent of patients discontinued treatment for adverse effects, concomitant disease or refusal. Osteoporosis or osteopenia, hypertriglyceridaemia, vaginal bleeding and hypercholesterolaemia were less frequent with exemestane.

ma17.methods: Double-blind, placebo-controlled trial testing five years of letrozole in postmenopausal women with breast cancer who had completed five years of tamoxifen therapy. The primary endpoint was disease-free survival.
ma17.results: 5187 women were enrolled, with median follow-up of 2.4 years. At the first interim analysis there were 207 local or metastatic recurrences or new contralateral primary cancers, 75 in the letrozole group and 132 in the placebo group. Estimated four-year disease-free survival was 93% versus 87% (P<=0.001). 31 women taking letrozole and 42 taking placebo died (P=0.25). New osteoporosis was diagnosed in 5.8% versus 4.5% (P=0.07), with similar fracture rates.

ma17r.methods: Double-blind, placebo-controlled trial assessing extended use of letrozole for an additional 5 years after 5 years of aromatase-inhibitor therapy given up front or after tamoxifen. The primary endpoint was disease-free survival.
ma17r.results: 1918 women were enrolled. After median follow-up of 6.3 years there were 165 events of disease recurrence or contralateral breast cancer, 67 with letrozole and 98 with placebo, and 200 deaths, 100 in each group. Five-year disease-free survival was 95% versus 91% (HR 0.66; P=0.01). Five-year overall survival was 93% versus 94% (HR 0.97; P=0.83). Annual contralateral breast cancer incidence was 0.21% versus 0.49% (HR 0.42; P=0.007).

ma20.methods: Randomised trial in women with node-positive or high-risk node-negative breast cancer treated with breast-conserving surgery and adjuvant systemic therapy. Women were assigned to whole-breast irradiation plus regional nodal irradiation covering the internal mammary, supraclavicular, and axillary nodes, or to whole-breast irradiation alone. The primary outcome was overall survival. Secondary outcomes were disease-free survival, isolated locoregional disease-free survival, and distant disease-free survival.
ma20.results: 1832 women were assigned between March 2000 and February 2007, 916 to each group. Median follow-up was 9.5 years. At 10 years, overall survival was 82.8% with nodal irradiation and 81.8% with control (HR 0.91, 95% CI 0.72 to 1.13; P=0.38). Disease-free survival was 82.0% versus 77.0% (HR 0.76, 0.61 to 0.94; P=0.01). Grade 2 or greater acute pneumonitis occurred in 1.2% versus 0.2% (P=0.01) and lymphedema in 8.4% versus 4.5% (P=0.001).

ma32.methods: Phase 3 randomised, placebo-controlled, double-blind trial in Canada, Switzerland, the USA, and the UK. 3649 patients with high-risk nonmetastatic breast cancer receiving standard therapy were enrolled between August 2010 and March 2013 and randomised to oral metformin 850 mg twice a day (n=1824) or placebo twice a day (n=1825) for 5 years, stratified by hormone receptor status, body mass index, HER2 status, and any chemotherapy. The primary outcome was invasive disease-free survival in hormone receptor-positive disease.
ma32.results: Mean age was 52.4 years and 3643 patients (99.8%) were women. Futility was declared for ER/PgR-negative patients, so the primary analysis covered 2533 ER/PgR-positive patients followed for a median of 96.2 months. 465 of them had invasive disease-free survival events, at 2.78 versus 2.74 per 100 patient-years (HR 1.01, 95% CI 0.84 to 1.21; P=.93). Death rates were 1.46 versus 1.32 per 100 patient-years (HR 1.10, 0.86 to 1.41; P=.47).

mahajan-postoperative-srs-trial.methods: Randomised controlled phase 3 trial at a single tertiary cancer centre in the USA. Eligible patients were older than 3 years, had a Karnofsky Performance Score of 70 or higher, could have an MRI, and had complete resection of one to three brain metastases with a cavity of 4 cm or less. Patients were assigned 1:1 to stereotactic radiosurgery of the cavity within 30 days of surgery or to observation, stratified by primary tumour histology, metastasis size and number.
mahajan-postoperative-srs-trial.results: 132 patients were randomly assigned between August 2009 and February 2016, 68 to observation and 64 to stereotactic radiosurgery, with 128 analysed after four were found ineligible. Median follow up was 11.1 months. Freedom from local recurrence at 12 months was 43 percent in the observation group and 72 percent in the radiosurgery group, hazard ratio 0.46 (95% CI 0.24 to 0.88, p=0.015). There were no adverse events or treatment related deaths in either group.

maintain.methods: Investigator-initiated, phase 2, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial. Patients with hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer whose disease progressed during endocrine therapy and a CDK4/6 inhibitor switched endocrine therapy to fulvestrant or exemestane and were randomly assigned 1:1 to ribociclib or placebo. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival, measured from random assignment to disease progression or death. The planned sample was 120 patients, with 80% power to detect a hazard ratio of 0.58.
maintain.results: Of the 119 randomly assigned participants, 103 (86.5%) had previously received palbociclib and 14 (11.7%) had received ribociclib. Median progression-free survival was 5.29 months (95% CI 3.02 to 8.12) with switched endocrine therapy plus ribociclib versus 2.76 months (95% CI 2.66 to 3.25) with placebo (HR 0.57, 95% CI 0.39 to 0.85; P=.006). Progression-free survival rates with ribociclib were 41.2% at 6 months and 24.6% at 12 months, versus 23.9% and 7.4% with placebo.

marianne.methods: Patients with centrally assessed HER2-positive advanced breast cancer and no prior therapy for advanced disease were randomly assigned 1:1:1 to control trastuzumab plus taxane, to T-DM1 plus placebo, or to T-DM1 plus pertuzumab, all at standard doses. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival by independent review.
marianne.results: Median progression-free survival was 13.7 months with trastuzumab plus taxane, 14.1 months with T-DM1, and 15.2 months with T-DM1 plus pertuzumab. Response rates were 67.9%, 59.7%, and 64.2%. Median response duration was 12.5, 20.7, and 21.2 months. Grade 3 or higher adverse events occurred in 54.1%, 45.4%, and 46.2% of patients.

masai.methods: Randomised, controlled, population-based, single-blinded, non-inferiority screening accuracy study at four Swedish sites. Women aged 40-80 years eligible for mammography screening were randomly allocated 1:1 to AI-supported screening or standard double reading without AI. The AI system scored malignancy risk on a 10-level scale, triaging examinations to single reading (score 1-9) or double reading (score 10). This prespecified clinical safety analysis assessed early screening performance and screen-reading workload in the modified intention-to-treat population.
masai.results: 80 033 women were randomised between April 2021 and July 2022, 40 003 to AI-supported screening and 40 030 to double reading, and 13 were excluded. AI-supported screening gave 244 screen-detected cancers, 861 recalls, and 46 345 screen readings. Standard screening gave 203 cancers, 817 recalls, and 83 231 readings. Cancer detection rates were 6.1 versus 5.1 per 1000 screened (ratio 1.2, 95% CI 1.0 to 1.5; p=0.052). Screen-reading workload fell by 44.3%.

mindact.methods: Randomised phase 3 study. 6693 women with early-stage breast cancer had genomic risk determined with the 70-gene signature and clinical risk with a modified Adjuvant! Online. Women at low clinical and low genomic risk received no chemotherapy. Women at high clinical and high genomic risk received chemotherapy. Patients with discordant results were assigned by either the genomic or the clinical risk. The primary goal tested 5-year survival without distant metastasis against a 92% non-inferiority boundary.
mindact.results: 1550 patients (23.2%) were at high clinical risk and low genomic risk. Among those not given chemotherapy, the 5-year rate of survival without distant metastasis was 94.7% (95% CI 92.5 to 96.2). The absolute difference against patients who received chemotherapy was 1.5 percentage points, lower without chemotherapy. Similar rates were reported in the ER-positive, HER2-negative subgroup. The 2021 updated analysis reported 8-year distant metastasis-free survival of 92.0% with chemotherapy and 89.4% without (hazard ratio 0.66).

monaleesa2.methods: Randomised, placebo-controlled phase 3 trial in 668 postmenopausal women with HR-positive, HER2-negative recurrent or metastatic breast cancer and no previous systemic therapy for advanced disease. Patients received ribociclib 600 mg per day on a 3-weeks-on, 1-week-off schedule plus letrozole 2.5 mg per day, or placebo plus letrozole. The primary end point was investigator-assessed progression-free survival. Secondary end points included overall survival, overall response rate and safety. A preplanned interim analysis followed 243 progression events or deaths.
monaleesa2.results: Progression-free survival was longer with ribociclib (hazard ratio 0.56; 95% CI 0.43 to 0.72). Median follow-up was 15.3 months. At 18 months the progression-free survival rate was 63.0% with ribociclib and 42.2% with placebo. Among patients with measurable disease the overall response rate was 52.7% versus 37.1%. Grade 3 or 4 neutropenia occurred in 59.3% versus 0.9%. The 2022 final overall survival analysis reported median overall survival of 63.9 versus 51.4 months (hazard ratio 0.76).

monaleesa3.methods: Phase 3 trial in postmenopausal women with HR-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer who were treatment naive or had received up to one line of prior endocrine therapy in the advanced setting. Patients were randomly assigned two to one to ribociclib plus fulvestrant (484 patients) or placebo plus fulvestrant (242 patients). The primary end point was locally assessed progression-free survival. Secondary end points included overall survival, overall response rate and safety.
monaleesa3.results: Median progression-free survival was 20.5 months with ribociclib plus fulvestrant and 12.8 months with placebo plus fulvestrant (hazard ratio 0.593; 95% CI 0.480 to 0.732). The effect held in treatment-naive patients (0.577) and after one prior line (0.565). Overall response rate with measurable disease was 40.9% versus 28.7%.
