Grade 3 neutropenia occurred in 46.6% versus 0%. The 2021 updated survival report gave median overall survival of 53.7 versus 41.5 months (hazard ratio 0.73).

monaleesa7.methods: Phase 3, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial at 188 centres in 30 countries. Eligible patients were premenopausal women aged 18 to 59 with HR-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer, ECOG performance status 0 or 1, and no prior CDK4/6 inhibitor. Up to one line of chemotherapy for advanced disease was allowed. Patients were assigned one to one to ribociclib 600 mg or placebo, each with tamoxifen or a non-steroidal aromatase inhibitor plus goserelin. The primary endpoint was investigator-assessed progression-free survival.
monaleesa7.results: 672 patients were randomly assigned, 335 to ribociclib and 337 to placebo. Median investigator-assessed progression-free survival was 23.8 months (95% CI 19.2 to not reached) with ribociclib and 13.0 months (95% CI 11.0 to 16.4) with placebo (hazard ratio 0.55; 95% CI 0.44 to 0.69). Grade 3 or 4 neutropenia occurred in 61% versus 4%. The 2022 updated survival analysis reported median overall survival of 58.7 versus 48.0 months (hazard ratio 0.76).

monarch2.methods: Global, double-blind phase 3 study of women with HR-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer that had progressed on neoadjuvant or adjuvant endocrine therapy, within 12 months of the end of adjuvant endocrine therapy, or on first-line endocrine therapy for metastatic disease. Patients were assigned two to one to abemaciclib or placebo 150 mg twice daily on a continuous schedule, each with fulvestrant 500 mg. The primary end point was investigator-assessed progression-free survival.
monarch2.results: 669 patients were assigned, 446 to abemaciclib plus fulvestrant and 223 to placebo plus fulvestrant. Median progression-free survival was 16.4 versus 9.3 months (hazard ratio 0.553; 95% CI 0.449 to 0.681). Among patients with measurable disease the objective response rate was 48.1% versus 21.3%. Diarrhea occurred in 86.4% versus 24.7% and neutropenia in 46.0% versus 4.0%. The 2020 interim survival analysis reported median overall survival of 46.7 versus 37.3 months (hazard ratio 0.757).

monarch3.methods: Double-blind randomised phase 3 study of abemaciclib or placebo 150 mg twice daily on a continuous schedule plus a non-steroidal aromatase inhibitor, anastrozole 1 mg or letrozole 2.5 mg daily, in 493 postmenopausal women with HR-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer and no prior systemic therapy in the advanced setting. The primary objective was investigator-assessed progression-free survival. A planned interim analysis occurred after 189 events.
monarch3.results: Progression-free survival was prolonged with abemaciclib (hazard ratio 0.54; 95% CI 0.41 to 0.72). The median was not reached with abemaciclib and was 14.7 months with placebo. Among patients with measurable disease the objective response rate was 59% versus 44%. Diarrhea affected 81.3% of the abemaciclib arm. The 2019 final progression-free survival report and the 2024 final overall survival report gave medians of 28.18 versus 14.76 months (hazard ratio 0.540) and 66.8 versus 53.7 months (hazard ratio 0.804).

monarche.methods: Open-label phase 3 study in patients with HR-positive, HER2-negative, high-risk early breast cancer treated with surgery and, as indicated, radiotherapy and chemotherapy. Eligible patients had four or more positive nodes, or one to three nodes with tumour 5 cm or larger, grade 3 histology, or central Ki-67 of 20% or more. Assignment was 1:1 to standard adjuvant endocrine therapy with or without abemaciclib 150 mg twice daily for two years. The primary end point was invasive disease-free survival.
monarche.results: At a preplanned interim analysis of 5637 randomly assigned patients, 323 invasive disease-free survival events had occurred in the intention-to-treat population. Abemaciclib plus endocrine therapy was superior to endocrine therapy alone (hazard ratio 0.75; 95% CI 0.60 to 0.93), with 2-year invasive disease-free survival rates of 92.2% versus 88.7%. The 2025 overall survival report gave 7-year overall survival of 86.8% versus 85.0% (hazard ratio 0.842, P = 0.027).

monarcher.methods: Open-label three-group trial at 75 centres in 14 countries. Women aged 18 or older with hormone receptor-positive, HER2-positive unresectable, locally advanced, recurrent or metastatic disease, performance status 0 or 1, and at least two prior HER2-targeted therapies for advanced disease were randomised 1:1:1 to abemaciclib plus trastuzumab plus fulvestrant, abemaciclib plus trastuzumab, or physician's choice chemotherapy plus trastuzumab.
monarcher.results: Of 325 patients screened, 237 were randomised, 79 per group. Median follow-up was 19.0 months. Median progression-free survival was 8.3 months in group A versus 5.7 months in group C, hazard ratio 0.67, p=0.051. Group B was 5.7 months, hazard ratio 0.94, p=0.77. The commonest grade 3 or 4 event was neutropenia in 27%, 22%, and 26%. Two deaths were treatment related.

nala.methods: Randomised, active-controlled phase 3 trial in patients with centrally confirmed HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer who had received two or more previous HER2-directed regimens. Patients with stable asymptomatic CNS disease were eligible. Assignment was one to one to neratinib 240 mg daily plus capecitabine 750 mg/m2 twice daily on 14 of 21 days with loperamide prophylaxis, or to lapatinib 1250 mg daily plus capecitabine 1000 mg/m2 twice daily. Coprimary end points were centrally confirmed progression-free survival and overall survival.
nala.results: 621 patients from 28 countries were assigned, 307 to neratinib plus capecitabine and 314 to lapatinib plus capecitabine. Centrally reviewed progression-free survival favoured neratinib (hazard ratio 0.76; 95% CI 0.63 to 0.93). The overall survival hazard ratio was 0.88 (95% CI 0.72 to 1.07). Cumulative incidence of intervention for CNS disease was 22.8% versus 29.2%. Objective response rates were 32.8% versus 26.7%. Median duration of response was 8.5 versus 5.6 months. Diarrhea occurred in 83% versus 66%.

natalee.methods: Phase 3 trial in women and men with HR-positive, HER2-negative early breast cancer of anatomical stage IIA (N0 with risk factors, or N1), IIB or III. Patients were randomised 1:1 to ribociclib 400 mg per day, three weeks on and one week off for 36 months, plus a non-steroidal aromatase inhibitor for 60 months (2549), or the aromatase inhibitor alone (2552). Premenopausal women and men also received goserelin. The primary endpoint was invasive disease-free survival.
natalee.results: At the 21 July 2023 cut-off, ribociclib had been stopped in 1996 patients (78.3%) and 1091 (42.8%) had completed three years. Median follow-up for invasive disease-free survival was 33.3 months. There were 226 events with ribociclib plus the aromatase inhibitor and 283 with the inhibitor alone (hazard ratio 0.749; 95% CI 0.628 to 0.892; P = 0.0012). Three-year invasive disease-free survival was 90.7% versus 87.6%. Overall survival data were immature.

ncctg-n0574.methods: Patients with one to three brain metastases at 34 North American institutions were randomised between February 2002 and December 2013 to radiosurgery alone or radiosurgery plus whole brain radiotherapy. Whole brain radiotherapy was 30 Gy in 12 fractions. Radiosurgery was 18 to 22 Gy in the combined group and 20 to 24 Gy alone. The primary endpoint was cognitive deterioration at 3 months.
ncctg-n0574.results: Of 213 patients randomised, 111 received radiosurgery alone and 102 radiosurgery plus whole brain radiotherapy. Cognitive deterioration at 3 months was 63.5% versus 91.7%, difference -28.2%, p<0.001. Overall quality of life change was -0.1 versus -12.0 points, p=0.001. Time to intracranial failure was shorter with radiosurgery alone, hazard ratio 3.6. Functional independence did not differ, p=0.26.

ncctg-n107c-cec-3.methods: Randomised controlled phase 3 trial at 48 institutions in the USA and Canada. Adults with one resected brain metastasis and a resection cavity under 5.0 cm were assigned 1:1 to postoperative radiosurgery of 12 to 20 Gy in a single fraction by cavity volume, or whole brain radiotherapy of 30 Gy in ten fractions or 37.5 Gy in 15 fractions. Analyses were by intention to treat.
ncctg-n107c-cec-3.results: 194 patients were randomised, 98 to radiosurgery and 96 to whole brain radiotherapy, with median follow-up 11.1 months. Median cognitive-deterioration-free survival was 3.7 versus 3.0 months, hazard ratio 0.47, p<0.0001. Cognitive deterioration at 6 months was 52% versus 85%. Median overall survival was 12.2 versus 11.6 months, hazard ratio 1.07, p=0.70. Commonest grade 3 or 4 events were hearing impairment and cognitive disturbance.

neoaltto.methods: Parallel-group, randomised, open-label phase 3 study. Women from 23 countries with HER2-positive primary breast cancer and tumours larger than 2 cm were assigned to oral lapatinib 1500 mg, intravenous trastuzumab, or lapatinib 1000 mg plus trastuzumab. Anti-HER2 therapy alone ran for six weeks, then weekly paclitaxel 80 mg/m2 was added for 12 weeks before surgery. Adjuvant chemotherapy and the same targeted therapy followed to 52 weeks. The primary endpoint was pathological complete response.
neoaltto.results: 154 patients received lapatinib, 149 trastuzumab and 152 the combination. Pathological complete response was 51.3% (78 of 152) with lapatinib plus trastuzumab against 29.5% (44 of 149) with trastuzumab, a difference of 21.1 percentage points (9.1 to 34.2, p=0.0001). Lapatinib alone gave 24.7% (38 of 154). Grade 3 diarrhoea occurred in 23.4%, 21.1% and 2.0% of the lapatinib, combination and trastuzumab groups. The 2019 survival report gave 6-year event-free survival of 74% with the combination and 67% with trastuzumab.

neoletrib.methods: Trial report for NEOLETRIB, which evaluates the response of ER-positive, HER2-negative luminal A or B breast cancer to neoadjuvant letrozole plus ribociclib. Treatment runs for six months. Molecular work includes sequential single-cell RNA sequencing of tumour biopsies, with biobanking of blood samples, tumour biopsies and gut microbiome specimens.

neomonarch.methods: Phase 2 neoadjuvant study. Postmenopausal women with stage I to IIIB HR-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer were randomised to a two-week lead-in of abemaciclib, anastrozole, or abemaciclib plus anastrozole, followed by 14 weeks of the combination. The primary objective was change in Ki67 from baseline to two weeks of treatment. Additional objectives were clinical, radiologic and pathologic response, safety, and gene expression changes related to cell proliferation and immune response.
neomonarch.results: Abemaciclib, alone or with anastrozole, gave a significant decrease in Ki67 expression and potent cell-cycle arrest at two weeks compared with anastrozole alone. Complete cell-cycle arrest was reached in 58% and 68% of the abemaciclib-containing arms versus 14% with anastrozole (P < 0.001). At the end of treatment 46% of intent-to-treat patients achieved a radiologic response and 4% a pathological complete response. The most common all-grade adverse events were diarrhea (62%), constipation (44%) and nausea (42%).

neopact.methods: Open-label phase 2 trial with a single group of patients with stage I to III triple-negative breast cancer at 2 sites. Neoadjuvant carboplatin (AUC 6) and docetaxel 75 mg/m2 plus pembrolizumab 200 mg were given every 21 days for 6 cycles with myeloid growth factor support. Enrolment ran from 2018 to 2022. The primary end point was pathologic complete response. Secondary end points were residual cancer burden, event-free survival, toxicity and immune biomarkers.
neopact.results: Among 115 eligible female patients, median age 50 years, 39% had node-positive disease. The pathologic complete response rate was 58% (95% CI 48-67) and the rate of residual cancer burden 0 plus 1 was 69% (95% CI 60-78). Grade 3 or higher immune-mediated adverse events occurred in 3.5% of patients. Estimated 3-year event-free survival was 86% overall, 98% in the pathologic complete response group and 68% in the no-response group.

neopal.methods: NeoPAL was a randomised, parallel, non-comparative phase 2 study. Patients with ER-positive, HER2-negative, Prosigna-defined luminal B or luminal A node-positive stage II-III breast cancer who were not candidates for breast-conserving surgery were assigned to letrozole 2.5 mg daily plus palbociclib 125 mg daily 3 weeks in 4 for 19 weeks, or to three cycles of FEC100 followed by three cycles of docetaxel 100 mg/m2. The primary end point was residual cancer burden 0-I rate.
neopal.results: 106 patients were randomised, with a median Prosigna ROR score of 71 (22-93). Residual cancer burden 0-I was seen in 4 patients on letrozole-palbociclib (7.7%, 95% CI 0.4-14.9) and 8 on chemotherapy (15.7%, 95% CI 5.7-25.7). Pathological complete response rates were 3.8% and 5.9%. Clinical response was 75% and breast-conserving surgery 69% in both arms. Preoperative Endocrine Prognostic Index 0 scores occurred in 17.6% and 8.0%. Serious adverse events numbered 2 versus 17.

neosphere.methods: Multicentre, open-label, phase 2 study. Treatment-naive women with HER2-positive breast cancer were randomly assigned 1:1:1:1, stratified by operable, locally advanced and inflammatory disease and by hormone receptor expression, to four neoadjuvant cycles of trastuzumab plus docetaxel (group A), pertuzumab and trastuzumab plus docetaxel (group B), pertuzumab and trastuzumab (group C), or pertuzumab plus docetaxel (group D). The primary endpoint was pathological complete response in the breast in the intention-to-treat population. Neither patients nor investigators were masked.
neosphere.results: Of 417 eligible patients, 107 went to group A, 107 to group B, 107 to group C and 96 to group D. Pathological complete response was 45.8% (95% CI 36.1-55.7) in group B against 29.0% (20.6-38.5) in group A, p=0.0141. It was 24.0% in group D and 16.8% in group C. The most common grade 3 or higher event was neutropenia. The 5-year analysis reported progression-free survival of 81%, 86%, 73% and 73% in groups A to D.

neostop.methods: Multisite randomised phase 2 trial. Patients aged 18 or older with stage I to III triple-negative breast cancer were randomised 1:1 to weekly paclitaxel for 12 weeks plus carboplatin AUC6 every 21 days for four cycles followed by doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide every 14 days for four cycles, or to carboplatin AUC6 plus docetaxel every 21 days for six cycles. Stromal tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes were assessed.
neostop.results: 100 patients were randomised, 48 to arm A and 52 to arm B. Pathologic complete response was 54% in each arm and residual cancer burden 0 or I was 67% in each. Median stromal tumour-infiltrating lymphocyte density was 20% with pathologic complete response versus 5% with residual disease. Grade 3 or 4 neutropenia was 60% versus 8% and febrile neutropenia 19% versus 0%. Mean cost was lower in arm B.

neotrip.methods: 280 patients with triple-negative breast cancer were enrolled in this multicentre randomised study. They received neoadjuvant carboplatin AUC 2 and nab-paclitaxel 125 mg/m2 intravenously on days 1 and 8, without atezolizumab (n=142) or with atezolizumab 1200 mg intravenously on day 1 (n=138). Both regimens were given every 3 weeks for eight cycles before surgery, followed by four cycles of an adjuvant anthracycline regimen. The primary aim was event-free survival, with pathological complete response an important secondary aim.
neotrip.results: In the intention-to-treat analysis the pathological complete response rate was 48.6% with atezolizumab against 44.4% without, odds ratio 1.18, 95% CI 0.74-1.89, P=0.48. Treatment-related adverse events were similar between regimens except for significantly more serious adverse events and liver transaminase abnormalities with atezolizumab. In multivariate analysis PD-L1 expression was the most significant factor influencing the rate of pathological complete response, odds ratio 2.08.

noah.methods: Randomised superiority trial. Women with HER2-positive locally advanced or inflammatory breast cancer received neoadjuvant chemotherapy of doxorubicin, paclitaxel, cyclophosphamide, methotrexate and fluorouracil, with 1 year of trastuzumab given neoadjuvantly and adjuvantly (n=117) or without trastuzumab (n=118). Randomisation used a computer program with minimisation by geographical area, disease stage and hormone receptor status. A parallel cohort of 99 patients with HER2-negative disease received the same chemotherapy. The primary endpoint was event-free survival, analysed by intention to treat.
noah.results: Trastuzumab significantly improved event-free survival in HER2-positive patients. Three-year event-free survival was 71% (95% CI 61-78, 36 events) with trastuzumab and 56% (46-65, 51 events) without, hazard ratio 0.59 (95% CI 0.38-0.90), p=0.013. Two patients (2%) developed symptomatic cardiac failure despite concurrent doxorubicin, and both responded to cardiac drugs. The 2014 follow-up reported 5-year event-free survival of 58% with trastuzumab and 43% with chemotherapy alone, hazard ratio 0.64 (95% CI 0.44-0.93), p=0.016.

nrg-cc001.methods: Phase 3 trial enrolling adult patients with brain metastases, randomised to hippocampal-avoidance whole brain radiotherapy plus memantine or whole brain radiotherapy plus memantine. The primary endpoint was time to cognitive function failure, defined as decline by the reliable change index on at least one cognitive test. Secondary endpoints were overall survival, intracranial progression-free survival, toxicity, and patient-reported symptom burden.
nrg-cc001.results: 518 patients were randomised between July 2015 and March 2018, with median follow-up of 7.9 months for living patients. Cognitive failure risk was lower with hippocampal avoidance, adjusted hazard ratio 0.74, p=0.02, driven by less deterioration in executive function at 4 months, 23.3% versus 40.4%, and in learning and memory at 6 months. Overall survival, intracranial progression-free survival, and toxicity did not differ.

nrg-oncology-krog-rtog-1119.methods: Randomised phase 2 trial in patients with HER2-positive breast cancer and at least one measurable, unirradiated brain metastasis. Patients were randomised to whole brain radiotherapy of 37.5 Gy over 3 weeks or stereotactic radiosurgery at size-based dosing, with or without concurrent lapatinib 1000 mg daily for 6 weeks. Secondary endpoints were objective response rate, lesion-specific response, central nervous system progression-free survival, and overall survival.
nrg-oncology-krog-rtog-1119.results: 143 patients were randomised from July 2012 to September 2019, with 116 analysable for the primary endpoint. Intracranial complete response at 12 weeks was 0% with radiotherapy plus lapatinib versus 6% with radiotherapy alone, one-sided p=0.97, and 12-week objective response was not improved. At 4 weeks objective response was 55% versus 42%. Grade 3 and 4 adverse event rates were 8% and 0% for radiotherapy and 28% and 6% with lapatinib.

nsabp-b-14.methods: Randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of postoperative tamoxifen 10 mg twice daily in 2,644 patients with breast cancer, histologically negative axillary nodes, and estrogen-receptor-positive tumours of at least 10 fmol. Disease-free survival and survival were compared over four years of follow-up, with multivariate analysis of subgroups. A later correlative study measured a 21-gene recurrence score by RT-PCR in tumour blocks from tamoxifen-treated patients.
nsabp-b-14.results: Disease-free survival was 83 percent with tamoxifen versus 77 percent with placebo (P<0.00001), and survival 93 versus 92 percent (P=0.3). Benefit held in women 49 or younger (P=0.0005) and 50 or older (P=0.0008). Tamoxifen reduced local and distant treatment failure, contralateral tumours, and recurrence after lumpectomy. In 668 assayed tumours, 10-year distant recurrence was 6.8, 14.3 and 30.5 percent across low, intermediate and high recurrence-score groups.

nsabp-b-18.methods: 1,523 women with primary operable breast cancer were randomly assigned to doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide given preoperatively or postoperatively. Clinical tumour response to preoperative therapy was graded complete, partial or absent, and clinical complete responses were classified as pathologic complete response or residual invasive cells. Disease-free survival, distant disease-free survival and survival were estimated through five years and updated through nine years.
nsabp-b-18.results: No significant difference in disease-free survival, distant disease-free survival or survival at five years (P=.99, .70 and .83). At nine years survival was 69 versus 70 percent and disease-free survival 55 versus 53 percent. Lumpectomy with radiotherapy was more frequent after preoperative therapy (67.8 versus 59.8 percent). Relapse-free survival was 85.7 percent after pathologic complete response versus 63.9 percent with no clinical response (P<.0001).

nsabp-b-20.methods: 2,306 patients with node-negative, estrogen receptor-positive breast cancer were randomly assigned after surgery to one of three groups. 771 assessable patients received tamoxifen alone, 767 received methotrexate, fluorouracil and tamoxifen, and 768 received cyclophosphamide, methotrexate, fluorouracil and tamoxifen. Disease-free survival, distant disease-free survival and survival were estimated by the Kaplan-Meier method with two-sided P values. A later analysis measured the 21-gene recurrence score in 651 tumours.
nsabp-b-20.results: Through five years, disease-free survival was 90 and 89 percent with the two chemotherapy plus tamoxifen regimens versus 85 percent with tamoxifen (P=.01 and .001), distant disease-free survival 92 and 91 versus 87 percent, and survival 97 and 96 versus 94 percent. Benefit was greatest in patients aged 49 or under. Chemotherapy benefit interacted with recurrence score (P=.038), being large at scores of 31 or more and minimal below 18.

nsabp-b-27.methods: 2,411 women with operable breast cancer were randomly assigned to preoperative doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide followed by surgery, to the same chemotherapy followed by docetaxel then surgery, or to the same chemotherapy followed by surgery then docetaxel. Tamoxifen was started concurrently with chemotherapy in all groups. Median time on study for the 2,404 patients with follow-up was 77.9 months.
nsabp-b-27.results: Adding docetaxel did not significantly change disease-free survival or overall survival, with trends toward better disease-free survival. Docetaxel reduced local recurrence as a first event (P=.0034). Preoperative but not postoperative docetaxel improved disease-free survival in patients with a clinical partial response after AC (hazard ratio 0.71, 95 percent CI 0.55 to 0.91, P=.007). Pathologic complete response, doubled by preoperative docetaxel, predicted overall survival (hazard ratio 0.33, P<.0001).

nsabp-b-28.methods: Between August 1995 and May 1998, 3,060 patients with resected operable breast cancer and positive axillary nodes were randomly assigned to four cycles of doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide (1,529) or the same followed by four cycles of paclitaxel (1,531). Patients aged 50 or older and younger patients with receptor-positive tumours also received five years of tamoxifen. Postlumpectomy radiotherapy was required. Median follow-up was 64.6 months.
nsabp-b-28.results: Paclitaxel reduced the hazard of a disease-free survival event by 17 percent (relative risk 0.83, 95 percent CI 0.72 to 0.95, P=.006). Five-year disease-free survival was 76 percent with paclitaxel versus 72 percent without. Five-year overall survival was 85 percent in both groups (relative risk 0.93, 95 percent CI 0.78 to 1.12, P=.46). No significant interaction with receptor status or tamoxifen use was seen. Toxicity was acceptable.

nsabp-b-41.methods: Open-label randomised phase 3 trial in women aged 18 or older with operable HER2-positive breast cancer and ECOG performance status 0 or 1. All received four cycles of doxorubicin 60 mg/m2 and cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m2, then four cycles of weekly paclitaxel 80 mg/m2 with weekly trastuzumab, daily lapatinib 1250 mg, or weekly trastuzumab plus daily lapatinib 750 mg until surgery. Randomisation was 1:1:1. All received trastuzumab after surgery to complete 52 weeks.
nsabp-b-41.results: 529 women were enrolled and 519 had pathological response determined. Breast pathological complete response occurred in 93 of 177 patients on trastuzumab (52.5 percent), 91 of 171 on lapatinib (53.2 percent, p=0.9852) and 106 of 171 on the combination (62.0 percent, p=0.095). Grade 3 diarrhoea affected 2, 20 and 27 percent of the three groups (p<0.0001). Symptomatic congestive heart failure occurred in 4, 4 and under 1 percent.

nsabp-b06.methods: A randomised trial begun in 1976. A total of 1851 women with invasive breast cancer, for whom follow-up data were available and nodal status was known, underwent randomly assigned treatment consisting of total mastectomy, lumpectomy alone, or lumpectomy plus breast irradiation. Outcomes were estimated by Kaplan-Meier and cumulative-incidence methods. Follow-up extended to 20 years.
nsabp-b06.results: The cumulative incidence of recurrent tumour in the ipsilateral breast was 14.3% after lumpectomy plus irradiation against 39.2% after lumpectomy alone, P<0.001. Disease-free survival, distant-disease-free survival and overall survival did not differ significantly among the three groups. The hazard ratio for death was 1.05 (95% CI 0.90-1.23, P=0.51) for lumpectomy alone versus mastectomy and 0.97 (0.83-1.14, P=0.74) for lumpectomy plus irradiation versus mastectomy.

nsabp-b31-n9831.methods: Planned joint analysis of two adjuvant trials. In all, 4046 patients with HER2-positive operable breast cancer were enrolled to receive doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide followed by paclitaxel with or without trastuzumab. The required number of events for the definitive overall survival analysis, 710 events, was reached in September 2012. Updated analyses of overall disease-free survival and related subgroups were also performed.
nsabp-b31-n9831.results: Median time on study was 8.4 years. Adding trastuzumab gave a 37% relative improvement in overall survival, hazard ratio 0.63 (95% CI 0.54-0.73), P<0.001, and raised the 10-year overall survival rate from 75.2% to 84%. Disease-free survival improved by 40%, hazard ratio 0.60 (95% CI 0.53-0.68), P<0.001, with the 10-year disease-free survival rate rising from 62.2% to 73.7%. All patient subgroups benefited.

nsabp-b32.methods: Randomised controlled phase 3 trial at 80 centres in Canada and the USA between May 1999 and February 2004. Women with invasive breast cancer were randomly assigned 1:1 to sentinel lymph node resection plus axillary dissection (group 1) or to sentinel node resection alone with axillary dissection only if the sentinel nodes were positive (group 2). Sentinel node resection used blue dye and radioactive tracer. The primary endpoint was overall survival.
nsabp-b32.results: 5611 women were randomly assigned and 3989 had pathologically negative sentinel nodes. Among 3986 such patients with follow-up, 309 deaths occurred, 140 of 1975 in group 1 and 169 of 2011 in group 2, hazard ratio 1.20 (95% CI 0.96-1.50, p=0.12). Eight-year overall survival was 91.8% in group 1 and 90.3% in group 2. The disease-free survival hazard ratio was 1.05 (0.90-1.22, p=0.54), with 8-year estimates 82.4% and 81.5%.

nsabp-b39.methods: Randomised phase 3 equivalence trial at 154 clinical centres in the USA, Canada, Ireland and Israel. Adult women with stage 0, I or II breast cancer up to 3 cm and lumpectomy with negative margins were assigned 1:1 to whole-breast irradiation, 50 Gy in 25 fractions over 5 weeks, or to accelerated partial breast irradiation, 34 Gy brachytherapy or 38.5 Gy external beam in 10 fractions. The primary outcome was ipsilateral breast tumour recurrence as a first recurrence.
nsabp-b39.results: Between March 2005 and April 2013, 4216 women were enrolled, 2109 to whole-breast irradiation and 2107 to partial breast irradiation. At a median follow-up of 10.2 years, ipsilateral breast tumour recurrence occurred in 90 of 2089 partial irradiation patients (4%) and 71 of 2036 whole-breast patients (3%), hazard ratio 1.22 (90% CI 0.94-1.58). The 10-year cumulative incidence was 4.6% against 3.9%. Deaths from recurring breast cancer were 49 of 2093 and 44 of 2039.

nsabp-b42.methods: Randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 trial at 158 centres in the USA, Canada and Ireland. Postmenopausal women with stage I-IIIA hormone receptor-positive breast cancer who were disease free after about 5 years of an aromatase inhibitor, or tamoxifen followed by an aromatase inhibitor, were assigned 1:1 to 5 years of letrozole 2.5 mg daily or placebo. Randomisation was stratified by nodal status, previous tamoxifen use and lowest bone mineral density T score. The primary endpoint was disease-free survival.
nsabp-b42.results: Between September 2006 and January 2010, 3966 patients were assigned to letrozole (n=1983) or placebo (n=1983), with follow-up data for 3903 and a median follow-up of 6.9 years. Letrozole did not significantly improve disease-free survival, with 292 events against 339 on placebo, hazard ratio 0.85 (95% CI 0.73-0.999), p=0.048. Seven-year disease-free survival was 84.7% with letrozole and 81.3% with placebo. The 10-year update reported a disease-free survival hazard ratio of 0.85 (0.74-0.96), P=.01.

nsabp-b51.methods: Randomised trial of regional nodal irradiation in patients with biopsy-proven node-positive breast cancer who reached ypN0 status after neoadjuvant chemotherapy. Patients with clinical stage T1 to T3, N1, M0 disease were assigned to regional nodal irradiation or no regional nodal irradiation. The primary end point was the invasive breast cancer recurrence-free interval, defined as freedom from invasive recurrence or death from breast cancer. Secondary end points were locoregional and distant recurrence-free interval, disease-free survival and overall survival.
nsabp-b51.results: A total of 1641 patients were enrolled and 1556 were included in the primary-event analysis, 772 in the irradiation group and 784 in the no-irradiation group. After a median follow-up of 59.5 months there were 109 primary end-point events, 50 with irradiation and 59 without. The hazard ratio for the invasive breast cancer recurrence-free interval was 0.88 (95% CI 0.60-1.28, P=0.51), with point estimates of 92.7% and 91.8%. Grade 4 adverse events occurred in 0.5% and 0.1%.

olympia.methods: Phase 3, double-blind, randomised trial in patients with HER2-negative early breast cancer carrying germline pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants and high-risk clinicopathological factors, who had received local treatment and neoadjuvant or adjuvant chemotherapy. Patients were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to 1 year of oral olaparib or placebo. The primary end point was invasive disease-free survival.
olympia.results: A total of 1836 patients underwent randomisation. At a prespecified interim analysis with median follow-up 2.5 years, 3-year invasive disease-free survival was 85.9% with olaparib and 77.1% with placebo, difference 8.8 percentage points (95% CI 4.5-13.0), hazard ratio 0.58 (99.5% CI 0.41-0.82), P<0.001. Three-year distant disease-free survival was 87.5% against 80.4%, hazard ratio 0.57. Deaths numbered 59 against 86. The 6.1-year update reported 6-year overall survival of 87.5% against 83.2%, hazard ratio 0.72 (95% CI 0.56-0.93).

olympiad.methods: Randomized, open-label, phase 3 trial comparing olaparib monotherapy with standard therapy. Patients had a germline BRCA mutation and HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer and had received no more than two previous chemotherapy regimens for metastatic disease. Randomisation was 2:1 to olaparib tablets 300 mg twice daily or to single-agent chemotherapy of the physician's choice, being capecitabine, eribulin, or vinorelbine in 21-day cycles. The primary end point was progression-free survival by blinded independent central review, analysed by intention to treat.
olympiad.results: Of 302 patients randomized, 205 received olaparib and 97 standard therapy. Median progression-free survival was 7.0 months with olaparib versus 4.2 months with standard therapy (hazard ratio 0.58, 95% CI 0.43 to 0.80, P<0.001). Response rate was 59.9% versus 28.8%. Grade 3 or higher adverse events occurred in 36.6% versus 50.5%. Discontinuation for toxic effects occurred in 4.9% versus 7.7%. The 2019 final overall survival report gave median overall survival 19.3 versus 17.1 months (HR 0.90, P = 0.513).

p024.methods: Randomised, double-blind, multicentre study in 337 postmenopausal women with untreated primary breast cancer positive for estrogen or progesterone receptors. Patients received letrozole 2.5 mg or tamoxifen 20 mg once daily for four months before surgery. None were candidates for breast-conserving surgery at baseline and 14 percent were considered inoperable. The primary endpoint was overall objective response by clinical palpation, with response on ultrasound and mammography and breast-conserving surgery rate as secondary endpoints.
p024.results: Objective response by clinical palpation was 55 percent with letrozole versus 36 percent with tamoxifen (P<0.001). Ultrasound response was 35 versus 25 percent (P=0.042) and mammographic response 34 versus 16 percent (P<0.001). Breast-conserving surgery was performed in 45 percent of the letrozole group versus 35 percent of the tamoxifen group (P=0.022). Both treatments were well tolerated.

p1.methods: Women at increased risk for breast cancer were randomly assigned to placebo (n=6707) or tamoxifen 20 mg per day (n=6681) for 5 years, 13,388 in total. Eligible women were 60 years of age or older, were 35 to 59 years with a 5-year predicted breast cancer risk of at least 1.66% by the Gail algorithm, or had a history of lobular carcinoma in situ.
p1.results: Tamoxifen reduced invasive breast cancer risk by 49% (two-sided P<.00001), with cumulative incidence through 69 months of 43.4 versus 22.0 per 1000 women on placebo and tamoxifen. Noninvasive breast cancer fell by 50% (P<.002). Estrogen receptor-positive tumours fell by 69%, with no difference in receptor-negative tumours. Hip, radius and spine fractures were reduced. Endometrial cancer rose (risk ratio 2.53, 95% CI 1.35 to 4.97). Stroke, pulmonary embolism and deep-vein thrombosis rates were elevated.

pace.methods: Randomized multicenter phase II trial in patients with hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer whose disease had progressed on previous CDK4/6 inhibitor and aromatase inhibitor therapy. Patients were randomly assigned 1:2:1 to fulvestrant alone, fulvestrant plus palbociclib, or fulvestrant plus palbociclib and avelumab. The primary end point was investigator-assessed progression-free survival in patients treated with fulvestrant versus fulvestrant plus palbociclib.
pace.results: 220 patients were randomly assigned between September 2017 and February 2022. Median age was 57 years and 80.9% were postmenopausal. Median progression-free survival was 4.8 months with fulvestrant and 4.6 months with fulvestrant plus palbociclib (hazard ratio 1.11, 90% CI 0.79 to 1.55, P = .62). Median progression-free survival with fulvestrant, palbociclib and avelumab was 8.1 months (hazard ratio 0.75, 90% CI 0.50 to 1.12, P = .23).

pada1.methods: Randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial in 83 French hospitals. Women aged 18 years or older with oestrogen receptor-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer were monitored for rising ESR1 mutation during first-line aromatase inhibitor plus palbociclib therapy. Those with newly present or increased circulating ESR1 and no synchronous progression were randomly assigned 1:1 to continue the same therapy or to switch to fulvestrant plus palbociclib. Co-primary endpoints were investigator-assessed progression-free survival from randomisation and grade 3 or worse haematological adverse events.
pada1.results: From March 2017 to January 2019, 1017 patients were included. 279 (27%) developed a rising ESR1 mutation and 172 (17%) were randomly assigned, 88 to fulvestrant plus palbociclib and 84 to continued aromatase inhibitor plus palbociclib. Median follow-up from randomisation was 26.0 months. Median progression-free survival from randomisation was 11.9 months (95% CI 9.1 to 13.6) versus 5.7 months (3.9 to 7.5), stratified hazard ratio 0.61 (0.43 to 0.86), p=0.0040. Grade 3 or worse neutropenia affected 715 patients (70.3%).

pakt.methods: Double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomised phase 2 trial in women with untreated metastatic triple-negative breast cancer. 140 patients were randomly assigned 1:1 to paclitaxel 90 mg/m2 on days 1, 8 and 15 with either capivasertib 400 mg twice daily or placebo on days 2 to 5, 9 to 12 and 16 to 19 of each 28-day cycle, until progression or unacceptable toxicity. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival.
pakt.results: Median progression-free survival was 5.9 months with capivasertib versus 4.2 months with placebo (hazard ratio 0.74, 95 percent CI 0.50 to 1.08). Median overall survival was 19.1 versus 12.6 months (hazard ratio 0.61, 95 percent CI 0.37 to 0.99, P=.04). In 28 patients with pathway-altered tumours, median progression-free survival was 9.3 versus 3.7 months (hazard ratio 0.30, P=.01). Grade 3 or worse diarrhoea affected 13 percent versus 1 percent.

pallas.methods: Prospective, randomized, phase III trial. Patients with hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative early breast cancer were randomly assigned to 2 years of palbociclib 125 mg orally once daily on days 1-21 of a 28-day cycle with adjuvant endocrine therapy, or to adjuvant endocrine therapy alone for at least 5 years. The primary end point was invasive disease-free survival. Secondary end points were invasive breast cancer-free survival, distant recurrence-free survival, locoregional cancer-free survival and overall survival.
pallas.results: 5,796 patients were enrolled and 5,761 were included in the intention-to-treat population. At a median follow-up of 31 months, invasive disease-free survival events occurred in 253 of 2,884 patients (8.8%) on palbociclib plus endocrine therapy and 263 of 2,877 (9.1%) on endocrine therapy alone. Invasive disease-free survival at 4 years was 84.2% versus 84.5% (hazard ratio 0.96, CI 0.81 to 1.14, P = .65). The 5-year follow-up reported 5-year overall survival 92.6% versus 93.2% (hazard ratio 1.09).

pallet.methods: Phase II randomized trial in postmenopausal women with ER-positive primary breast cancer and tumors of at least 2.0 cm. Patients were assigned 3:2:2:2 to letrozole for 14 weeks, letrozole for 2 weeks then palbociclib plus letrozole to 14 weeks, palbociclib for 2 weeks then palbociclib plus letrozole to 14 weeks, or palbociclib plus letrozole for 14 weeks. Coprimary end points comparing letrozole with the palbociclib groups were change in Ki-67 to 14 weeks and clinical response.
pallet.results: 307 patients were recruited. Clinical response did not differ between palbociclib plus letrozole and letrozole (54.3% versus 49.5%, P = .20), and progressive disease was 3.2% versus 5.4%. Median log-fold change in Ki-67 was -4.1 versus -2.2 (P < .001) in the 190 evaluable patients (61.9%), a geometric mean change of -97.4% versus -88.5%. Complete cell-cycle arrest reached 90% versus 59% (P < .001). Grade 3 or greater toxicity was 49.8% versus 17.0% (P < .001).

palmira.methods: International, randomized, open-label, phase II study in 198 patients with hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer that progressed after first-line palbociclib plus endocrine therapy. Patients needed clinical benefit on the previous regimen, meaning response or stable disease for at least 24 weeks, or progression on adjuvant palbociclib. Randomisation was 2:1 to palbociclib rechallenge plus second-line endocrine therapy with fulvestrant or letrozole, or to second-line endocrine therapy alone. The primary end point was investigator-assessed progression-free survival.
palmira.results: Between April 2019 and October 2022, 136 patients were assigned to palbociclib plus endocrine therapy and 62 to endocrine therapy alone. Median investigator-assessed progression-free survival was 4.9 months (95% CI, 3.6 to 6.1) with palbociclib plus endocrine therapy versus 3.6 months (95% CI, 2.5 to 4.2) with endocrine therapy alone (hazard ratio 0.84, 95% CI 0.66 to 1.07, P = .149). Grade 3 or higher treatment-emergent adverse events were 47.4% versus 10.0%.

paloma-1-trio-18.methods: Open-label randomised phase 2 trial. Postmenopausal women with advanced oestrogen receptor-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer and no prior systemic therapy for advanced disease entered two sequential cohorts. Cohort 1 required biomarker status alone. Cohort 2 also required CCND1 amplification, p16 loss, or both. Patients were randomised 1:1, stratified by disease site and disease-free interval, to letrozole 2.5 mg daily or letrozole plus palbociclib 125 mg daily for three weeks on and one week off in 28-day cycles.
paloma-1-trio-18.results: 165 patients were randomised, 84 to palbociclib plus letrozole and 81 to letrozole. Median progression-free survival was 20.2 versus 10.2 months (hazard ratio 0.488, 95% CI 0.319-0.748, one-sided p=0.0004). The hazard ratio was 0.299 in cohort 1 and 0.508 in cohort 2. Grade 3-4 neutropenia occurred in 54% versus 1% and leucopenia in 19% versus none. 13% versus 2% discontinued for adverse events.

paloma2.methods: Double-blind phase 3 study. 666 postmenopausal women with ER-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer who had no prior treatment for advanced disease were randomly assigned 2:1 to palbociclib plus letrozole or placebo plus letrozole. The primary end point was investigator-assessed progression-free survival. Secondary end points were overall survival, objective response, clinical benefit response, patient-reported outcomes, pharmacokinetic effects and safety.
paloma2.results: Median progression-free survival was 24.8 months (95% CI, 22.1 to not estimable) with palbociclib plus letrozole versus 14.5 months (95% CI, 12.9 to 17.1) with placebo plus letrozole (hazard ratio 0.58, 95% CI 0.46 to 0.72, P<0.001). Grade 3 or 4 neutropenia occurred in 66.4% versus 1.4%. Permanent discontinuation for adverse events occurred in 43 patients (9.7%) versus 13 (5.9%). The 2024 overall survival report gave median overall survival 53.9 versus 51.2 months (hazard ratio 0.96).

paloma3.methods: Multicentre, double-blind, randomised phase 3 study at 144 centres in 17 countries. Women with hormone-receptor-positive, HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer that had progressed on previous endocrine therapy were randomly assigned 2:1 to oral palbociclib 125 mg daily for 3 weeks of each 28-day cycle plus fulvestrant 500 mg, or placebo plus fulvestrant. Stratification was by sensitivity to previous hormonal therapy, menopausal status and visceral metastasis. The primary endpoint was investigator-assessed progression-free survival, analysed by intention to treat.
paloma3.results: Between Oct 7, 2013, and Aug 26, 2014, 521 patients were assigned, 347 to fulvestrant plus palbociclib and 174 to fulvestrant plus placebo. Median follow-up was 8.9 months. Median progression-free survival was 9.5 months (95% CI 9.2-11.0) versus 4.6 months (3.5-5.6), hazard ratio 0.46 (95% CI 0.36-0.59, p<0.0001). Grade 3 or 4 adverse events occurred in 73% versus 22% of patients. The 2022 analysis reported median overall survival 34.8 versus 28.0 months (hazard ratio 0.81).

pamela.methods: Open-label, single-group phase 2 trial in 19 hospitals in Spain. Women aged at least 18 years with untreated, centrally confirmed HER2-positive stage I-IIIA breast cancer received lapatinib 1000 mg daily and trastuzumab for 18 weeks. Hormone receptor-positive patients also received letrozole or tamoxifen. Surgery followed one to three weeks after the last dose. Intrinsic subtype was determined by PAM50 on biopsies at day 0 and day 14.
pamela.results: 151 patients were recruited and 137 (91%) completed treatment as planned. At baseline 101 (67%) had HER2-enriched tumours. Pathological complete response in the breast occurred in 46 of 151 patients (30%, 95% CI 23-39). It occurred in 41 of 101 HER2-enriched tumours (41%) and in five of 50 non-HER2-enriched tumours (10%), odds ratio 6.2 (95% CI 2.3-16.8, p=0.0004).

patina.methods: Phase 3, open-label, randomized trial in patients with hormone-receptor-positive, HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer who did not have disease progression after four to eight cycles of chemotherapy plus HER2-targeted therapy. Patients were randomly assigned 1:1 to receive maintenance HER2-targeted and endocrine therapies with or without palbociclib. The primary end point was investigator-assessed progression-free survival. Secondary end points included objective response, clinical benefit, safety and overall survival.
patina.results: 518 patients underwent randomization, 261 to palbociclib and 257 to standard therapy. At a median follow-up of 53.5 months, median progression-free survival was 44.3 months with palbociclib versus 29.1 months with standard therapy (hazard ratio 0.75, 95% CI 0.59 to 0.96, two-sided P = 0.02). Grade 3 adverse events occurred in 79.7% of the palbociclib group and 30.6% of the standard-therapy group. Grade 4 events occurred in 10.0% and 3.6%. Neutropenia predominated.

patricia.methods: Single-arm study in patients with HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer and progressive central nervous system metastases after radiotherapy. Patients received standard-dose pertuzumab plus high-dose trastuzumab 6 mg/kg weekly until central nervous system or systemic progression or unacceptable toxicity. The primary endpoint was confirmed central nervous system objective response rate. Secondary endpoints were response duration, clinical benefit rate, progression-free survival, overall survival, safety and patient-reported outcomes. This report adds 21 months of follow-up.
patricia.results: 39 patients had completed or discontinued treatment by the cut-off. Confirmed central nervous system objective response rate was 11% (95% CI 3.0-25.4). Median central nervous system progression-free survival was 4.6 months (95% CI 4.0-8.9), as was combined central nervous system or systemic progression-free survival. Median overall survival was 27.2 months. Six-month central nervous system clinical benefit rate was 51% (19 patients). Treatment-related grade 3/4 adverse events occurred in 7.7%.

pattern.methods: Phase 3 randomized trial in China. Women aged 18 to 70 years with operable triple-negative breast cancer after definitive surgery, either node-positive or node-negative with tumor diameter over 10 mm, were randomized to paclitaxel 80 mg/m2 plus carboplatin AUC 2 on days 1, 8 and 15 every 28 days for 6 cycles, or to cyclophosphamide, epirubicin and fluorouracil every 3 weeks for 3 cycles followed by docetaxel for 3 cycles. The primary end point was disease-free survival.
pattern.results: 647 patients were randomized, 322 to CEF-T and 325 to paclitaxel plus carboplatin. At a median follow-up of 62 months, 5-year disease-free survival was 86.5% with paclitaxel plus carboplatin versus 80.3% with CEF-T (hazard ratio 0.65, 95% CI 0.44 to 0.96, P = .03). Overall survival did not differ (hazard ratio 0.71, 95% CI 0.42 to 1.22, P = .22). In subgroup analysis the disease-free survival hazard ratio was 0.44 with BRCA1/2 variants and 0.39 with HRR variants.

pearl.methods: Multicentre phase III randomised trial in patients with aromatase inhibitor-resistant metastatic breast cancer, enrolled in two consecutive cohorts. Cohort 1 randomised 1:1 to palbociclib plus exemestane or capecitabine. After evidence that ESR1 mutations drive aromatase inhibitor resistance, cohort 2 randomised 1:1 to palbociclib plus fulvestrant or capecitabine. Stratification was by disease site, prior endocrine sensitivity, prior chemotherapy for metastatic disease and country. Co-primary endpoints were progression-free survival in cohort 2 and in wild-type ESR1 patients.
pearl.results: 296 patients entered cohort 1 and 305 entered cohort 2. Palbociclib plus endocrine therapy was not superior to capecitabine in cohort 2 (median progression-free survival 7.5 versus 10.0 months, adjusted hazard ratio 1.13) or in wild-type ESR1 patients (8.0 versus 10.6 months, adjusted hazard ratio 1.11). Grade 3-4 neutropenia was 57.4% and 55.7% with palbociclib versus 5.5% with capecitabine. Time to deterioration of global health status favoured palbociclib, adjusted hazard ratio 0.67.

pearly.methods: Multicenter, randomized, phase III trial in patients with stage II or III triple-negative breast cancer, treated in the neoadjuvant or adjuvant setting. Patients received either doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide followed by a taxane, or doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide followed by a taxane with carboplatin added. The primary endpoint was event-free survival. Secondary endpoints included overall survival, invasive disease-free survival, distant recurrence-free survival, pathologic complete response rate and safety.
pearly.results: Between January 2016 and June 2020, 868 patients were randomly assigned. At a median follow-up of 57.2 months, carboplatin improved event-free survival (hazard ratio 0.67, 95% CI 0.49 to 0.92, P = 0.012). The 5-year event-free survival rate rose from 75.1% to 82.3%, an absolute difference of 7.2%. Overall survival, invasive disease-free survival and distant recurrence-free survival trended in favour of carboplatin without reaching significance. Grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events were 74.7% versus 56.7%.

pembrolizumab-in-bm-of-diverse-histologi.methods: Single-arm, open-label phase 2 trial of pembrolizumab, a programmed cell death protein 1 inhibitor, in patients with brain metastases of different histologies. Nine patients with untreated brain metastases formed cohort A and 48 with recurrent and progressive brain metastases formed cohort B. The primary endpoint was the proportion achieving intracranial benefit, defined as complete response, partial response or stable disease. Overall survival was a secondary endpoint.
pembrolizumab-in-bm-of-diverse-histologi.results: The primary endpoint was met with an intracranial benefit rate of 42.1% (90% CI 31-54%). Median overall survival was 8.0 months across both cohorts, 6.5 months in cohort A and 8.1 months in cohort B. Seven patients (12.3%) with breast, melanoma and sarcoma histologies survived beyond two years. Thirty patients (52%) had one or more grade 3 or higher possibly related adverse events, including two grade 4 cerebral oedema.

pembrolizumab-plus-radiotherapy-in-metas.methods: Single-arm, Simon two-stage phase 2 trial that enrolled 17 patients with metastatic triple-negative breast cancer, median age 52 years, unselected for programmed death-ligand 1 expression. Radiotherapy of 3000 cGy was delivered in five daily fractions. Pembrolizumab 200 mg was given intravenously within three days of the first radiotherapy fraction and then every three weeks until progression. The primary endpoint was overall response rate at week 13 in unirradiated lesions by RECIST version 1.1.
pembrolizumab-plus-radiotherapy-in-metas.results: The overall response rate was 17.6%, three of 17 patients (95% CI 4.7-44.2), with three complete responses, one stable disease and 13 progressive disease. Eight patients died before week 13 from progression. Among the nine women assessed at week 13, three (33%) had a complete response with 100% tumour volume reduction outside the irradiated field, durable for 18, 20 and 108 weeks. Four grade 3 events were attributed to pembrolizumab.

penelope-b.methods: Double-blind, placebo-controlled phase III trial in women with hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative primary breast cancer and no pathological complete response after taxane-containing neoadjuvant chemotherapy, at high risk of relapse by a CPS-EG score of 3 or more, or 2 with ypN+. Patients were assigned 1:1 to 13 cycles of palbociclib 125 mg once daily on days 1-21 of a 28-day cycle or placebo, each added to endocrine therapy. The primary endpoint was invasive disease-free survival.
penelope-b.results: 1250 patients were randomly assigned. At a median follow-up of 42.8 months, 308 invasive disease-free survival events were confirmed. The stratified hazard ratio was 0.93 (95% repeated CI 0.74 to 1.17, weighted log-rank p=0.525), with no difference across subgroups. Related serious adverse events occurred in 113 patients (9.1%). The final survival report recorded 225 deaths at a median 77.8 months, with 6-year overall survival 82.4% versus 80.3% (hazard ratio 0.87, 95% CI 0.67 to 1.14, P=0.31).

peony.methods: Multicentre, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 trial that randomised 329 Asian women 2:1. Patients had ERBB2-positive early (T2-3, N0-1, M0) or locally advanced breast cancer with a primary tumour larger than 2 cm. Before surgery they received four cycles of pertuzumab or placebo with trastuzumab and docetaxel every three weeks. After surgery they received three cycles of fluorouracil, epirubicin and cyclophosphamide, then 13 cycles of the same anti-ERBB2 therapy for up to one year.
peony.results: Total pathological complete response was 39.3% (86 of 219) with pertuzumab and 21.8% (24 of 110) with placebo, difference 17.5% (95% CI 6.9-28.0, p=0.001). Grade 3 or higher neutropenia was 38.1% versus 32.7% and serious adverse events 10.1% versus 8.2%. At 62.9 months median follow-up, five-year event-free survival was 84.8% versus 73.7% (hazard ratio 0.53) and five-year disease-free survival 86.0% versus 75.0% (hazard ratio 0.52).

perelisa.methods: Phase II multicentre study in postmenopausal patients with hormone receptor-positive, HER2-positive operable breast cancer. Patients received 2 weeks of letrozole, then re-biopsy for Ki67. Molecular responders, defined by a relative Ki67 reduction above 20%, continued letrozole and began five cycles of trastuzumab plus pertuzumab. Molecular non-responders received weekly paclitaxel for 13 weeks with trastuzumab plus pertuzumab. The primary aim was breast and axillary pathological complete response under a two-stage Simon design requiring at least 8 of 43.
perelisa.results: Sixty-four patients were enrolled and 44 were molecular responders. All 44 completed letrozole with trastuzumab and pertuzumab and had surgery. Pathological complete response occurred in 9 of 44 (20.5%, 95% CI 11.1% to 34.5%). Among molecular non-responders, 16 of 17 completed treatment and had surgery, with pathological complete response in 81.3%. PAM50 subtype was associated with Ki67 response and with pathological complete response. Among molecular responders the rate was 45.5% in HER2-enriched tumours versus 13.8% in other subtypes (P=0.042).

permeate.methods: Multicentre, single-arm, two-cohort phase 2 trial in eight tertiary hospitals in China. Patients aged 18 years or older with HER2-positive brain metastases that were radiotherapy-naive (cohort A) or progressive after radiotherapy (cohort B), with ECOG performance status 0-2, received pyrotinib 400 mg orally once daily and capecitabine 1000 mg/m2 twice daily for 14 days followed by seven days off every three weeks until progression or unacceptable toxicity. The primary endpoint was confirmed intracranial objective response rate.
permeate.results: 78 women were enrolled, 59 in cohort A and 19 in cohort B. The intracranial objective response rate was 74.6% (44 of 59) in cohort A and 42.1% (eight of 19) in cohort B. Median progression-free survival was 10.9 and 5.7 months and median overall survival 35.9 and 30.6 months. Grade 3 or worse diarrhoea occurred in 24% and 21%. No treatment-related deaths occurred.

persephone.methods: Open-label randomised phase 3 non-inferiority trial at 152 UK centres. Patients aged 18 years or older with HER2-positive early breast cancer and a clear indication for chemotherapy were assigned 1:1 to 6 or 12 months of trastuzumab every 3 weeks, intravenously at an 8 mg/kg loading dose then 6 mg/kg or subcutaneously at 600 mg, combined with chemotherapy. The primary endpoint was disease-free survival by intention to treat, with a 3% non-inferiority margin at 4 years.
persephone.results: 2045 patients were assigned to 12 months and 2044 to 6 months. Median follow-up was 5.4 years. A disease-free survival event occurred in 265 of 2043 patients (13%) in the 6-month group and 247 of 2045 (12%) in the 12-month group. 4-year disease-free survival was 89.4% versus 89.8% (hazard ratio 1.07, 90% CI 0.93 to 1.24, non-inferiority p=0.011). Severe adverse events were reported by 373 of 1939 (19%) versus 459 of 1894 (24%), p=0.0002.

pertain.methods: Patients with previously untreated HER2-positive and hormone receptor-positive metastatic or locally advanced breast cancer were randomised 1:1. Arm A received pertuzumab 840 mg then 420 mg plus trastuzumab 8 mg/kg then 6 mg/kg every 3 weeks with an aromatase inhibitor, either anastrozole 1 mg or letrozole 2.5 mg daily. Arm B received trastuzumab and an aromatase inhibitor. Induction chemotherapy was at investigator discretion. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival, with overall survival and safety as key secondary endpoints.
pertain.results: Median progression-free survival was 20.6 months in Arm A and 15.8 months in Arm B, stratified hazard ratio 0.67, P=0.006. Median overall survival was 60.2 versus 57.2 months, stratified hazard ratio 1.05, P=0.78. In patients given no induction chemotherapy, median progression-free survival was 26.6 versus 12.5 months. Grade 3 or worse adverse events occurred in 72 patients (56.7%) and 51 (41.1%). Serious adverse events occurred in 46 (36.2%) and 28 (22.6%).

peruse.methods: Patients with inoperable HER2-positive locally recurrent or metastatic breast cancer and no prior systemic therapy for advanced disease, except endocrine therapy, received docetaxel, paclitaxel or nab-paclitaxel with trastuzumab and pertuzumab until progression or unacceptable toxicity. The primary endpoint was safety. Secondary endpoints included progression-free survival and overall survival. Prespecified subgroups were defined by taxane, hormone receptor status and prior trastuzumab. Exploratory analyses identified prognostic factors used to define risk subgroups.
peruse.results: Of 1436 treated patients, 588 (41%) initially received paclitaxel and 918 (64%) had hormone receptor-positive disease. Grade 3 or worse neutropenia occurred in 10% and diarrhoea in 8%. At a median follow-up of 5.7 years, median progression-free survival was 20.7 months and median overall survival was 65.3 months. Overall survival was more favourable in hormone receptor-positive disease. Trastuzumab-pretreated patients with visceral disease had median progression-free survival of 13.1 months and overall survival of 46.3 months.

phare.methods: Open-label phase 3 non-inferiority trial at 156 French centres comparing 6 months with 12 months of adjuvant trastuzumab. Eligible women were 18 years or older with non-metastatic operable HER2-positive breast cancer, either node-positive or node-negative with a tumour of at least 10 mm. All had received at least four chemotherapy cycles and started adjuvant trastuzumab. Randomisation occurred between the third and sixth month. The primary objective was non-inferiority for disease-free survival with a hazard margin of 1.15.
phare.results: 3384 patients were randomly assigned, 1691 to 12 months and 1693 to 6 months, with 1690 per group analysed. At a median follow-up of 7.5 years, 704 disease-free survival events were observed, 345 (20.4%) in the 12-month group and 359 (21.2%) in the 6-month group. The adjusted hazard ratio was 1.08 (95% CI 0.93 to 1.25, p=0.39). The confidence interval included the non-inferiority margin. No subgroup differences by duration were found.

phedra.methods: In this multicentre double-blind phase 3 study, treatment-naive women with HER2-positive early or locally advanced breast cancer were randomly assigned 1:1 to four neoadjuvant cycles of oral pyrotinib 400 mg or placebo once daily, plus intravenous trastuzumab 8 mg/kg loading then 6 mg/kg and docetaxel 100 mg/m2 every 3 weeks. The primary endpoint was the total pathological complete response rate, defined as ypT0/is and ypN0, by independent central review.
phedra.results: 355 patients were randomised, 178 to pyrotinib and 177 to placebo. Total pathological complete response was 41.0% versus 22.0%, a difference of 19.0% with one-sided P<0.0001. Investigator-assessed objective response after neoadjuvant treatment was 91.6% versus 81.9%, an increase of 9.7%. The most common grade 3 or worse adverse events were diarrhoea in 79 patients (44.4%) versus nine (5.1%), neutropenia in 33 (18.5%) versus 36 (20.3%), and decreased white blood cell count in 29 (16.3%) versus 24 (13.6%).

phergain.methods: Randomised open-label phase 2 trial at 45 hospitals in seven European countries. Patients with HER2-positive stage I-IIIA operable breast cancer and a PET-evaluable lesion were allocated 1:4 to group A, given docetaxel, carboplatin, trastuzumab and pertuzumab, or group B, given trastuzumab and pertuzumab with or without endocrine therapy. PET was done at baseline and after two cycles. Group B treatment followed PET and pathological response. This report covers the 3-year invasive disease-free survival endpoint in group B.
phergain.results: 356 patients were randomly allocated, 71 to group A and 285 to group B. Surgery was done in 63 group A patients (89%) and 267 group B patients (94%). Median follow-up was 43.3 months. In group B the 3-year invasive disease-free survival rate was 94.8% (95% CI 91.4 to 97.1, p=0.001). Grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events occurred in 62% of group A and 33% of group B, and serious adverse events in 28% versus 14%.

phergain2.methods: Multicentre single-arm phase II study in treatment-naive adults with centrally confirmed HER2-positive, node-negative early breast cancer and tumours of 5-30 mm on MRI. Patients received eight cycles of neoadjuvant trastuzumab plus pertuzumab every 3 weeks, with endocrine therapy if hormone receptor-positive. After surgery 10 adjuvant cycles followed the pathological response: trastuzumab plus pertuzumab for pathological complete response, T-DM1 for residual disease, and optional chemotherapy then T-DM1 for ypN1-3. Co-primary endpoints were 1-year quality-of-life decline and 3-year recurrence-free interval.
phergain2.results: 396 patients started neoadjuvant treatment and 391 (98.7%) had surgery. Pathological complete response was achieved by 236 patients (59.6%). Among those with residual disease, 148 (37.8%) entered cohort B and 7 (1.8%) cohort C. One year after starting treatment, a 10% or greater decline in global quality of life affected 42.8% (95% CI 36.9% to 48.8%), 37.3% with pathological complete response and 51.9% with residual disease. Treatment-related adverse events occurred in 86.6%, with one death from pneumonitis.

phila.methods: Randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 trial at 40 centres in China. 590 female patients with untreated HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer were randomised 1:1 to oral pyrotinib 400 mg once daily or placebo, each with intravenous trastuzumab 8 mg/kg in cycle 1 then 6 mg/kg, and docetaxel 75 mg/m2 on day 1 of each 21-day cycle. Randomisation was stratified by prior neoadjuvant or adjuvant trastuzumab and hormone receptor status. The primary endpoint was investigator-assessed progression-free survival.
phila.results: 297 patients received pyrotinib and 293 received placebo. At a median follow-up of 15.5 months, median progression-free survival was 24.3 months versus 10.4 months, hazard ratio 0.41 with one-sided P<0.001. Treatment-related adverse events of grade 3 or higher occurred in 267 patients (90%) versus 224 (76%). No treatment-related deaths occurred in the pyrotinib group and one occurred in the placebo group.

phoebe.methods: Open-label randomised controlled phase 3 trial at 29 hospitals in China. Patients aged 18 to 70 years with HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer and ECOG performance status 0 or 1, previously treated with trastuzumab and taxanes, were randomised 1:1 to oral pyrotinib 400 mg or lapatinib 1250 mg once daily, each with capecitabine 1000 mg/m2 twice daily on days 1 to 14 of a 21-day cycle. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival by masked independent central review.
phoebe.results: 267 patients were enrolled and randomly assigned, with 134 receiving pyrotinib plus capecitabine and 132 receiving lapatinib plus capecitabine. Median progression-free survival was 12.5 months versus 6.8 months, hazard ratio 0.39 with one-sided P<0.0001. Grade 3 or worse diarrhoea occurred in 41 patients (31%) versus 11 (8%) and hand-foot syndrome in 22 (16%) versus 20 (15%). Serious adverse events occurred in 14 patients (10%) versus 11 (8%).

plasmamatch.methods: Open-label multicohort phase 2a platform trial of circulating tumour DNA testing at 18 UK hospitals. Women with advanced breast cancer and at least one previous line of treatment entered four cohorts matched to ctDNA mutations. Cohort A was ESR1 given extended-dose fulvestrant, cohort B HER2 given neratinib, cohort C AKT1 with oestrogen receptor-positive disease given capivasertib plus fulvestrant, cohort D AKT1 oestrogen receptor-negative or PTEN given capivasertib. The primary endpoint in each cohort was confirmed objective response rate.
plasmamatch.results: 1051 patients registered and ctDNA results were available for 1034. Agreement between digital PCR and targeted sequencing was 96-99% in 800 patients. Sensitivity of digital PCR against tissue sequencing was 93% (95% CI 83-98) overall and 98% with contemporaneous biopsies. Median follow-up was 14.4 months. Responses occurred in 5 of 20 patients in cohort B (25%), 4 of 18 in cohort C (22%), 6 of 74 in cohort A (8%) and 2 of 19 in cohort D (11%).

poems.methods: Randomised trial of 257 premenopausal women with operable hormone-receptor-negative breast cancer assigned to standard chemotherapy with the gonadotropin-releasing hormone agonist goserelin or standard chemotherapy alone. The primary endpoint was the rate of ovarian failure at 2 years, defined as absence of menses in the preceding 6 months together with follicle-stimulating hormone in the postmenopausal range. Rates were compared by conditional logistic regression. Secondary endpoints included pregnancy outcomes, disease-free survival and overall survival.
poems.results: 218 patients were eligible and evaluable. Among the 135 with complete primary endpoint data, the ovarian failure rate was 8% with goserelin and 22% with chemotherapy alone (odds ratio 0.30, 95% CI 0.09 to 0.97, two-sided P=0.04). Sensitivity analyses for missing data were consistent. Among the 218 evaluable patients, pregnancy occurred in 21% of the goserelin group versus 11% (P=0.03). The goserelin group also had improved disease-free survival (P=0.04) and overall survival (P=0.05).

poetic.methods: Open-label multicentre parallel-group randomised phase 3 trial at 130 UK hospitals. Postmenopausal women aged at least 50 years with performance status 0-1 and hormone receptor-positive operable breast cancer were randomly assigned 2:1 to a perioperative aromatase inhibitor, letrozole 2.5 mg or anastrozole 1 mg daily for 14 days before and after surgery, or to no such treatment. The primary endpoint was time to recurrence. A second objective examined 2-week Ki67 dichotomised at 10%.
poetic.results: 4480 women were randomly assigned, 2976 to perioperative aromatase inhibitor and 1504 to control. Median follow-up was 62.9 months. Breast cancer recurrence occurred in 434 of 4480 women (10%), 280 in the treated group and 154 in the control group, hazard ratio 0.92 (95% CI 0.75 to 1.12), p=0.40. Freedom from recurrence at 5 years was 91.0% versus 90.4%. In the treated HER2-negative subgroup, 5-year recurrence risk was 4.3% for low-low Ki67, 8.4% for high-low and 21.5% for high-high.

positive.methods: Single-group trial of temporary interruption of adjuvant endocrine therapy to attempt pregnancy in young women with previous breast cancer. Eligible women were 42 years or younger, had stage I, II or III disease, had taken adjuvant endocrine therapy for 18 to 30 months and desired pregnancy. The primary endpoint was the number of breast cancer events, assessed after 1600 patient-years against a safety threshold of 46 events. Outcomes were compared with an external control cohort.
positive.results: Among 516 women the median age was 37 years and 93.4% had stage I or II disease. Of 497 women followed for pregnancy status, 368 (74.0%) had at least one pregnancy and 317 (63.8%) at least one live birth. At 1638 patient-years, median follow-up 41 months, 44 patients had a breast cancer event, below the safety threshold. The updated results report gave a 5-year incidence of breast cancer-free interval events of 12.3% versus 13.2% in SOFT/TEXT controls.

postmonarch.methods: Double-blind randomised phase III study in patients with hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer who had progressed on a previous CDK4/6 inhibitor plus aromatase inhibitor as initial therapy for advanced disease, or who recurred on or after adjuvant CDK4/6 inhibitor plus endocrine therapy. Patients were assigned 1:1 to abemaciclib plus fulvestrant or placebo plus fulvestrant. The primary endpoint was investigator-assessed progression-free survival. Secondary endpoints included progression-free survival by blinded independent central review, objective response rate and safety.
postmonarch.results: 368 patients were randomly assigned, 182 to abemaciclib plus fulvestrant and 186 to placebo plus fulvestrant. At the primary analysis with 258 events the hazard ratio was 0.73 (95% CI 0.57 to 0.95, nominal p=0.017). Median progression-free survival was 6.0 months versus 5.3 months, with 6-month rates of 50% and 37%. Central review gave a hazard ratio of 0.55 (95% CI 0.39 to 0.77). Objective response rate in measurable disease was 17% versus 7% (nominal p=0.015).

prime2.methods: Phase 3 randomised trial of omitting radiotherapy in women 65 years of age or older with hormone receptor-positive, node-negative, T1 or T2 primary breast cancer up to 3 cm, treated with breast-conserving surgery with clear margins and adjuvant endocrine therapy. Patients were randomly assigned to whole-breast irradiation of 40 to 50 Gy or to no irradiation. The primary endpoint was local recurrence. Regional recurrence, breast cancer-specific survival, distant recurrence as first event and overall survival were also assessed.
prime2.results: 1326 women were enrolled, 658 assigned to whole-breast irradiation and 668 to no irradiation. Median follow-up was 9.1 years. The cumulative incidence of local recurrence within 10 years was 9.5% without radiotherapy and 0.9% with radiotherapy (hazard ratio 10.4, 95% CI 4.1 to 26.1, P<0.001). The 10-year incidence of distant recurrence as a first event was 1.6% without radiotherapy and 3.0% with it. Overall survival at 10 years was 80.8% versus 80.7%.

proact.methods: Randomised multicentre study in postmenopausal women with hormone receptor-positive large operable or potentially operable breast cancer. Patients received anastrozole (n=228) or tamoxifen (n=223), with or without chemotherapy, for 12 weeks before primary surgery. The study also examined the effect of preoperative endocrine therapy in patients scheduled for mastectomy and in patients with inoperable tumours at baseline.
proact.results: Objective response occurred in 39.5% with anastrozole and 35.4% with tamoxifen by ultrasound, and in 50.0% and 46.2% by caliper measurement. Among the 314 patients given hormonal therapy only, feasible surgery improved after 3 months in 43.0% with anastrozole and 30.8% with tamoxifen (P=0.04). In the intent-to-treat population the improvement was numerically higher with anastrozole but not significant. Drug-related adverse events occurred in 20.2% and 18.1%.

proton-csi-versus-photon-ifrt.methods: Randomised phase 2 trial conducted between April 2020 and October 2021 in patients with non-small cell lung cancer or breast cancer and leptomeningeal metastasis. Patients with other solid tumours were enrolled in an exploratory proton craniospinal irradiation cohort. After stratification by histology and systemic disease status, randomised patients were assigned 2:1 to proton craniospinal irradiation or photon involved-field radiotherapy. The primary endpoint was central nervous system progression-free survival. Secondary endpoints included overall survival.
proton-csi-versus-photon-ifrt.results: Of 98 patients, 72 (73.5%) were female and the median age was 59 years. 42 patients were assigned to proton craniospinal irradiation and 21 to photon involved-field radiotherapy. Median central nervous system progression-free survival was 8.2 months versus 2.3 months (P<0.001). Median overall survival was 11.3 months versus 4.9 months (P=0.04). In the exploratory cohort of 35 patients, median central nervous system progression-free survival was 5.8 months and median overall survival was 7.0 months.

right-choice.methods: Open-label, multicenter, randomized phase II trial. Pre- or perimenopausal women with clinically aggressive HR-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer were randomly assigned 1:1 to first-line ribociclib 600 mg once daily, 3 weeks on and 1 week off, plus letrozole or anastrozole and goserelin, or to investigator's choice of combination chemotherapy with docetaxel plus capecitabine, paclitaxel plus gemcitabine, or capecitabine plus vinorelbine. The primary end point was progression-free survival.
right-choice.results: 222 patients were randomized, 112 to ribociclib plus endocrine therapy and 110 to chemotherapy. 150 (67.6%) had symptomatic visceral metastases and 106 (47.7%) had investigator-assessed visceral crisis. Median follow-up was 37.0 months. Median progression-free survival was 21.8 months versus 12.8 months, hazard ratio 0.61 (95% CI 0.43 to 0.87), P=.003. Overall response rates were 66.1% versus 61.8%. Median time to response was 4.9 versus 3.2 months. Symptomatic adverse events were less frequent with ribociclib.

rtog-0614.methods: Adults with brain metastases received whole-brain radiotherapy and were randomised to memantine 20 mg daily or placebo, started within 3 days of beginning radiotherapy and continued for 24 weeks. Serial standardised tests of cognitive function were performed.
rtog-0614.results: Of 554 patients accrued, 508 were eligible. Delayed recall declined less with memantine at 24 weeks (P = .059), not significant with 149 analysable patients and 35% power. Time to cognitive decline was longer with memantine (hazard ratio 0.78, 95% CI 0.62-0.99, P = .01), and cognitive failure at 24 weeks was 53.8% versus 64.9%. Executive function, processing speed and delayed recognition favoured memantine. Grade 3 or 4 toxicity was similar.

rtog-9508.methods: Patients with one to three newly diagnosed brain metastases were randomly allocated whole-brain radiotherapy or whole-brain radiotherapy followed by a stereotactic radiosurgery boost. Stratification was by number of metastases and extracranial disease status. The primary outcome was survival. Secondary outcomes were tumour response, local and overall intracranial recurrence rates, cause of death and performance measurements.
rtog-9508.results: 333 patients were enrolled at 55 institutions, 167 assigned whole-brain radiotherapy plus radiosurgery and 164 whole-brain radiotherapy alone. In patients with a single metastasis median survival was 6.5 versus 4.9 months (p = 0.0393). A stable or improved Karnofsky score at 6 months was seen in 43% versus 27% (p = 0.03). On multivariate analysis survival improved with RPA class 1 (p < 0.0001) and favourable histology (p = 0.0121).

rtog1014.methods: Phase 2, single-arm, prospective trial of three-dimensional conformal external beam partial breast reirradiation after a second lumpectomy. Eligible women had a unifocal ipsilateral breast recurrence smaller than 3 cm more than 1 year after breast-conserving therapy with whole breast irradiation, excised with negative margins. Reirradiation was 1.5 Gy twice daily for 30 treatments over 15 days, 45 Gy total. The study ran from June 2010 to June 2013. Median follow-up was 5.5 years.
rtog1014.results: 65 women were enrolled and 58 were evaluable, mean age 65.1 years. 23 recurrences (40%) were noninvasive and 35 (60%) invasive. 53 tumors (91%) were 2 cm or smaller. Four patients had a further breast recurrence, a 5-year cumulative incidence of 5% (95% CI 1%-13%). Seven underwent ipsilateral mastectomy, a 5-year cumulative incidence of 10% (95% CI 4%-20%). Distant metastasis-free survival and overall survival were both 95%. Four patients (7%) had grade 3 late adverse events.

rtog9804.methods: Randomized phase III trial. Women who underwent lumpectomy for mammogram-detected ductal carcinoma in situ measuring 2.5 cm or less, with final margins of at least 3 mm and low or intermediate nuclear grade, were randomly assigned to whole breast irradiation or to observation. Tamoxifen use was optional. The primary outcome was ipsilateral breast recurrence. Cumulative incidence estimated recurrence, with log-rank and Gray's tests for comparison and Fine-Gray regression for hazard ratios.
rtog9804.results: 636 women were randomly assigned from 1999 to 2006. Median age was 58 years and mean pathologic size was 0.60 cm. Intended tamoxifen use was 69% in both arms, but actual receipt was 58% with radiation versus 66% with observation. At 13.9 years median follow-up, the 15-year cumulative incidence of ipsilateral breast recurrence was 7.1% with radiation versus 15.1% with observation (HR 0.36, 95% CI 0.20 to 0.66). Invasive local recurrence was 5.4% versus 9.5% (HR 0.44).

rxponder.methods: Prospective randomized trial. Women with hormone-receptor-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer, one to three positive axillary lymph nodes, and a 21-gene recurrence score of 25 or lower were assigned to endocrine therapy alone or to chemotherapy plus endocrine therapy. The primary objective was the effect of chemotherapy on invasive disease-free survival and whether that effect varied by recurrence score. Distant relapse-free survival was a secondary end point.
rxponder.results: 5083 women underwent randomization, 33.2% premenopausal and 66.8% postmenopausal, and 5018 participated. Chemotherapy benefit differed by menopausal status (P=0.008). Among postmenopausal women, 5-year invasive disease-free survival was 91.9% with endocrine therapy alone and 91.3% with chemoendocrine therapy (hazard ratio 1.02, 95% CI 0.82 to 1.26, P=0.89). Among premenopausal women it was 89.0% and 93.9% (hazard ratio 0.60, 95% CI 0.43 to 0.83, P=0.002), with distant relapse-free survival hazard ratio 0.58. Relative benefit did not rise with recurrence score.

sabr-comet.methods: Randomized phase II screening trial. Patients had a controlled primary malignancy and one to five metastatic lesions, all amenable to stereotactic ablative radiotherapy.
