They were stratified by number of metastases (1-3 or 4-5) and randomized 1:2 to palliative standard-of-care treatment alone or to standard of care plus stereotactic ablative radiotherapy. The primary end point was overall survival, tested at an alpha of 0.20. Secondary end points were progression-free survival, toxicity and quality of life.
sabr-comet.results: 99 patients were randomized at 10 centers between 2012 and 2016. The commonest primary tumors were breast (18), lung (18), colorectal (18) and prostate (16). Median follow-up was 51 months. The 5-year overall survival rate was 17.7% in the control arm versus 42.3% with added stereotactic ablative radiotherapy (stratified log-rank P=.006). The 5-year progression-free survival rate was 17.3% with radiotherapy, against 3.2% at 4 years in the control arm (P=.001). No new grade 2-5 adverse events occurred.

sacituzumab-govitecan-phase-0-window-stu.methods: Prospective single-centre window-of-opportunity trial. 25 patients aged 18 or older with breast cancer brain metastases or recurrent glioblastoma received a single intravenous dose of sacituzumab govitecan 10 mg/kg one day before resection, then continued on days 1 and 8 of 21-day cycles after recovery. Intratumoral drug concentration was the primary endpoint, with survival, toxicity and biomarkers also assessed.
sacituzumab-govitecan-phase-0-window-stu.results: Median total SN-38 was 249.8 ng/g in breast cancer brain metastases and 104.5 ng/g in recurrent glioblastoma. Progression-free survival was 8 months and 2 months, and overall survival 35.2 months and 9.5 months. Objective response was 38% and 29%. Grade 3 or higher events included neutropenia in 28% and hypokalemia, seizure, thromboembolism, urinary tract infection and lower limb weakness in 8% each. Trop-2 was expressed in 100% of breast and 78% of glioblastoma tumours.

senomac.methods: Noninferiority randomized trial. Patients with clinically node-negative primary T1 to T3 breast cancer and one or two sentinel-node macrometastases larger than 2 mm were assigned 1:1 to completion axillary-lymph-node dissection or to sentinel-node biopsy only. Adjuvant systemic treatment and radiation therapy followed national guidelines. The primary end point was overall survival. This report gives per-protocol and modified intention-to-treat analyses of recurrence-free survival, with a noninferiority margin of 1.44 for the hazard ratio.
senomac.results: 2766 patients were enrolled in five countries between January 2015 and December 2021. The per-protocol population was 2540 patients, 1335 assigned to sentinel-node biopsy only and 1205 to dissection. Nodal radiation therapy was given to 89.9% and 88.4% respectively. Median follow-up was 46.8 months and 191 patients had recurrence or died. Estimated 5-year recurrence-free survival was 89.7% with sentinel-node biopsy only and 88.7% with dissection, country-adjusted hazard ratio 0.89 (95% CI 0.66 to 1.19), P<0.001 for noninferiority.

sentina.methods: Four-arm prospective multicentre cohort study at 103 institutions in Germany and Austria. Women scheduled for neoadjuvant chemotherapy were enrolled. Clinically node-negative patients had sentinel-lymph-node biopsy before chemotherapy (arm A), and those with a positive node had a second biopsy afterwards (arm B). Clinically node-positive patients who converted to node-negative had biopsy plus axillary dissection (arm C). Those still node-positive had dissection alone (arm D). The primary endpoint was the false-negative rate in arm C.
sentina.results: 1737 patients received treatment. Among 1022 women biopsied before chemotherapy the detection rate was 99.1% (1013 of 1022). In arm C the detection rate was 80.1% (474 of 592) and the false-negative rate was 14.2% (32 of 226). The false-negative rate was 24.3% (17 of 70) with one node removed and 18.5% (10 of 54) with two. In arm B the detection rate was 60.8% (219 of 360) and the false-negative rate 51.6% (33 of 64).

serena2.methods: Open-label randomised phase 2 trial at 74 centres in Asia, Europe, the Middle East and North America. Post-menopausal women with oestrogen receptor-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer, performance status 0 or 1, and progression on at least one prior endocrine therapy were randomised 1:1:1:1 to oral camizestrant 75 mg, 150 mg or 300 mg once daily, or intramuscular fulvestrant 500 mg. The primary endpoint was investigator-assessed progression-free survival by intention to treat.
serena2.results: 240 patients were randomly assigned between May 2020 and August 2021: 74 to camizestrant 75 mg, 73 to 150 mg, 20 to 300 mg and 73 to fulvestrant. Median progression-free survival was 7.2 months with 75 mg, 7.7 months with 150 mg and 3.7 months with fulvestrant. Hazard ratios versus fulvestrant were 0.59 (90% CI 0.42-0.82, p=0.017) for 75 mg and 0.64 (0.46-0.89, p=0.0090) for 150 mg. Treatment-related adverse events occurred in 53%, 67% and 18%.

serena6.methods: Double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomised phase 3 trial at 264 centres in 23 countries. Patients on first-line aromatase inhibitor plus CDK4/6 inhibitor for at least 6 months for oestrogen receptor-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer had ctDNA tested for ESR1 mutation every 2-3 months. Those with an ESR1 mutation and no radiological progression were randomised 1:1 to switch to camizestrant 75 mg daily with the same CDK4/6 inhibitor or to continue the aromatase inhibitor. The primary endpoint was investigator-assessed progression-free survival.
serena6.results: 3325 patients were screened and 3256 had at least one ESR1 mutation test. 548 had a positive test and 315 were randomised, 157 to camizestrant plus CDK4/6 inhibitor and 158 to aromatase inhibitor plus CDK4/6 inhibitor. After median follow-up of 23.5 months, median progression-free survival was 16.8 versus 9.2 months (HR 0.45, 95% CI 0.34-0.59). Median second progression-free survival was 25.7 versus 19.1 months (HR 0.63, 0.46-0.86, p=0.0037). Grade 3-4 neutropenia occurred in 27% versus 17%.

shorther.methods: Randomized phase III non-inferiority trial. HER2-positive breast cancer patients with node-positive disease, or node-negative disease with at least one risk factor (tumor over 2 cm, grade 3, lympho-vascular invasion, Ki-67 above 20%, age 35 years or younger, or hormone receptor negativity), were assigned to sequential anthracycline-taxane chemotherapy plus 1 year of trastuzumab (arm A) or plus 9 weeks of trastuzumab (arm B). The primary end point was disease-free survival, with a non-inferiority margin of 1.29.
shorther.results: 1254 patients were randomized, 627 to 1 year and 626 to 9 weeks. Five-year disease-free survival was 88% with 1 year and 85% with 9 weeks, hazard ratio 1.13 (90% CI 0.89 to 1.42), the upper limit crossing the non-inferiority margin. The Bayesian probability of non-inferiority was 80%. Five-year overall survival was 95.2% and 95.0% (hazard ratio 1.07, 90% CI 0.74 to 1.56). Cardiac events were fewer with 9 weeks, risk ratio 0.33.

sofea.methods: Composite multicentre phase 3 trial in the UK and South Korea. Postmenopausal women with hormone receptor-positive locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer progressing on a non-steroidal aromatase inhibitor were randomised 1:1:1 to fulvestrant 500 mg then 250 mg every 28 days plus anastrozole 1 mg, fulvestrant plus matched placebo, or exemestane 25 mg daily. Stratification was by centre and previous setting of aromatase inhibitor use. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival by intention to treat.
sofea.results: 723 patients were randomised between March 2004 and August 2010, 243 to fulvestrant plus anastrozole, 231 to fulvestrant plus placebo and 249 to exemestane. Median progression-free survival was 4.4, 4.8 and 3.4 months. Hazard ratios were 1.00 (95% CI 0.83-1.21, p = 0.98) for the two fulvestrant arms and 0.95 (0.79-1.14, p = 0.56) for fulvestrant plus placebo versus exemestane. 87 serious adverse events were reported and grade 3-4 events were rare.

soft.methods: Premenopausal women with breast cancer were randomly assigned to 5 years of tamoxifen, tamoxifen plus ovarian suppression, or exemestane plus ovarian suppression in SOFT. Randomization was stratified according to receipt of chemotherapy. This report gives updated results from SOFT and from the parallel TEXT trial, in which women received tamoxifen plus ovarian suppression or exemestane plus ovarian suppression.
soft.results: In SOFT, 8-year disease-free survival was 78.9% with tamoxifen alone, 83.2% with tamoxifen plus ovarian suppression, and 85.9% with exemestane plus ovarian suppression (P=0.009 for the first two). Eight-year overall survival was 91.5%, 93.3% and 92.1% (P=0.01 for the same comparison). Grade 3 or higher adverse events occurred in 24.6%, 31.0% and 32.3%. The 12-year report gave disease-free survival of 71.9%, 76.1% and 79.0%, and overall survival of 86.8%, 89.0% and 89.4%.

soft-text.methods: Combined analysis of the SOFT and TEXT trials. 4,690 premenopausal women with estrogen or progesterone receptor-positive early breast cancer were randomly assigned to 5 years of exemestane plus ovarian function suppression or tamoxifen plus ovarian function suppression. This report covers disease-free survival, distant recurrence-free interval and overall survival in the intention-to-treat population after a median follow-up of 13 years.
soft-text.results: 12-year disease-free survival improved by 4.6 percentage points with exemestane plus OFS (HR 0.79, 95% CI 0.70 to 0.90) and distant recurrence-free interval by 1.8 points (HR 0.83, 0.70 to 0.98). 12-year overall survival was 90.1% versus 89.1% (HR 0.93, 0.78 to 1.11). Among patients with HER2-negative tumours, 86.0% of the population, the 12-year overall survival gain was 2.0% (HR 0.85) and 3.3% in those who received chemotherapy.

solar1.methods: Randomized phase 3 trial comparing alpelisib 300 mg per day plus fulvestrant 500 mg with placebo plus fulvestrant in patients with hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer who had received endocrine therapy previously. Patients were enrolled into two cohorts on the basis of tumour tissue PIK3CA mutation status. The primary end point was investigator-assessed progression-free survival in the mutated cohort. Secondary end points included overall response and safety.
solar1.results: 572 patients underwent randomization, including 341 with confirmed PIK3CA mutations. In the mutated cohort median progression-free survival at a median follow-up of 20 months was 11.0 months with alpelisib versus 5.7 months with placebo (HR 0.65, 95% CI 0.50 to 0.85). The hazard ratio in the non-mutated cohort was 0.85. Grade 3 or 4 hyperglycaemia occurred in 36.6% versus 0.7%. The final overall survival report gave 39.3 versus 31.4 months (HR 0.86).

sold.methods: Open-label trial that randomly assigned 2,176 women with HER2-positive early breast cancer 1:1 between 2008 and 2014 in seven countries. All received three cycles of three-weekly docetaxel, 80 or 100 mg/m2, plus trastuzumab for 9 weeks, then three cycles of fluorouracil, epirubicin and cyclophosphamide. The 9-week group received no further trastuzumab. Controls continued trastuzumab to 1 year. Disease-free survival was compared with a non-inferiority margin of 1.3.
sold.results: 2,174 women were analysed, median age 56 years, median follow-up 5.2 years. Non-inferiority of the 9-week treatment was not demonstrated for disease-free survival (hazard ratio 1.39, 2-sided 90% CI 1.12 to 1.72). Distant disease-free survival and overall survival did not differ substantially. Cardiac failure occurred in 36 patients (3%) in the 1-year group and 21 (2%) in the 9-week group. Patients given 80 mg/m2 docetaxel had inferior disease-free survival.

sole.methods: Multicentre open-label phase 3 trial at 240 centres in 22 countries. Postmenopausal women with hormone receptor-positive, node-positive operable breast cancer who had completed 4 to 6 years of adjuvant endocrine therapy were randomised 1:1 to continuous letrozole 2.5 mg daily for 5 years or intermittent letrozole for 9 months with a 3-month break in years 1 to 4 and continuous dosing in year 5. The primary endpoint was disease-free survival by intention to treat.
sole.results: 4884 women were enrolled and 4851 formed the intention-to-treat population, 2425 intermittent and 2426 continuous. At a median follow-up of 60 months, disease-free survival was 85.8% versus 87.5% (hazard ratio 1.08, 95% CI 0.93-1.26, p = 0.31). The final analysis at 84 months gave 7-year disease-free survival of 81.4% versus 81.5% (hazard ratio 1.03, 95% CI 0.91-1.17). Grade 3-5 hypertension occurred in 24% versus 21%.

sonia.methods: Phase 3 trial that randomized 1,050 patients with hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer who had received no previous therapy for advanced disease to a CDK4/6 inhibitor in the first-line or the second-line setting. All patients received the same endocrine therapy, an aromatase inhibitor first line and fulvestrant second line. The primary end point was time from randomization to disease progression after second-line treatment, PFS2.
sonia.results: Median PFS2 was 31.0 months with first-line use and 26.8 months with second-line use (hazard ratio 0.87, 95% CI 0.74 to 1.03, P = 0.10). Health-related quality of life was similar. Median CDK4/6 inhibitor treatment duration was 24.6 versus 8.1 months, with 2,763 versus 1,591 grade 3 or higher adverse events. The later overall survival report gave median overall survival of 47.9 versus 48.1 months (HR 0.91).

sophia.methods: Final overall survival analysis of a randomized phase 3 trial in previously treated HER2-positive advanced breast cancer. 536 patients in the intention-to-treat population were assigned to margetuximab 15 mg/kg every 3 weeks plus chemotherapy (n = 266) or trastuzumab 6 mg/kg every 3 weeks after an 8 mg/kg loading dose plus chemotherapy (n = 270). Primary end points were progression-free survival, reported earlier, and overall survival. The analysis was triggered by 385 prespecified events.
sophia.results: Median overall survival was 21.6 months with margetuximab versus 21.9 months with trastuzumab (hazard ratio 0.95, 95% CI 0.77 to 1.17, P = .620). Preplanned exploratory CD16A genotyping suggested better overall survival with margetuximab in CD16A-158FF patients (23.6 versus 19.2 months, HR 0.72) and better overall survival with trastuzumab in CD16A-158VV patients (31.1 versus 22.0 months, HR 1.77, 95% CI 1.01 to 3.12). Safety was comparable.

sound.methods: Prospective phase 3 noninferiority randomised trial in Italy, Switzerland, Spain and Chile. 1463 women of any age with breast cancer up to 2 cm and a negative preoperative axillary ultrasonography result were enrolled between February 2012 and June 2017. Patients were randomised 1:1 to sentinel lymph node biopsy or no axillary surgery. The primary endpoint was 5-year distant disease-free survival analysed as intention to treat.
sound.results: 1405 women were analysed by intention to treat, 708 assigned to sentinel lymph node biopsy and 697 to no axillary surgery. 97 patients (13.7%) in the biopsy group had positive axillary nodes. Median follow-up was 5.7 years. Five-year distant disease-free survival was 97.7% with biopsy and 98.0% without axillary surgery (hazard ratio 0.84, noninferiority P = .02). There were 21 deaths in the biopsy group and 18 in the no axillary surgery group.

srs-plus-nivolumab.methods: Non-randomised open-label phase Ib study. Patients aged 18 or older with breast cancer brain metastases of any subtype, ECOG performance status 2 or better and 10 or fewer brain metastases received nivolumab 480 mg intravenously every 4 weeks, with stereotactic radiosurgery one week after the first dose. Blood was collected at baseline and every 4 weeks for flow cytometry and cell-free DNA assessment.
srs-plus-nivolumab.results: 12 patients received radiosurgery to 17 brain metastases, 50% triple negative, 33% HR+/HER2- and 17% HR-/HER2+. At a median follow-up of 56 months there was no radionecrosis. Two lesions failed locally, for 12-month local control of 94%. Median distant intracranial control was 7.4 months, systemic progression-free survival 7.7 months and overall survival 24.7 months. Intracranial control was associated with lower CD4 regulatory T cells and higher CD4 effector memory T cells.

stage.methods: Double-blind, randomised, parallel-group, multicentre phase 3 trial. Premenopausal women with ER positive, HER2 negative operable breast cancer were assigned 1:1 to goserelin 3.6 mg monthly plus either anastrozole 1 mg daily or tamoxifen 20 mg daily, with matching placebo, for 24 weeks before surgery. Randomisation was stratified by centre and all study personnel were masked. The primary endpoint was best overall tumour response in the intention-to-treat population, tested for non-inferiority and then superiority.
stage.results: 204 patients were enrolled and 197 randomised, 98 to anastrozole and 99 to tamoxifen. 185 completed 24 weeks of treatment and had surgery. Response occurred in 70.4 percent with anastrozole and 50.5 percent with tamoxifen, difference 19.9 percent, 95 percent CI 6.5 to 33.3, p=0.004. Treatment-related grade 3 events occurred in two anastrozole patients and one tamoxifen patient. One serious adverse event occurred in the anastrozole group.

start.methods: Prespecified 10-year analysis of two randomized trials. From 1999 to 2002, women with completely excised invasive breast cancer (pT1-3a, pN0-1, M0) were enrolled at 35 UK radiotherapy centres and randomly assigned after primary surgery. START-A compared 50 Gy in 25 fractions over 5 weeks with 41.6 Gy or 39 Gy in 13 fractions. START-B compared 50 Gy with 40 Gy in 15 fractions over 3 weeks. Primary endpoints were local-regional relapse and late normal tissue effects.
start.results: START-A enrolled 2,236 women, median follow-up 9.3 years, with 139 local-regional relapses. 10-year local-regional relapse rates were 6.3% with 41.6 Gy, 8.8% with 39 Gy and 7.4% with 50 Gy (HR 0.91 and 1.18 versus 50 Gy). START-B enrolled 2,215 women, median follow-up 9.9 years, with 95 relapses and 10-year rates of 4.3% with 40 Gy versus 5.5% with 50 Gy (HR 0.77). Normal tissue effects were less common with 39 Gy and 40 Gy.

study301.methods: Phase III open-label randomized study. Women with locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer who had received prior anthracycline- and taxane-based therapy were randomly assigned to eribulin or capecitabine as their first-, second- or third-line chemotherapy for advanced or metastatic disease. Stratification factors were HER2 status and geographic region. Coprimary end points were overall survival and progression-free survival.
study301.results: Median overall survival was 15.9 months with eribulin (n = 554) and 14.5 months with capecitabine (n = 548) (hazard ratio 0.88, 95% CI 0.77 to 1.00, P = .056). Median progression-free survival was 4.1 and 4.2 months (hazard ratio 1.08, 95% CI 0.93 to 1.25, P = .30). Objective response rates were 11.0% and 11.5%. Global health status and overall quality-of-life scores over time were similar.

summit.methods: Report of 71 patients with hormone receptor-positive, HER2-mutant metastatic breast cancer in the SUMMIT basket study, including 21 from a randomized substudy. Patients with activating HER2 mutations and prior CDK4/6 inhibitor therapy received neratinib 240 mg per day with loperamide prophylaxis plus fulvestrant and trastuzumab, or fulvestrant plus trastuzumab, or fulvestrant alone, with cross-over allowed on progression. Endpoints included objective response rate, clinical benefit rate, duration of response and progression-free survival.
summit.results: Objective response rate for the 57 patients given neratinib, fulvestrant and trastuzumab was 39% (95% CI 26% to 52%), and median progression-free survival was 8.3 months (95% CI 6.0 to 15.1). No responses occurred with fulvestrant alone or fulvestrant plus trastuzumab. Patients crossing over to the triplet responded. Responses occurred with ductal and lobular histology, one or more HER2 mutations and co-occurring HER3 mutations. Circulating tumour DNA showed acquired HER2 and PIK3CA alterations.

swog-8814-int-0100.methods: Open-label phase 3 trial in postmenopausal women with hormone receptor positive, node positive breast cancer. Patients were randomised 2:3:3 to tamoxifen alone for five years, to six cycles of CAF every four weeks followed by tamoxifen, or to CAF with concurrent tamoxifen. The primary endpoint was disease-free survival, addressing chemotherapy benefit and then tamoxifen timing. Overall survival and toxicity were predefined secondary outcomes. Analysis was by intention to treat among eligible patients using stratified log-rank tests and adjusted Cox regression.
swog-8814-int-0100.results: Of 1558 randomised women, 1477 were eligible for analysis. Median follow-up was 8.94 years and 637 had a disease-free survival event. CAF plus tamoxifen beat tamoxifen alone for disease-free survival, hazard ratio 0.76, 95 percent CI 0.64 to 0.91, p=0.002, and marginally for overall survival, hazard ratio 0.83, p=0.057. Sequential versus concurrent tamoxifen gave hazard ratio 0.84, p=0.061. Neutropenia, stomatitis, thromboembolism, heart failure and leukaemia were more frequent with chemotherapy.

swog-s0226.methods: Phase 3 randomised trial. Postmenopausal women with previously untreated hormone receptor positive metastatic breast cancer were assigned 1:1 to anastrozole 1 mg daily, with crossover to fulvestrant at progression strongly encouraged, or to anastrozole plus fulvestrant. Fulvestrant was given intramuscularly at 500 mg on day 1 and 250 mg on days 14 and 28 and monthly thereafter. Randomisation was stratified by prior adjuvant tamoxifen. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival, with overall survival prespecified as secondary.
swog-s0226.results: Median progression-free survival was 15.0 months with the combination and 13.5 months with anastrozole alone, hazard ratio 0.80, 95 percent CI 0.68 to 0.94, p=0.007. Median overall survival was 47.7 versus 41.3 months, hazard ratio 0.81, p=0.05, despite 41 percent crossover. In the final analysis of 694 patients, median overall survival was 49.8 versus 42.0 months, hazard ratio 0.82. Grade 3 to 5 toxicity rates were similar.

swog-s0500.methods: Patients with metastatic breast cancer starting first-line chemotherapy were grouped by circulating tumour cell count, increased meaning five or more cells per 7.5 mL of whole blood. Those without increased counts at baseline stayed on initial therapy (arm A). Those whose counts fell by day 21 also stayed on it (arm B). Those with persistently increased counts were randomly assigned to continue initial therapy (arm C1) or change to alternative chemotherapy (arm C2). The primary outcome was overall survival.
swog-s0500.results: Of 595 eligible and evaluable patients, 276 (46%) had no increased counts (arm A). Of those with increased counts, 31 (10%) were not retested, 165 went to arm B and 123 were randomly assigned to arm C1 or C2. Median overall survival was 10.7 months in arm C1 versus 12.5 months in arm C2 (P = .98), and 35, 23 and 13 months in arms A, B and C (P < .001).

sysucc-002.methods: Open-label, noninferiority phase 3 randomised trial at nine hospitals in China. Patients were stratified by previous adjuvant endocrine therapy and by recurrent versus de novo metastatic disease, then assigned 1:1 to trastuzumab plus endocrine therapy, using investigator's choice of oestrogen receptor modulator or aromatase inhibitor with or without ovarian suppression, or to trastuzumab plus chemotherapy, using investigator's choice of taxane, capecitabine or vinorelbine. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival with a noninferiority margin of 1.35, analysed by intention to treat.
sysucc-002.results: 392 patients were randomised, 196 to each group. After a median follow-up of 30.2 months, interquartile range 15.0 to 44.7, median progression-free survival was 19.2 months, 95 percent CI 16.7 to 21.7, with endocrine therapy and 14.8 months, 95 percent CI 12.8 to 16.8, with chemotherapy. The hazard ratio was 0.88, 95 percent CI 0.71 to 1.09, noninferiority p less than 0.0001. Toxicity was significantly more prevalent in the chemotherapy group.

sysucc001.methods: Randomized trial at 13 academic centres and clinical sites in China from April 2010 to December 2016. 443 patients with early-stage triple-negative breast cancer who had completed standard adjuvant chemotherapy were randomized 1:1 to capecitabine 650 mg/m2 twice a day by mouth for 1 year without interruption (n = 222) or to observation (n = 221). The primary end point was disease-free survival. Secondary end points included distant disease-free survival, overall survival and locoregional recurrence-free survival.
sysucc001.results: 434 women formed the full analysis set, mean age 46 years, 61.8% node-negative, median follow-up 61 months. 94 events occurred, 38 in the capecitabine group and 56 in the observation group. Estimated 5-year disease-free survival was 82.8% versus 73.0% (hazard ratio 0.64, 95% CI 0.42 to 0.95, P = .03), distant disease-free survival 85.8% versus 75.8% (HR 0.60) and overall survival 85.5% versus 81.3% (HR 0.75). Hand-foot syndrome affected 45.2%.

tailorx.methods: Prospective trial involving 10,273 women with hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative, axillary node-negative breast cancer. Of the 9,719 eligible patients with follow-up information, 6,711 (69%) had a midrange 21-gene recurrence score of 11 to 25 and were randomly assigned to chemoendocrine therapy or endocrine therapy alone. The trial was designed to show non-inferiority of endocrine therapy alone for invasive disease-free survival, defined as freedom from invasive recurrence, second primary cancer or death.
tailorx.results: Endocrine therapy was non-inferior to chemoendocrine therapy for invasive disease-free survival (hazard ratio 1.08, 95% CI 0.94 to 1.24, P = 0.26). At 9 years the groups had similar invasive disease-free survival (83.3% versus 84.3%), freedom from distant recurrence (94.5% and 95.0%), freedom from distant or local-regional recurrence (92.2% and 92.9%) and overall survival (93.9% and 93.8%). Chemotherapy benefit varied with recurrence score and age, with some benefit in women 50 or younger scoring 16 to 25.

tam01.methods: 10-year follow-up of a phase III placebo-controlled trial. 500 women with breast intraepithelial neoplasia, comprising atypical ductal hyperplasia, lobular carcinoma in situ, or hormone-sensitive or unknown ductal carcinoma in situ, were randomly assigned after surgery with or without irradiation to low-dose tamoxifen 5 mg once daily for 3 years or placebo. The primary end point was the incidence of invasive breast cancer or ductal carcinoma in situ.
tam01.results: The population was 20% atypical ductal hyperplasia, 11% lobular carcinoma in situ and 69% ductal carcinoma in situ, mean age 54 years. After a median follow-up of 9.7 years, 66 breast cancers were diagnosed, 25 with tamoxifen and 41 with placebo (11.3 versus 19.5 per 1,000 person-years, hazard ratio 0.58, 95% CI 0.35 to 0.95). Contralateral cancers numbered six versus 16 (HR 0.36). In the DCIS cohort the HR was 0.50.

tandem.methods: Randomised phase 3 trial. Postmenopausal women with HER2 positive and hormone receptor positive metastatic breast cancer were assigned to anastrozole 1 mg daily with or without trastuzumab, given as a 4 mg/kg intravenous loading dose on day 1 then 2 mg/kg every week, until progression. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival in the intention-to-treat population.
tandem.results: 103 patients received trastuzumab plus anastrozole and 104 received anastrozole alone. Median progression-free survival was 4.8 versus 2.4 months, hazard ratio 0.63, 95 percent CI 0.47 to 0.84, p=0.0016. Among 150 patients with centrally confirmed hormone receptor positivity it was 5.6 versus 3.8 months, p=0.006. Grade 3 and grade 4 events occurred in 23 and 5 percent with the combination versus 15 and 1 percent with anastrozole alone.

tbcrc-022.methods: Multicenter phase 2 study, cohort 4. Patients with measurable HER2 positive breast cancer brain metastases received neratinib 160 mg daily plus ado-trastuzumab emtansine 3.6 mg/kg intravenously every 21 days in three parallel enrolling cohorts: 4A with previously untreated brain metastases, 4B progressing after local central nervous system therapy without prior T-DM1, and 4C with prior T-DM1. Diarrhoea prophylaxis was required in cycle 1. The primary endpoint was central nervous system response by RANO-BM in each cohort.
tbcrc-022.results: Between 2018 and 2021, 6, 17 and 21 patients enrolled in cohorts 4A, 4B and 4C, and enrolment stopped early for slow accrual. Central nervous system objective response rates were 33.3, 35.3 and 28.6 percent. Between 38.1 and 50 percent had response or stable disease for at least six months. Grade 3 diarrhoea occurred in 22.7 percent. Median overall survival was 30.2, 23.3 and 20.9 months.

tbcrc-049.methods: Phase 2, nonrandomised, single-arm, multicenter study. Women with magnetic resonance imaging confirmed newly diagnosed leptomeningeal metastasis and HER2 positive breast cancer received tucatinib, trastuzumab and capecitabine. The primary endpoint was overall survival, compared against a historical control of 4.4 months at a prespecified interim efficacy threshold. Secondary endpoints were central nervous system progression-free survival, leptomeningeal objective response, neurological symptom improvement, pharmacokinetics and safety.
tbcrc-049.results: 17 women enrolled, 15 were symptomatic and 8 had abnormal cerebrospinal fluid cytology. At a median follow-up of 18 months, 6 of 17 remained alive and median overall survival was 10 months, 95 percent CI 4.1 to not reached. Median time to central nervous system progression was 6.9 months, 95 percent CI 2.8 to 13.8. 5 of 13 evaluable patients had a composite leptomeningeal response and 7 of 12 had improved neurological deficits. Tucatinib reached therapeutic cerebrospinal fluid levels.

tbcrc006.methods: Multicentre phase II study. Women with stage II to III HER2-positive breast cancer received weekly trastuzumab (4 mg/kg loading, then 2 mg/kg) and lapatinib 1000 mg once daily for 12 weeks, without chemotherapy. Women with ER-positive tumours also received letrozole, plus a luteinizing hormone-releasing hormone agonist if premenopausal. Pathologic response was assessed by ER status. Biopsies were taken at baseline, at weeks 2 and 8, and at surgery.
tbcrc006.results: Sixty-six patients were enrolled. Sixty-four were eligible and evaluable for response. Median tumour size was 6 cm (range 1.5 to 30 cm). In-breast pathologic complete response (ypT0-is) was 27% overall, 21% in ER-positive and 36% in ER-negative disease. Low-volume residual disease (ypT1a-b) occurred in 22% overall, 33% ER-positive and 4% ER-negative. Adverse events were mainly grade 1 to 2. Grade 3 metabolic, gastrointestinal and liver toxicity affected 12 patients (18%).

tbcrc048.methods: Investigator-initiated phase II study of olaparib in metastatic breast cancer with measurable disease. Cohort 1 had germline mutations in homologous recombination related genes. Cohort 2 had somatic mutations in those genes. Prior PARP inhibitor use, platinum-refractory disease, or progression on more than two chemotherapy regimens for metastatic disease were not allowed. Patients received olaparib 300 mg orally twice a day until progression. A single-arm, two-stage design was used. The primary endpoint was objective response rate.
tbcrc048.results: Fifty-four patients enrolled. Seventy-six percent had oestrogen receptor-positive HER2-negative disease. Objective response rate was 33% (90% CI 19% to 51%) in cohort 1 and 31% (90% CI 15% to 49%) in cohort 2. Confirmed responses were seen in only two mutation groups, with response rates of 82% and 50%. Median progression-free survival was 13.3 months (90% CI 12 months to not available) and 6.3 months (90% CI 4.4 months to not available) in those two groups.

team.methods: Open-label phase 3 trial conducted in hospitals in nine countries. Postmenopausal women with hormone-receptor-positive breast cancer, median age 64 years (range 35 to 96), were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to oral exemestane 25 mg once a day alone or to the same exemestane following tamoxifen 20 mg once a day, for 5 years. Randomisation used a computer-generated random permuted block method. The primary endpoint was disease-free survival at 5 years, analysed by intention to treat.
team.results: 9779 patients were assigned to sequential treatment (n=4875) or exemestane alone (n=4904), with 4868 and 4898 analysed by intention to treat. At 5 years, 4154 (85%) of the sequential group and 4186 (86%) of the exemestane alone group were disease free (hazard ratio 0.97, 95% CI 0.88 to 1.08, p=0.60). Sequential treatment carried more gynaecological symptoms, venous thrombosis and endometrial abnormalities. Exemestane alone carried more musculoskeletal events, hypertension and hyperlipidaemia.

th3resa.methods: Randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial in medical centres in 22 countries. Eligible patients were aged 18 years or older with progressive HER2-positive advanced breast cancer after two or more HER2-directed regimens, including trastuzumab and lapatinib, plus previous taxane therapy. Randomisation was 2:1 to trastuzumab emtansine 3.6 mg/kg intravenously every 21 days or treatment of physician's choice, stratified by world region, number of previous regimens and visceral disease. Coprimary endpoints were investigator-assessed progression-free survival and overall survival.
th3resa.results: 602 patients were randomly assigned, 404 to trastuzumab emtansine and 198 to physician's choice. Median progression-free survival was 6.2 months versus 3.3 months (stratified hazard ratio 0.528, 95% CI 0.422 to 0.661, p<0.0001). The interim overall survival analysis favoured trastuzumab emtansine (stratified hazard ratio 0.552, 95% CI 0.369 to 0.826, p=0.0034) without crossing the stopping boundary. The 2017 final overall survival report gave median 22.7 months versus 15.8 months, hazard ratio 0.68 (95% CI 0.54 to 0.85).

tnt.methods: Phase 3 randomised trial in patients with unselected advanced triple-negative breast cancer. Carboplatin was compared with docetaxel. A prespecified protocol allowed biomarker by treatment interaction analyses in germline BRCA1/2 carriers and in BRCAness subgroups defined by BRCA1 methylation, low BRCA1 mRNA, a Myriad homologous recombination deficiency score, and basal-like phenotype. The primary endpoint was objective response rate.
tnt.results: Among 376 patients, 188 received carboplatin and 188 received docetaxel. Objective response rate was 31.4% versus 34.0%, P = 0.66. In germline BRCA1/2 carriers response was 68% with carboplatin versus 33% with docetaxel, interaction P = 0.01. No such benefit was seen with BRCA1 methylation, BRCA1 mRNA-low tumours or high Myriad homologous recombination deficiency score. The basal-like interaction was driven by high docetaxel response in nonbasal tumours.

torchlight.methods: Randomised double-blinded phase 3 trial of first-line toripalimab plus nab-paclitaxel in 353 women against placebo plus nab-paclitaxel in 178 women with metastatic or recurrent triple-negative breast cancer. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival assessed by blinded independent central review in the PD-L1-positive and intention-to-treat populations. Secondary endpoints included overall survival and safety.
torchlight.results: PD-L1-positive disease was present in 200 patients in the toripalimab arm and 100 in the placebo arm. At the prespecified interim analysis median progression-free survival in the PD-L1-positive population was 8.4 versus 5.6 months, hazard ratio 0.65, P = 0.0102. Median overall survival was 32.8 versus 19.5 months, hazard ratio 0.62, P = 0.0148. Grade 3 or worse treatment-emergent adverse events occurred in 56.4% versus 54.3%, and fatal events in 0.6% versus 3.4%.

train-3.methods: Single-arm phase 2 study across 43 hospitals in the Netherlands. Patients received paclitaxel, trastuzumab, carboplatin and pertuzumab for up to nine cycles and were referred for surgery once MRI showed a complete radiological response. Patients with a pathological complete response completed one year of trastuzumab and pertuzumab. Patients with residual invasive disease completed nine cycles then received 14 cycles of trastuzumab emtansine. The primary endpoint was three-year event-free survival.
train-3.results: 235 patients with hormone receptor-negative and 232 with hormone receptor-positive tumours were enrolled. Median follow-up was 40.1 months. Three-year event-free survival was 92.2% and 92.0% respectively, with 40 events in 467 patients. By cycles given, event-free survival was 96.1% and 98.6% after one to three cycles, 89.2% and 94.2% after four to six, and 90.6% and 85.4% after seven to nine. Grade 3-4 neutropenia affected 40%.

train2.methods: Secondary analysis of an open-label, randomised phase 3 trial at 37 hospitals in the Netherlands. 438 patients with stage II and III ERBB2-positive breast cancer were randomised 1:1, stratified by age, tumour stage, nodal stage and oestrogen receptor status, to three cycles of fluorouracil, epirubicin and cyclophosphamide then six cycles of paclitaxel and carboplatin, or to nine cycles of paclitaxel and carboplatin. Both groups received trastuzumab and pertuzumab every three weeks. Outcomes were 3-year event-free survival and overall survival.
train2.results: Median follow-up was 48.8 months (interquartile range 44.1 to 55.2). There were 23 event-free survival events (10.5%) in the anthracycline group and 21 (9.6%) in the non-anthracycline group (hazard ratio 0.90, 95% CI 0.50 to 1.63). Three-year event-free survival was 92.7% with anthracyclines and 93.6% without. Three-year overall survival was 97.7% and 98.2%. A left ventricular ejection fraction decline of 10% or more to below 50% occurred in 7.7% versus 3.2% (P=.04).

tropics02.methods: Randomised, open-label, multicentre phase 3 trial at 91 centres in North America and Europe. Patients with hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative locally recurrent inoperable or metastatic breast cancer who had received at least one previous endocrine therapy, a taxane and a CDK4/6 inhibitor, plus two to four previous chemotherapy regimens for metastatic disease, were randomly assigned 1:1 to sacituzumab govitecan or chemotherapy (eribulin, vinorelbine, capecitabine or gemcitabine). This report is the final overall survival analysis.
tropics02.results: 543 patients were randomly assigned, 272 to sacituzumab govitecan and 271 to chemotherapy. With a median follow-up of 12.5 months, 390 deaths had occurred. Median overall survival was 14.4 months versus 11.2 months (hazard ratio 0.79, 95% CI 0.65 to 0.96, p=0.020), consistent across Trop-2 expression subgroups. Objective response rate was 21% versus 14% (odds ratio 1.63, p=0.035). The 2022 primary analysis reported median progression-free survival of 5.5 months versus 4.0 months, hazard ratio 0.66.

tropion-b01.methods: Global, open-label, randomised phase 3 trial. Adults with inoperable or metastatic hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer who had progressed on endocrine therapy or for whom it was unsuitable, and who had received one to two previous lines of chemotherapy in that setting, were randomly assigned 1:1 to datopotamab deruxtecan 6 mg/kg every 3 weeks or investigator's choice chemotherapy (eribulin, vinorelbine, capecitabine or gemcitabine). Dual primary endpoints were progression-free survival by blinded independent central review and overall survival.
tropion-b01.results: 365 patients were assigned to datopotamab deruxtecan and 367 to investigator's choice chemotherapy. Progression-free survival by blinded review favoured datopotamab deruxtecan (hazard ratio 0.63, 95% CI 0.52 to 0.76, p<0.0001), with consistent benefit across subgroups. Overall survival data were immature, with a hazard ratio of 0.84 (95% CI 0.62 to 1.14). Grade 3 or worse treatment-related adverse events occurred in 20.8% versus 44.7%. Commonest were nausea (51.1%) and stomatitis (50%) with datopotamab deruxtecan, neutropenia (42.5%) with chemotherapy.

tropion-b02.methods: Randomised, open-label, international phase III trial. Patients with previously untreated, locally recurrent inoperable or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer for whom immunotherapy was not an option were randomly assigned 1:1 to datopotamab deruxtecan 6 mg/kg intravenously every 3 weeks or to investigator's choice of chemotherapy. Randomisation was stratified by geographic location, disease-free interval and programmed cell death ligand-1 status. Dual primary endpoints were progression-free survival by blinded independent central review and overall survival. Efficacy was analysed by intention to treat.
tropion-b02.results: Between 16 May 2022 and 11 June 2024, 644 patients were randomly assigned, 323 to datopotamab deruxtecan and 321 to chemotherapy. Median progression-free survival was 10.8 months versus 5.6 months (hazard ratio 0.57, 99% CI 0.44 to 0.73, P<0.0001). Median overall survival was 23.7 months versus 18.7 months (hazard ratio 0.79, 95.01% CI 0.64 to 0.98, P=0.029). Grade 3 or worse treatment-related adverse events affected 105 patients (33%) and 89 patients (29%). There were no treatment-related deaths.

tropion-b03.methods: Ongoing randomised phase III global trial in patients aged 18 years or older with stage I to III triple-negative breast cancer and residual invasive disease at surgical resection after neoadjuvant treatment. Patients are randomised 2:1:2 to datopotamab deruxtecan 6 mg/kg intravenously every 3 weeks for eight cycles plus durvalumab 1120 mg every 3 weeks for nine cycles, to datopotamab deruxtecan monotherapy, or to investigator's choice of capecitabine, pembrolizumab, or both. The primary endpoint is invasive disease-free survival.

tryphaena.methods: Multicentre, open-label phase II cardiac safety study. Patients with operable, locally advanced or inflammatory HER2-positive breast cancer were randomised 1:1:1 to six neoadjuvant cycles every 3 weeks. Arm A gave fluorouracil, epirubicin and cyclophosphamide with trastuzumab and pertuzumab for three cycles, then docetaxel with both antibodies. Arm B gave the same chemotherapy alone for three cycles, then docetaxel with both antibodies. Arm C gave docetaxel, carboplatin, trastuzumab and pertuzumab. Adjuvant treatment completed one year of trastuzumab.
tryphaena.results: Two hundred twenty-five patients were randomised. During neoadjuvant treatment two patients (2.7%, arm B) had symptomatic left ventricular systolic dysfunction. Eleven patients had ejection fraction declines of 10 points or more from baseline to below 50% (four in arm A, four in arm B, three in arm C). Pathologic complete response (ypT0/is) was 61.6% in arm A, 57.3% in arm B, 66.2% in arm C. The 2017 long-term analysis gave 3-year disease-free survival of 87%, 88% and 90%.

tutor.methods: Prospective single-arm multicentre phase 1 trial at six United States centres. Eligible patients are aged 18 or older with ECOG 0 to 2 and up to ten newly diagnosed brain metastases. Any number of prior systemic therapies is allowed except tucatinib or capecitabine. Patients receive oral tucatinib alongside stereotactic radiosurgery and a two-week dose-limiting toxicity period, then capecitabine on days 1 to 14 and trastuzumab on day 1 of each 21-day cycle. A 3+3 de-escalation design starts at 300 mg.

tuxedo-1.methods: Prospective open-label single-arm phase 2 trial. Patients aged 18 years or older with HER2-positive breast cancer and newly diagnosed untreated brain metastases or brain metastases progressing after local therapy, with previous trastuzumab and pertuzumab and no indication for immediate local therapy, received trastuzumab deruxtecan 5.4 mg/kg every three weeks. The primary endpoint was intracranial response rate. A Simon two-stage design tested a null response rate below 26% against 61%.
tuxedo-1.results: Fifteen patients were treated. Two patients (13.3%) had a complete intracranial response, nine (60%) a partial response and three (20%) stable disease, giving a best intracranial response rate of 73.3%, 95% CI 48.1 to 89.1. No new safety signals were seen and quality of life and cognitive function were maintained. At final analysis with 26.5 months median follow-up, median progression-free survival was 21 months and median overall survival was not reached.

us-oncology-9735.methods: Patients with early breast cancer were randomly assigned to four cycles of doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide at 60 and 600 mg/m2 (n = 510) or four cycles of docetaxel and cyclophosphamide at 75 and 600 mg/m2 (n = 506), each given intravenously every three weeks. This report covers seven-year disease-free and overall survival and the effect of age, hormone receptor status and HER2 status on outcome and toxicity.
us-oncology-9735.results: Median age was 50 years in women younger than 65 and 69 years in those 65 or older, with more nodal involvement in older women. At seven years disease-free survival was 81% with docetaxel and cyclophosphamide versus 75%, hazard ratio 0.74, P = 0.033, and overall survival 87% versus 82%, hazard ratio 0.69, P = 0.032. The advantage held in older and younger patients. No interaction was seen with hormone receptor or HER2 status.

veritac2.methods: Phase 3, open-label, randomised trial enrolling patients with oestrogen receptor-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer who had received one previous line of CDK4/6 inhibitor therapy plus one line of endocrine therapy, and up to one additional line of endocrine therapy. Patients were randomly assigned 1:1 to vepdegestrant 200 mg orally once daily in 28-day cycles or fulvestrant 500 mg intramuscularly, stratified by mutation status and visceral disease. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival by blinded independent central review.
veritac2.results: 624 patients underwent randomisation, 313 to vepdegestrant and 311 to fulvestrant. Among the 270 patients with mutations, median progression-free survival was 5.0 months (95% CI 3.7 to 7.4) with vepdegestrant and 2.1 months (95% CI 1.9 to 3.5) with fulvestrant (hazard ratio 0.58, 95% CI 0.43 to 0.78, P<0.001). Among all patients it was 3.8 months versus 3.6 months (hazard ratio 0.83, 95% CI 0.69 to 1.01, P=0.07). Grade 3 or higher adverse events occurred in 23.4% and 17.6%.

viktoria1.methods: Phase III randomised trial in patients with hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative, PIK3CA wild-type advanced breast cancer whose disease progressed during or after CDK4/6 inhibitor and aromatase inhibitor treatment. Patients were randomly assigned 1:1:1 to gedatolisib with palbociclib and fulvestrant, to gedatolisib with fulvestrant, or to fulvestrant monotherapy. The primary objective was progression-free survival by blinded independent central review, comparing each gedatolisib group with fulvestrant.
viktoria1.results: 392 patients were randomly assigned. Median study follow-up was 10.1 months. Median progression-free survival was 9.3 months in the gedatolisib triplet group, 7.4 months in the gedatolisib doublet group and 2.0 months in the fulvestrant group. Hazard ratios for progression or death versus fulvestrant were 0.24 (95% CI 0.17 to 0.35) for the triplet and 0.33 (95% CI 0.24 to 0.48) for the doublet, both P<.001. Grade 3 or higher neutropenia was 62.3% and 0.8%.

wbrt-with-or-without-temozolomide.methods: Multicentre prospective randomised phase 2 study in patients with newly diagnosed intraparenchymal brain metastases from breast cancer unsuitable for surgery or radiosurgery. All patients received conformal whole-brain radiation therapy of 3 Gy fractions to 10 to 30 Gy, with or without concomitant temozolomide 75 mg/m2 daily during irradiation. The primary endpoint was objective response rate at six weeks on brain MRI by modified WHO criteria. Secondary endpoints were progression-free survival, overall survival, neurologic symptoms and tolerability.
wbrt-with-or-without-temozolomide.results: 100 patients were enrolled between February 2008 and November 2010, 50 per arm. Median age was 55 years and median follow-up 9.4 months. Objective response rate at six weeks was 36% with whole-brain radiation alone and 30% with added temozolomide, not significant. Median progression-free survival was 7.4 months versus 6.9 months and median overall survival 11.1 months versus 9.4 months. The most common grade 2 or worse acute toxicity was reversible lymphopenia.

wsg-adapt-hr-her2.methods: Trial combining the 21-gene recurrence score with response to three weeks of preoperative endocrine therapy to guide systemic treatment. Baseline and post-endocrine Ki67 were assessed centrally. Patients with none to three involved nodes received endocrine therapy alone, in the control arm if recurrence score was 11 or lower and in the experimental arm if recurrence score was 12 to 25 with endocrine response, meaning Ki67 of 10% or less. All other patients received dose-dense chemotherapy then endocrine therapy.
wsg-adapt-hr-her2.results: The intention-to-treat population was 2,290 patients, 1,422 experimental and 868 control. Five-year invasive disease-free survival was 92.6% versus 93.9%, five-year distant disease-free survival 95.6% versus 96.3% and five-year overall survival 97.3% versus 98.0%. Results were similar across age and nodal subgroups. Endocrine response occurred in 78.1% on aromatase inhibitors versus 41.1% on tamoxifen, and in 78.8% of recurrence score 0 to 11, 62.2% of 12 to 25 and 32.7% above 25.

wsg-adapt-tp.methods: Phase 2 trial. 375 patients with centrally confirmed HR+/HER2+ early breast cancer, clinical stage I to III, were randomly assigned 1:1:1 to 12 weeks of neoadjuvant T-DM1, T-DM1 plus endocrine therapy, or trastuzumab plus endocrine therapy every 3 weeks. Adjuvant chemotherapy could be omitted after pathologic complete response. Patients receiving at least one dose were analysed. Survival used Kaplan-Meier, log-rank and Cox models stratified for nodal and menopausal status.
wsg-adapt-tp.results: Five-year invasive disease-free survival was 88.9%, 85.3% and 84.6% across the three arms, p=0.608. Five-year overall survival was 97.2%, 96.4% and 96.3%, p=0.534. Patients with pathologic complete response had 5-year invasive disease-free survival of 92.7% versus 82.7% without, hazard ratio 0.40. Of 117 patients with pathologic complete response, 41 omitted adjuvant chemotherapy, with rates of 92.1% versus 93.0%, p=0.848.

wsg-planb.methods: Phase 3 trial in HER2-negative early breast cancer, pT1 to pT4c, all node-positive and high-risk node-negative disease. After an amendment, hormone receptor-positive tumours had recurrence score testing and chemotherapy omission was recommended for recurrence score 11 or lower with pN0 to pN1 disease. Remaining patients were randomly assigned to four cycles of epirubicin and cyclophosphamide followed by four cycles of docetaxel, or six cycles of docetaxel and cyclophosphamide, every 3 weeks.
wsg-planb.results: Of 3198 registered patients, 348 with recurrence score 11 or lower omitted chemotherapy and 2449 formed the randomised intention-to-treat population. After 60 months median follow-up, 5-year disease-free survival was 89.6% versus 89.9% and overall survival was 94.5% versus 94.7%. Among endocrine-treated patients with recurrence score 11 or lower, 5-year disease-free survival was 94% and overall survival was 99%.

wsg-tpii.methods: The trial was a multicenter, randomized, open-label phase II trial. 207 patients with hormone receptor-positive, HER2-positive early breast cancer were randomly assigned 1:1 to 12 weeks of neoadjuvant trastuzumab and pertuzumab with endocrine therapy or with weekly paclitaxel. All patients received dual HER2 blockade in the adjuvant setting. Further standard chemotherapy was obligatory in patients without pathologic complete response and optional after pathologic complete response. This report is the final 5-year survival analysis.
wsg-tpii.results: The pathologic complete response rate was 56.4% with paclitaxel and 23.7% with endocrine therapy. At 5 years, overall survival was 100% with endocrine therapy and 97.9% (95.0 to 100.0) with paclitaxel. Event-free survival-ductal carcinoma in situ at 5 years was 92.1% (86.6 to 97.9) with endocrine therapy and 94.8% (90.5 to 99.3) with paclitaxel. Five-year invasive disease-free survival was 97.7% (94.5 to 100.0) and 79.8% (55.6 to 100.0).

young-pearl-kcsg-br15-10.methods: Multicentre open-label phase 2 trial at 14 institutions in South Korea. Premenopausal women aged 19 years or older with hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer that relapsed or progressed on tamoxifen were randomly assigned 1:1 to palbociclib 125 mg plus exemestane 25 mg with leuprolide, or capecitabine 1250 mg/m2 twice daily. One previous line of chemotherapy for metastatic disease was allowed. Randomisation was stratified by previous chemotherapy and visceral metastasis. Analysis was modified intention to treat.
young-pearl-kcsg-br15-10.results: 184 patients were randomly assigned, 92 to each group, and 178 entered the modified intention-to-treat analysis. At 17 months median follow-up, median progression-free survival was 20.1 months versus 14.4 months, hazard ratio 0.659, one-sided p=0.0235. Grade 3 or worse neutropenia occurred in 75% versus 16%. Treatment-related serious adverse events occurred in 2% versus 17%. No treatment-related deaths occurred.

z0011.methods: Phase 3 randomised noninferiority trial enrolling patients from May 1999 to December 2004 at 115 sites. Eligible women had clinical T1 or T2 invasive breast cancer, no palpable axillary adenopathy, and 1 or 2 sentinel lymph nodes with metastases. All patients had planned lumpectomy, tangential whole-breast irradiation and adjuvant systemic therapy, with third-field radiation prohibited. Patients were randomised to sentinel lymph node dissection alone or axillary lymph node dissection. The primary outcome was overall survival, noninferiority margin 1.3.
z0011.results: 891 women were randomised, 446 to sentinel lymph node dissection alone and 445 to axillary dissection. At a median follow-up of 9.3 years, 10-year overall survival was 86.3% with sentinel dissection alone and 83.6% with axillary dissection (hazard ratio 0.85, noninferiority P = .02). 10-year disease-free survival was 80.2% and 78.2% (hazard ratio 0.85, P = .32). Between years 5 and 10, 1 regional recurrence occurred with sentinel dissection alone and none with axillary dissection.

z1031.methods: Z1031 was a randomized phase II neoadjuvant trial designed to select agents for phase III study. 377 postmenopausal women with clinical stage II to III estrogen receptor-positive breast cancer, Allred score 6 to 8, were randomly assigned to neoadjuvant exemestane, letrozole, or anastrozole. The primary end point was clinical response. Secondary end points were breast-conserving surgery, change in Ki67, the Preoperative Endocrine Prognostic Index, and PAM50-based intrinsic subtype.
z1031.results: Letrozole and anastrozole were selected for further investigation on the basis of clinical response rates. No other differences in surgical outcome, PEPI score, or Ki67 suppression were detected. The breast-conserving surgery rate among patients presenting as mastectomy-only candidates was 51%. PAM50 identified aromatase inhibitor-unresponsive nonluminal subtypes in 3.3%. Clinical response and surgical outcomes were similar in luminal A and luminal B tumors. A PEPI of 0 was more frequent in luminal A tumors (27.1% v 10.7%; P = .004).

z1071.methods: The trial enrolled 756 women at 136 institutions from July 2009 to June 2011 with clinical T0 to T4, N1 to N2, M0 breast cancer treated with neoadjuvant chemotherapy. After chemotherapy each patient underwent both sentinel lymph node surgery and axillary lymph node dissection. Mapping with both blue dye and a radiolabeled colloid was encouraged. The primary end point was the false-negative rate of sentinel node surgery in women presenting with biopsy-proven cN1 disease.
z1071.results: Of 663 evaluable cN1 patients, 649 underwent both sentinel node surgery and axillary dissection. No sentinel node was found in 46 (7.1%) and only one in 78 (12.0%). Of the remaining 525 with two or more sentinel nodes, 215 had no nodal cancer, a 41.0% pathological complete nodal response (36.7% to 45.3%). In 39 patients the dissection found cancer that the sentinel nodes missed, a false-negative rate of 12.6% (90% credible interval, 9.85% to 16.05%).

zephir.methods: Patients with HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer, IHC 3+ or FISH 2.2 or higher, scheduled for trastuzumab emtansine had a pretreatment HER2 PET/CT with 89Zr-trastuzumab, plus FDG-PET/CT at baseline and before cycle 2. HER2-PET/CT was graded into four patterns by the share of FDG-avid tumor load taking up 89Zr above blood pool. Predictive values were assessed against RECIST 1.1 response after three cycles and time to treatment failure.
zephir.results: Fifty-six patients were analyzed. HER2-PET/CT was negative in 29%. Intrapatient heterogeneity was present in 46%. Against RECIST 1.1, negative and positive predictive values were 88% and 72% for HER2-PET/CT and 83% and 96% for early FDG-PET/CT. Combining the two gave predictive values of 100% and separated a group with median time to treatment failure of 2.8 months (n = 12, 95% CI 1.4 to 7.6) from one with 15 months (n = 25, 95% CI 9.7 to not calculable).
